# command.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(composables)/command.mdx

title: Command
description: Fast, composable command menu for keyboard-first navigation and actions
type: composable
builtOn: ["dialog"]

The command menu is a searchable list of actions and links, driven from the
keyboard. Use it for a ⌘K palette, a quick switcher, or any
search-then-select flow.

For a simple dropdown of options bound to a form field, use
[`Select`](/docs/components/select) instead.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="command" example="command-basic-command-menu" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="command" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="command" />

## Composition

```text
Command
└── CommandContent
    ├── CommandInput
    └── CommandList
        └── CommandGroup
            ├── CommandGroupLabel
            ├── CommandSeparator
            └── CommandCollection
                └── CommandItem
                    └── CommandShortcut
```

Wrap the whole menu in `CommandDialog` to open it as a modal, and add
`CommandFooter` below `CommandContent` for navigation hints.

## Examples

### Command Dialog

Wrap the menu in `CommandDialog` to open it as a ⌘K modal.

<ComponentPreview component="command" example="command-command-dialog" />

### With Footer

Use `CommandFooter` to show keyboard navigation hints below the list.

<ComponentPreview component="command" example="command-with-footer" />

### Fuzzy Search

Use `useFuzzyFilter` to match across multiple fields and tolerate typos.

<ComponentPreview component="command" example="command-fuzzy" />

### Virtualized

Use `CommandVirtualizedList` for large lists (100+ items); it only renders the items in view.

<ComponentPreview component="command" example="command-virtualized" />

**Key concepts:**

1. **Use `useListVirtualizer` hook** - Handles scroll positioning, keyboard navigation, and item measurement. See [useListVirtualizer docs](/docs/hooks/use-list-virtualizer) for full API reference.
2. **Use `useCommandFilteredItems()` inside Command** - Call `useCommandFilteredItems()` in a child component of `Command` to get internally filtered items without manual filtering boilerplate.
3. **Replace `CommandList` with `CommandVirtualizedList`** - Accepts `scrollRef` and `totalSize` from the hook.
4. **Pass `virtualized` and `items` on Command** - Enables virtualized mode with your full item list.
5. **Use `useHighlightHandler`** - Pass a `virtualizerRef` to the child and use `useHighlightHandler(virtualizerRef)` on the parent so keyboard navigation scrolls to the highlighted item.

> **Manual filtering still works.** If you need custom filter logic (fuzzy search, server-side filtering), you can still compute `filteredItems` externally, pass `filter={null}` to `Command`, and spread `rootProps` from `useListVirtualizer`. See [useCommandFilter](#usecommandfilter).

## Accessibility

### Keyboard navigation

The menu is operable entirely from the keyboard: type to filter, `↑`/`↓` to move
between items, and `Enter` to select. `autoHighlight="always"` keeps an item
highlighted at all times so `Enter` always has a target.

### Label the input

`CommandInput` is the search field. Give it a `placeholder`, and when the menu
opens outside a labeled `CommandDialog`, add an `aria-label` so its purpose is
announced.

```tsx showLineNumbers
<CommandInput placeholder="Search commands…" aria-label="Search commands" />
```

## API Reference

The Command component is built on top of [Base UI's Autocomplete](https://base-ui.com/react/components/autocomplete) and [Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog). All Base UI props are supported. The documentation below only covers custom props and modified defaults specific to our implementation.

For the complete Base UI API, see the [Base UI Autocomplete documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/autocomplete).

### Props

#### Command

Root component that manages command menu state and keyboard navigation. Wraps Base UI's `Autocomplete.Root`.

<ApiProp
  name="items"
  fullType="T[] | { items: T[] }[]"
  simpleType="array"
  defaultValue="[]"
>
  Array of items or grouped items to display. Used with the collection pattern
  where `CommandList`, `CommandGroup`, and `CommandCollection` receive render
  functions as children.

<ApiProp
  name="autoHighlight"
  fullType='boolean | "always"'
  defaultValue='"always"'
>
  Whether the first matching item is highlighted automatically. Set to
  `"always"` to ensure an item is always highlighted during keyboard navigation.
  Base UI defaults to `false`.

<ApiProp name="open" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="true">
  Keeps the autocomplete list always open. Appropriate for command menu behavior
  where the list is always visible. Base UI defaults to `false`.

<ApiProp name="keepHighlight" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="true">
  Whether the highlighted item should be preserved when the pointer leaves the
  list. Prevents the highlight from going to a "null" state during navigation.
  Base UI defaults to `false`.

<ApiProp name="level" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="3">
  Surface elevation level for the outer Command frame. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs. Bump to `7` when rendered inside `CommandDialog` so the palette pops above the dialog.

<ApiProp name="shadowLevel" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="3">
  Shadow weight for the outer frame. The bg is pinned to `bg-muted` (gray frame); only the shadow + rim track this prop.

#### CommandList

Scrollable container for command items with empty state handling. Wraps Base UI's `Autocomplete.List`.

<ApiProp
  name="emptyMessage"
  fullType="ReactNode"
  simpleType="node"
  defaultValue='"No results found."'
>
  Custom prop not available in Base UI. Message shown when no results are found
  in the command list.

<ApiProp name="nativeScroll" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Use native browser scrolling with styled scrollbars instead of Base UI's
  scroll virtualization. Enables CSS scroll-driven animations for fade edges.

<ApiProp
  name="fadeEdges"
  fullType="boolean | 'top' | 'bottom' | 'left' | 'right' | 'x' | 'y' | FadeEdge[]"
  defaultValue="true"
>
  Controls the fade effect on scroll edges. See
  [ScrollArea](/docs/components/scroll-area#custom-props) for all options.

<ApiProp name="scrollbarGutter" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Reserves space for the scrollbar when content overflows, preventing layout
  shift.

<ApiProp name="persistScrollbar" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Always show the scrollbar instead of fading it in on hover or scroll.

<ApiProp name="hideScrollbar" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Hides the scrollbar while keeping scroll functionality.

#### CommandVirtualizedList

Virtualized scrollable container for large lists. Use with `useListVirtualizer` hook for optimal performance with 100+ items.

<ApiProp
  name="scrollRef"
  fullType="(element: HTMLDivElement | null) => void"
  required
>
  Ref callback from `useListVirtualizer` for the scroll container.

<ApiProp name="totalSize" fullType="number" required>
  Total height of all virtual items in pixels. Provided by `useListVirtualizer`.

<ApiProp
  name="emptyMessage"
  fullType="ReactNode"
  simpleType="node"
  defaultValue='"No results found."'
>
  Message shown when no results are found.

<ApiProp
  name="fadeEdges"
  fullType="boolean | 'x' | 'y' | FadeEdge[]"
  defaultValue='"y"'
>
  Controls the fade effect on scroll edges.

<ApiProp name="nativeScroll" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Use native browser scrolling instead of custom scrollbars.

### Utilities

#### highlightText

Highlights matching portions of text by wrapping them in `<mark>` tags. Useful for showing which parts of a command match the user's input.

See [highlightText](/docs/utils/highlight-text) for full documentation and API reference.

### Hooks

#### useCommandFilter

```ts
function useCommandFilter(): {
  contains: (
    item: T,
    query: string,
    getItemLabel: (item: T) => string,
  ) => boolean;
  startsWith: (
    item: T,
    query: string,
    getItemLabel: (item: T) => string,
  ) => boolean;
  endsWith: (
    item: T,
    query: string,
    getItemLabel: (item: T) => string,
  ) => boolean;
};
```

Exposes Base UI's built-in filter matchers for external filtering. Useful when you need manual control over filtering (e.g., with custom logic or server-side filtering).

**Returns**

| Property     | Type                                     | Description                                                  |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `contains`   | `(item, query, getItemLabel) => boolean` | Returns true if item label contains query (case-insensitive) |
| `startsWith` | `(item, query, getItemLabel) => boolean` | Returns true if item label starts with query                 |
| `endsWith`   | `(item, query, getItemLabel) => boolean` | Returns true if item label ends with query                   |

```tsx
import { useCommandFilter } from "@/registry/default/command/command";

const { contains } = useCommandFilter();
const getItemLabel = (item: Item | null) => item?.name ?? "";

const filteredItems = useMemo(
  () => items.filter((item) => contains(item, query, getItemLabel)),
  [contains, query],
);
```

#### useCommandFilteredItems

```ts
function useCommandFilteredItems<T>(): T[];
```

Returns the internally filtered items from the Command root. Must be called inside `Command`. Simplifies virtualized implementations by eliminating manual query state, `useDeferredValue`, `useFilter()`, and `useMemo` filtering.

```tsx
import { useCommandFilteredItems } from "@/registry/default/command/command";

function VirtualizedListContent() {
  // Must be called inside Command
  const filteredItems = useCommandFilteredItems<MyItem>();

  const virtualizer = useListVirtualizer({
    items: allItems,
    filteredItems,
  });
  // ...
}
```

#### useFuzzyFilter

Provides fuzzy matching capabilities for flexible searching across multiple fields. Returns filter functions compatible with Base UI's Autocomplete.

See [useFuzzyFilter](/docs/hooks/use-fuzzy-filter) for full documentation and API reference.

#### useListVirtualizer

Provides virtualization for large command lists using TanStack Virtual. Abstracts scroll handling, item positioning, and keyboard navigation.

See [useListVirtualizer](/docs/hooks/use-list-virtualizer) for full documentation and API reference.

---

# copy-button.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(composables)/copy-button.mdx

title: Copy Button
description: A button component for copying text to clipboard with visual feedback
type: composable
builtOn: ["button"]

import { CopyButton } from "@/registry/default/copy-button/copy-button";

The copy button copies a string to the clipboard and animates to a checkmark to confirm. Use it beside code snippets, API keys, share links, or any value a user needs to grab.

For a full multi-line code sample with its own copy control, use [`CodeBlock`](/docs/components/code-block) instead.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="copy-button" example="copy-button-demo" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="copy-button" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="copy-button" />

## Examples

### Custom Icons

Pass `copyIcon` and `checkIcon` to replace the default copy and confirmation icons.

<ComponentPreview component="copy-button"
  example="copy-button-custom-icons-demo"
 />

### With Toast

Set `toast` to show an anchored toast above the button on a successful copy. Pass an options object to customize the description, side, duration, or any other anchored toast option.

<ComponentPreview component="copy-button" example="copy-button-with-toast" />

## Accessibility

The button is icon-only, so it ships with a built-in `aria-label` that switches from `"Copy to clipboard"` to `"Copied to clipboard"` when the copy succeeds. Do not pass children; if you need a different label, override `aria-label`.

## API Reference

The CopyButton component extends the [Button component](/docs/components/button) with clipboard functionality. All Button props are supported except `size`, `variant`, `onClick`, and `children` which are controlled internally.

### Props

#### CopyButton

Button that copies text to clipboard with visual feedback. Extends the Button component.

<ApiProp name="content" fullType="string" required>
  The text content to copy to the clipboard when the button is clicked.

<ApiProp name="timeout" fullType="number" defaultValue="2000">
  Duration in milliseconds to show the success state (checkmark icon) after
  copying. Defaults to 2 seconds.

<ApiProp name="copyIcon" fullType="React.ReactNode" simpleType="node">
  Custom icon to display in the default (not copied) state. Defaults to the
  lucide Copy icon.

<ApiProp name="checkIcon" fullType="React.ReactNode" simpleType="node">
  Custom icon to display in the copied/success state. Defaults to the lucide
  Check icon with green color.

<ApiProp name="toast" fullType="true | Omit<AnchoredToastOptions, 'anchor'>" simpleType="boolean | object">
  Show an anchored toast above the button on successful copy. Pass `true` to
  use the defaults (`"Copied to clipboard!"`, `side: "top"`, arrow, duration
  matches `timeout`), or an options object to override any anchored toast
  option except `anchor` (which is always the button itself).

<ApiProp name="onCopied" fullType="(text: string) => void" simpleType="function">
  Fires after a successful copy with the copied text. Runs independently of
  `toast`; use it for analytics or extra side effects.

---

# cropper.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(composables)/cropper.mdx

title: Cropper
description: Image cropping tool with zoom, rotation, and customizable aspect ratios
type: composable

import { Cropper } from "@/registry/default/cropper/cropper";

The cropper lets users pan and zoom an image inside a fixed crop frame, then export the result. Use it for avatar uploads, cover images, and any flow that needs a constrained crop with optional aspect-ratio presets.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="cropper" example="cropper-simple" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="cropper" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="cropper" />

## Composition

`Cropper` holds the image and crop frame. The control components render alongside it and drive state through the `useCropper` hook.

```text
Cropper
├── CropperImage
├── CropperCropArea | CropperCropAreaCircular
└── CropperDescription

CropperControls
├── CropperZoomControls
├── CropperAspectRatioControls
├── CropperInfo
└── CropperActions
```

## Examples

### Aspect Ratios

Pass `aspectRatio` to constrain the crop frame to a fixed ratio.

<ComponentPreview component="cropper" example="cropper-aspect-ratios" />

### With Preview

Read `onCropChange` to render a live preview of the cropped result.

<ComponentPreview component="cropper" example="cropper-with-preview" />

### Download Cropped Image

Use `createCropCanvas` and `downloadCroppedImage` to export the crop as a file.

<ComponentPreview component="cropper" example="cropper-download" />

### Pro Features

Combine aspect-ratio presets, circular crops, and custom dimensions for a full editor.

<ComponentPreview component="cropper" example="cropper-pro" />

## API Reference

The image surface (`Cropper`, `CropperImage`, `CropperCropArea`, `CropperCropAreaCircular`, `CropperDescription`) is built on top of [@origin-space/image-cropper](https://github.com/origin-space/image-cropper). Its props pass through to that library. The control parts (`CropperControls`, `CropperZoomControls`, `CropperAspectRatioControls`, `CropperInfo`, `CropperActions`) are custom, and `useCropper` wires them together.

### Props

#### Cropper

Pan-and-zoom image surface and crop frame. Wraps the cropper library's `Root`.

<ApiProp name="image" fullType="string" required>
  URL or data URL of the image to crop.

<ApiProp name="aspectRatio" fullType="number">
  Locks the crop frame to a fixed width-to-height ratio. Omit for a free-form crop.

<ApiProp name="zoom" fullType="number">
  Controlled zoom level. Pair with `onZoomChange`.

<ApiProp name="minZoom" fullType="number" defaultValue="1">
  Lowest zoom level allowed.

<ApiProp name="maxZoom" fullType="number" defaultValue="3">
  Highest zoom level allowed.

<ApiProp name="cropPadding" fullType="number">
  Space in pixels between the crop frame and the container edge.

<ApiProp name="zoomSensitivity" fullType="number">
  Multiplier applied to wheel and pinch zoom input.

<ApiProp name="keyboardStep" fullType="number">
  Pixels the crop position moves per arrow-key press.

<ApiProp
  name="onCropChange"
  fullType="(pixels: Area | null) => void"
  simpleType="function"
>
  Callback fired with the cropped area in source-image pixels whenever the crop changes.

<ApiProp
  name="onZoomChange"
  fullType="(zoom: number) => void"
  simpleType="function"
>
  Callback fired when the zoom level changes.

#### CropperZoomControls

Zoom out, zoom in, and optional reset buttons. Renders a custom toolbar.

<ApiProp name="zoom" fullType="number" required>
  Current zoom level to display as a percentage.

<ApiProp
  name="onZoomChange"
  fullType="(zoom: number) => void"
  simpleType="function"
  required
>
  Callback fired when a zoom button is pressed, clamped to `minZoom` and `maxZoom`.

<ApiProp name="minZoom" fullType="number" defaultValue="1">
  Lowest zoom the buttons allow.

<ApiProp name="maxZoom" fullType="number" defaultValue="3">
  Highest zoom the buttons allow.

<ApiProp name="step" fullType="number" defaultValue="0.1">
  Amount each button press changes the zoom.

<ApiProp name="onReset" fullType="() => void" simpleType="function">
  Callback for the reset button. The button only renders when this is provided.

#### CropperAspectRatioControls

Row of preset buttons for switching the crop ratio.

<ApiProp name="aspectRatio" fullType="number" required>
  Currently active ratio, used to highlight the matching preset.

<ApiProp
  name="onAspectRatioChange"
  fullType="(ratio: number) => void"
  simpleType="function"
  required
>
  Callback fired with the selected preset's value.

<ApiProp name="presets" fullType="AspectRatioPreset[]" defaultValue="ASPECT_RATIO_PRESETS">
  Presets to render. Each is `{ label: string; value: number; icon?: IconSvgElement }`. Defaults to Free, Square, Portrait, Landscape, and Widescreen.

#### CropperInfo

Read-only summary of zoom, aspect, and crop size.

<ApiProp name="cropData" fullType="CropData" simpleType="object">
  Crop metadata to display, `{ cropArea, zoom, aspectRatio }`. Renders nothing when absent.

<ApiProp name="showDetails" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Also shows the aspect ratio and pixel dimensions in addition to zoom.

#### CropperActions

Optional download and export buttons.

<ApiProp name="onDownload" fullType="() => void" simpleType="function">
  Callback for the download button. The button only renders when provided.

<ApiProp name="onExport" fullType="() => void" simpleType="function">
  Callback for the export button. The button only renders when provided.

<ApiProp name="downloadLabel" fullType="string" defaultValue='"Download"'>
  Label for the download button.

<ApiProp name="exportLabel" fullType="string" defaultValue='"Export"'>
  Label for the export button.

### Hooks

#### useCropper

```ts
function useCropper(options?: UseCropperOptions): {
  zoom: number;
  aspectRatio: number;
  cropData: CropData | undefined;
  setZoom: (zoom: number) => void;
  setAspectRatio: (ratio: number) => void;
  onCropChange: (cropArea: Area | null) => void;
  reset: () => void;
  exportCrop: (
    image: HTMLImageElement,
    filename?: string,
  ) => Promise<{ canvas: HTMLCanvasElement; blob: Blob; dataUrl: string } | null>;
  config: { minZoom: number; maxZoom: number; zoomStep: number };
};
```

Manages zoom, aspect ratio, and crop state for a `Cropper`, and wires up the control parts. Pass `setZoom`/`zoom` to `CropperZoomControls`, `setAspectRatio`/`aspectRatio` to `CropperAspectRatioControls`, and `onCropChange` to `Cropper`.

**Options**

<ApiProp name="initialZoom" fullType="number" defaultValue="1">
  Starting zoom level.

<ApiProp name="initialAspectRatio" fullType="number" defaultValue="1">
  Starting aspect ratio.

<ApiProp name="minZoom" fullType="number" defaultValue="1">
  Lowest zoom `setZoom` clamps to.

<ApiProp name="maxZoom" fullType="number" defaultValue="3">
  Highest zoom `setZoom` clamps to.

<ApiProp name="zoomStep" fullType="number" defaultValue="0.1">
  Step exposed via `config` for zoom controls.

**Returns**

| Property         | Type                                                              | Description                                                       |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `zoom`           | `number`                                                         | Current zoom level.                                               |
| `aspectRatio`    | `number`                                                         | Current aspect ratio.                                             |
| `cropData`       | `CropData \| undefined`                                          | Latest crop metadata from `onCropChange`.                        |
| `setZoom`        | `(zoom: number) => void`                                        | Sets zoom, clamped to `minZoom`/`maxZoom`.                       |
| `setAspectRatio` | `(ratio: number) => void`                                      | Sets the aspect ratio.                                           |
| `onCropChange`   | `(cropArea: Area \| null) => void`                             | Handler to pass to `Cropper`.                                    |
| `reset`          | `() => void`                                                    | Resets zoom and aspect ratio to their initial values.            |
| `exportCrop`     | `(image, filename?) => Promise<{ canvas; blob; dataUrl } \| null>` | Renders the current crop to a canvas, optionally downloading it. |
| `config`         | `{ minZoom; maxZoom; zoomStep }`                               | Resolved zoom bounds and step.                                   |

### Utilities

#### createCropCanvas

```ts
function createCropCanvas(
  image: HTMLImageElement,
  cropArea: Area,
  isCircular?: boolean,
): HTMLCanvasElement;
```

Draws the cropped region of `image` to a canvas. Pass `isCircular` to clip the output to a circle.

#### downloadCroppedImage

```ts
function downloadCroppedImage(canvas: HTMLCanvasElement, filename?: string): void;
```

Triggers a browser download of the canvas as a PNG. `filename` defaults to `"cropped-image.png"`.

#### getCroppedImageBlob

```ts
function getCroppedImageBlob(canvas: HTMLCanvasElement): Promise<Blob>;
```

Resolves the canvas contents as a `Blob`, useful for uploading the crop.

# data-table.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(composables)/data-table.mdx

title: Data Table
description: A powerful data table component built on TanStack Table for sorting, filtering, and row selection.
type: composable
builtOn: ["table"]

import { DataTable } from "@/registry/default/data-table/data-table";

The data table renders rows and columns with sorting, filtering, row selection, and pagination. Use it for dashboards, admin lists, and any tabular data that needs interaction. It is built on TanStack Table, so you define columns with `ColumnDef` and compose the table from parts.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="data-table" example="data-table-basic" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="data-table" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="data-table" />

## Composition

`DataTable` builds the TanStack Table instance from `columns` and `data` and shares it through context. Compose the parts you need inside it.

```text
DataTable                       (columns + data)
├── DataTableToolbar
│   ├── DataTableSearch
│   ├── DataTableColumnToggle
│   └── DataTableToolbarSeparator
├── DataTableContent
│   ├── DataTableHeader
│   ├── DataTableBody
│   └── DataTableFooter
└── DataTablePagination
```

```tsx
<DataTable columns={columns} data={data} enableSorting>
  <DataTableToolbar>
    <DataTableSearch />
    <DataTableColumnToggle />
  </DataTableToolbar>
  <DataTableContent>
    <DataTableHeader enableSorting />
    <DataTableBody emptyState="No results found." />
  </DataTableContent>
</DataTable>
```

## Examples

### Sorting

Set `enableSorting` on `DataTable` and pass it to `DataTableHeader`; columns with string headers get clickable sort controls.

<ComponentPreview component="data-table" example="data-table-sorting" />

### Row Selection

Set `enableRowSelection` to add a checkbox column, and control state with `rowSelection` and `onRowSelectionChange`.

<ComponentPreview component="data-table" example="data-table-row-selection" />

### Toolbar

Compose `DataTableToolbar` with `DataTableSearch` and `DataTableColumnToggle`, and set `enableFiltering` on `DataTable` so search works.

<ComponentPreview component="data-table" example="data-table-toolbar" />

### Striped

Set `striped` on `DataTableContent` for alternating row backgrounds.

<ComponentPreview component="data-table" example="data-table-striped" />

## Column Definitions

Define columns using the `ColumnDef` type from TanStack Table. Each column can have:

- `accessorKey` - The key to access data from the row
- `header` - Header content (string or render function)
- `cell` - Cell content render function
- `enableSorting` - Whether the column is sortable (default: `true` when `enableSorting` prop is set)

When `enableSorting` is enabled, columns with string headers automatically render a sortable button with direction indicators. Use `meta.align` to control header alignment, or a render function for fully custom headers.

```tsx
import { type ColumnDef } from "@/registry/default/data-table/data-table"

const columns: ColumnDef<YourDataType>[] = [
  {
    accessorKey: "name",
    header: "Name", // Auto-renders with sort UI when enableSorting is true
  },
  {
    accessorKey: "amount",
    header: "Amount",
    meta: { align: "right" as const }, // Right-align the header
    cell: ({ row }) => {
      const amount = parseFloat(row.getValue("amount"))
      return <div className="text-right">${amount.toFixed(2)}</div>
    },
  },
  {
    accessorKey: "status",
    header: "Status",
    enableSorting: false, // Disable sorting for this column
  },
]
```

## API Reference

### DataTable

Root component that creates the TanStack Table instance and provides context to children.

<ApiProp
  name="columns"
  fullType="ColumnDef<TData, TValue>[]"
  required
>
  Array of column definitions. See TanStack Table documentation for full options.

<ApiProp
  name="data"
  fullType="TData[]"
  required
>
  Array of data objects to display in the table.

<ApiProp
  name="children"
  fullType="React.ReactNode"
  required
>
  Composition slot for toolbar, content, and other sub-components.

<ApiProp
  name="enableSorting"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Enables column sorting at the table level. Pass `enableSorting` to `DataTableHeader` to render sort UI.

<ApiProp
  name="enableRowSelection"
  fullType="boolean | ((row: Row<TData>) => boolean)"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Enables row selection. Pass a function for conditional selection.

<ApiProp
  name="enableMultiRowSelection"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="true"
>
  Allows multiple rows to be selected. Set to `false` for single selection.

<ApiProp
  name="showSelectionColumn"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="true"
>
  When `enableRowSelection` is true, automatically adds a checkbox column. Set to `false` to handle selection UI yourself.

<ApiProp
  name="enableFiltering"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Enables column filtering.

<ApiProp
  name="enablePagination"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Enables pagination. Use with `DataTablePagination` component.

<ApiProp
  name="sorting"
  fullType="SortingState"
>
  Controlled sorting state. Use with `onSortingChange` for controlled mode.

<ApiProp
  name="onSortingChange"
  fullType="OnChangeFn<SortingState>"
>
  Callback when sorting changes.

<ApiProp
  name="rowSelection"
  fullType="RowSelectionState"
>
  Controlled row selection state. Use with `onRowSelectionChange` for controlled mode.

<ApiProp
  name="onRowSelectionChange"
  fullType="OnChangeFn<RowSelectionState>"
>
  Callback when row selection changes.

<ApiProp
  name="columnFilters"
  fullType="ColumnFiltersState"
>
  Controlled column filters state. Use with `onColumnFiltersChange`.

<ApiProp
  name="onColumnFiltersChange"
  fullType="OnChangeFn<ColumnFiltersState>"
>
  Callback when column filters change.

<ApiProp
  name="pagination"
  fullType="PaginationState"
>
  Controlled pagination state. Use with `onPaginationChange`.

<ApiProp
  name="onPaginationChange"
  fullType="OnChangeFn<PaginationState>"
>
  Callback when pagination changes.

<ApiProp
  name="columnVisibility"
  fullType="VisibilityState"
>
  Controlled column visibility state. Use with `onColumnVisibilityChange` for controlled mode.

<ApiProp
  name="onColumnVisibilityChange"
  fullType="OnChangeFn<VisibilityState>"
>
  Callback when column visibility changes.

<ApiProp
  name="globalFilter"
  fullType="string"
>
  Controlled global filter value. Filters across all columns.

<ApiProp
  name="onGlobalFilterChange"
  fullType="OnChangeFn<string>"
>
  Callback when global filter changes.

<ApiProp
  name="getRowId"
  fullType="(originalRow: TData, index: number) => string"
>
  Function to derive a unique ID for each row. Defaults to using the row index.

DataTable's outer wrapper uses the same `solidSurface(3, 1)` + `bg-muted` pattern as Card inset and Table, a flat outlined gray frame. The inner `DataTableContent` Table inside has its own bg-muted/inner-card visual (body cells `bg-surface-3 dark:bg-surface-1`), with its outer Table styling suppressed (`bg-transparent shadow-none ring-0`) so the elevation lives on the DataTable wrapper only. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs.

### DataTableToolbar

Container for toolbar controls. Renders above the table content with visual connection to the header.

<ApiProp
  name="variant"
  fullType="'default' | 'ghost'"
  defaultValue="'default'"
>
  Visual style of the toolbar.

<ApiProp
  name="children"
  fullType="React.ReactNode"
>
  Toolbar contents such as search, filters, and column toggle.

### DataTableSearch

Search input that filters across all columns using the global filter.

<ApiProp
  name="placeholder"
  fullType="string"
  defaultValue='"Search and filter"'
>
  Placeholder text for the search input.

<ApiProp
  name="size"
  fullType="'default' | 'sm'"
  defaultValue="'sm'"
>
  Size of the search input.

### DataTableColumnToggle

Dropdown button that allows users to show/hide columns.

This component has no configurable props. It automatically reads column visibility state from the DataTable context.

### DataTableContent

Wrapper for the table that applies styling props. Accepts all `Table` component props.

<ApiProp
  name="bordered"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Adds borders to all table cells for a grid appearance.

<ApiProp
  name="striped"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Adds alternating background colors to rows.

<ApiProp
  name="hoverable"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="true"
>
  Enables hover effect on rows.

<ApiProp
  name="rowDividers"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="true"
>
  Shows horizontal dividers between body rows.

### DataTableHeader

Renders the table header with optional sort controls.

<ApiProp
  name="enableSorting"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  When true, columns with string headers render clickable sort buttons with direction indicators.

### DataTableBody

Renders the table body with support for empty state.

<ApiProp
  name="emptyState"
  fullType="React.ReactNode"
  defaultValue='"No results."'
>
  Content to display when the table has no data.

### DataTablePagination

Pagination controls with previous/next buttons and selection count.

<ApiProp
  name="showSelectedCount"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="true"
>
  Shows the count of selected rows (e.g., "2 of 10 row(s) selected").

### DataTableToolbarSeparator

Visual separator for toolbar items. No configurable props.

# date-picker.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(composables)/date-picker.mdx

title: Date Picker
description: Input field with calendar popup for selecting dates
type: composable
builtOn: ["calendar", "popover"]

import { DatePicker } from "@/registry/default/date-picker/date-picker";

The date picker is a trigger button that opens a calendar popover for choosing a single date. Use it for due dates, birthdays, and any form field that needs one date.

To select a start and end date together, use [`DateRangePicker`](/docs/components/date-range-picker) instead.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="date-picker" example="date-picker-basic" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="date-picker" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="date-picker" />

## Examples

### Controlled

Pass `value` and `onSelect` to manage the selected date externally.

<ComponentPreview component="date-picker" example="date-picker-controlled" />

### Custom Placeholder and Format

Use `placeholder` and `format` to set the empty-state text and the displayed date format.

<ComponentPreview component="date-picker" example="date-picker-custom-placeholder-and-format" />

### Different Widths

Set a width utility via `className` to size the trigger.

<ComponentPreview component="date-picker" example="date-picker-different-widths" />

### Disabled State

Set `disabled` to prevent opening the picker.

<ComponentPreview component="date-picker" example="date-picker-disabled-state" />

## Accessibility

The trigger opens a calendar popover that traps focus while open. Inside the calendar, use the arrow keys to move between days, `PageUp` and `PageDown` to change months, `Enter` or `Space` to select, and `Escape` to close.

## API Reference

The DatePicker composes [`Calendar`](/docs/components/calendar) inside a [`Popover`](/docs/components/popover), with a [`Button`](/docs/components/button) trigger. It exposes its own props rather than forwarding to the underlying parts.

### Props

#### DatePicker

Trigger button that opens a single-date calendar popover.

<ApiProp name="value" fullType="Date" simpleType="object">
  The selected date. Pair with `onSelect` for controlled use.

<ApiProp
  name="onSelect"
  fullType="(date: Date | undefined) => void"
  simpleType="function"
>
  Callback fired when a date is picked.

<ApiProp name="placeholder" fullType="string" defaultValue='"Select a date"'>
  Text shown on the trigger when no date is selected.

<ApiProp name="format" fullType="string" defaultValue='"DD MMMM YYYY"'>
  Day.js format string for the displayed date.

<ApiProp name="disabled" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Prevents the popover from opening.

<ApiProp name="className" fullType="string">
  Classes applied to the trigger button. Use a width utility to size it.

## API Reference

The DateRangePicker composes [`Calendar`](/docs/components/calendar) in `range` mode inside a [`Popover`](/docs/components/popover), with a [`Button`](/docs/components/button) trigger. It exposes its own props rather than forwarding to the underlying parts.

Trigger button that opens a range-selection calendar popover with hover preview.

<ApiProp name="value" fullType="DateRange" simpleType="object">

<ApiProp name="disabled" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Prevents the popover from opening.

  Classes applied to the trigger button. Use a width utility to size it.

# drawer.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(composables)/drawer.mdx

title: Drawer
description: Swipeable slide-in panel with snap points for mobile-friendly interactions
type: composable
builtOn: ["dialog"]

import {
  Drawer,
  DrawerBody,
  DrawerClose,
  DrawerContent,
  DrawerDescription,
  DrawerFooter,
  DrawerHandle,
  DrawerHeader,
  DrawerTitle,
  DrawerTrigger,
} from "@/registry/default/drawer/drawer";

The drawer is a swipeable panel that slides in from a screen edge and rests at configurable snap points. Use it for mobile-style bottom sheets, multi-height panels like a music player, or any surface a user drags between heights. For a plain slide-in panel without snap points or drag gestures, use [`Sheet`](/docs/components/sheet) instead.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="drawer" example="drawer-basic" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="drawer" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="drawer" />

## Composition

```text
Drawer
├── DrawerTrigger
└── DrawerContent
    ├── DrawerHandle
    ├── DrawerHeader
    │   ├── DrawerTitle
    │   └── DrawerDescription
    ├── DrawerBody
    └── DrawerFooter
        └── DrawerClose
```

`DrawerContent` composes the portal, backdrop, viewport, and popup. Use `DrawerBody` for scrollable content that cooperates with swipe gestures.

## Examples

### Controlled

Use `open` and `onOpenChange` to drive the drawer's open state externally.

<ComponentPreview component="drawer" example="drawer-controlled" />

### Directions

Use `direction` to choose which edge the drawer slides in from.

<ComponentPreview component="drawer" example="drawer-directions" />

| Value      | Description                          |
| ---------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `"bottom"` | Slides up from the bottom (default). |
| `"top"`    | Slides down from the top.            |
| `"left"`   | Slides in from the left.             |
| `"right"`  | Slides in from the right.            |

### Snap Points

Use `snapPoints` to let the drawer rest at multiple heights.

<ComponentPreview component="drawer" example="drawer-snap-points" />

### Pixel-Based Snap Points

Pass pixel strings in `snapPoints` for fixed heights that ignore content size.

<ComponentPreview component="drawer" example="drawer-pixel-snap-points" />

### Sequential Snap Points

Set `sequentialSnap` to stop at each snap point instead of skipping them on fast swipes.

<ComponentPreview component="drawer" example="drawer-sequential-snap" />

### Floating Variant

Use `variant="floating"` for an inset, modal-like panel with rounded corners and shadow.

<ComponentPreview component="drawer" example="drawer-floating" />

### Music Player

Combine snap points with `--drawer-snap-progress` for progressive disclosure: mini player, expanded controls, and full queue.

<ComponentPreview component="drawer" example="drawer-music-player" />

### Scrollable Content

Use `DrawerBody` for scrollable content that cooperates with swipe gestures.

<ComponentPreview component="drawer" example="drawer-with-scroll" />

### With Form

Place form fields inside `DrawerBody`, with actions in `DrawerFooter`.

<ComponentPreview component="drawer" example="drawer-with-form" />

### Inset Footer

Set `footerVariant="inset"` on `DrawerContent` for a separated footer with a muted background and top border.

<ComponentPreview component="drawer" example="drawer-inset-footer" />

### Sticky Footer

Add `className="sticky bottom-0"` to `DrawerFooter` to pin it as the drawer is dragged down.

<ComponentPreview component="drawer" example="drawer-sticky-footer" />

### Nested

Open a drawer from inside another; the parent scales down and dims behind the nested drawer.

<ComponentPreview component="drawer" example="drawer-nested" />

### Non-Modal

Use `modal` to control focus trapping and page interaction.

<ComponentPreview component="drawer" example="drawer-non-modal" />

| Value          | Description                                                          |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `true`         | Focus trapped, backdrop shown, body scroll locked (default).        |
| `"trap-focus"` | Focus trapped, but the page stays interactive.                      |
| `false`        | No focus trap, no backdrop; the page is fully interactive.          |

## Accessibility

Include a `DrawerTitle` (and ideally a `DrawerDescription`) inside every `DrawerContent` so the dialog is named for assistive technology. When the modal drawer opens, focus moves into it and is trapped until it closes; `modal="trap-focus"` keeps the trap while leaving the page interactive, and `modal={false}` removes the trap entirely. `DrawerHandle` is a real button labeled "Close drawer" by default; set `preventClose` to relabel it "Drawer handle" when it should not dismiss.

## API Reference

The Drawer component is built on top of [Base UI's Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog). All Base UI props are supported. The documentation below only covers custom props specific to our implementation.

For the complete Base UI API, see the [Base UI Dialog documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog).

### Props

#### Drawer

Root component that manages drawer state and provides context to child components. Wraps Base UI's `Dialog.Root`.

<ApiProp
  name="direction"
  fullType='"top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"bottom"'
>
  Which edge of the screen the drawer slides in from.

<ApiProp
  name="variant"
  fullType='"default" | "floating"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"default"'
>
  Visual style of the drawer. Use `"floating"` for a modal-like appearance with
  rounded corners, shadow, and inset from screen edges.

<ApiProp
  name="snapPoints"
  fullType="(number | `${number}px`)[]"
  simpleType="array"
  defaultValue="[1]"
>
  Array of snap points where the drawer can rest. Accepts percentages (0-1) or
  pixel values (`"200px"`). For example, `[0.5, 1]` creates snap points at
  half-open and fully open. Use `["200px", "400px", 1]` for fixed pixel heights.
  Dismissing is handled separately via the `dismissible` prop.

<ApiProp
  name="defaultSnapPoint"
  fullType="number | `${number}px`"
  simpleType="SnapPoint"
  defaultValue="first snap point"
>
  Initial snap point value when the drawer opens (uncontrolled mode). Pass the
  actual value from your `snapPoints` array.

<ApiProp
  name="activeSnapPoint"
  fullType="number | `${number}px` | null"
  simpleType="SnapPoint"
>
  Controlled snap point value. Use with `onActiveSnapPointChange` for controlled
  mode. Pass the actual value from your `snapPoints` array.

<ApiProp
  name="onActiveSnapPointChange"
  fullType="(snapPoint: SnapPoint) => void"
  simpleType="function"
>
  Callback fired when the active snap point changes (via swipe or
  programmatically). Receives the snap point value.

<ApiProp
  name="dismissible"
  fullType="boolean"
  simpleType="boolean"
  defaultValue="true"
>
  Whether the drawer can be dismissed by swiping past the lowest snap point.
  When `true`, swiping down past the lowest snap point will close the drawer.

<ApiProp
  name="sequentialSnap"
  fullType="boolean"
  simpleType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  When enabled, prevents skipping snap points during fast swipes. The drawer
  will stop at each intermediate snap point instead of jumping directly to the
  furthest one.

<ApiProp
  name="repositionInputs"
  fullType="boolean"
  simpleType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  When enabled, automatically repositions bottom drawers when a virtual keyboard
  appears on mobile devices, keeping form inputs visible. Only applies to
  `direction="bottom"`.

<ApiProp
  name="modal"
  fullType='boolean | "trap-focus"'
  simpleType="boolean | string"
  defaultValue="true"
>
  Controls modal behavior. `true`: focus trapped, backdrop shown, body scroll
  locked. `"trap-focus"`: focus trapped but page remains interactive. `false`:
  non-modal, no focus trapping, no backdrop, page fully interactive.

<ApiProp
  name="children"
  fullType="ReactNode | ((props: DrawerRenderProps) => ReactNode)"
  simpleType="ReactNode | function"
>
  Children can be a render function to access animation state: `snapProgress`,
  `dragProgress`, `isDragging`, and `activeSnapPoint`. See "Animating Content"
  section below.

#### DrawerContent

Main drawer container with swipe gesture handling and positioning. Composes `Dialog.Portal`, `Dialog.Backdrop`, `Dialog.Viewport`, and `Dialog.Popup`. Props are forwarded to `Dialog.Popup`.

<ApiProp
  name="footerVariant"
  fullType='"default" | "inset"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"default"'
>
  Footer styling variant. Use `"inset"` for a visually separated footer with a
  muted background and top border.

<ApiProp name="level" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="5">
  Surface elevation level. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs. The default (viewport-flush) variant uses a single-edge rim on the inner-facing side.

<ApiProp name="shadowLevel" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="5">
  Shadow weight.

#### DrawerBody

Scrollable content area with adaptive padding based on surrounding elements. Wraps `ScrollArea`.

<ApiProp name="nativeScroll" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Use native browser scrolling instead of Base UI's ScrollArea. Fade edges still
  work using CSS scroll-driven animations (Chrome 115+, with static fallback).
  Note: `persistScrollbar` is not supported with `nativeScroll`.

<ApiProp
  name="fadeEdges"
  fullType="boolean | 'top' | 'bottom' | 'left' | 'right' | 'x' | 'y' | FadeEdge[]"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Controls the fade effect on scroll edges. See
  [ScrollArea](/docs/components/scroll-area#custom-props) for all options.

<ApiProp name="scrollbarGutter" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Reserves space for the scrollbar when content overflows, preventing layout
  shift.

<ApiProp name="persistScrollbar" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Always show the scrollbar instead of fading it in on hover or scroll.

<ApiProp name="hideScrollbar" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Hides the scrollbar while keeping scroll functionality.

<ApiProp name="scrollLock" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Disables scrolling when the drawer is not at its last snap point. Useful for
  drawers with multiple snap points where content should only be scrollable at
  full height.

#### DrawerHandle

Visual drag indicator that doubles as a close button. Automatically adjusts orientation based on drawer direction.

<ApiProp name="hidden" fullType="boolean">
  When true, the handle is not rendered.

<ApiProp name="preventClose" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  When true, clicking the handle will not close the drawer. The default `aria-label` changes from "Close drawer" to "Drawer handle" accordingly.

<ApiProp name="aria-label" fullType="string" defaultValue='"Close drawer"'>
  Override for internationalization. Passed via props and merged with defaults using `mergeProps`.

### Components

| Component           | Description                                                        |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `Drawer`            | Root component that manages state and provides context             |
| `DrawerTrigger`     | Button that opens the drawer                                       |
| `DrawerPortal`      | Renders drawer content into a portal                               |
| `DrawerContent`     | Main content container with swipe gesture handling                 |
| `DrawerHandle`      | Visual drag indicator (automatically adjusts for direction)        |
| `DrawerHeader`      | Container for title and description with adaptive padding          |
| `DrawerTitle`       | Accessible title element                                           |
| `DrawerDescription` | Accessible description element                                     |
| `DrawerBody`        | Scrollable content area with adaptive padding                      |
| `DrawerFooter`      | Container for action buttons, supports `inset` variant via content |
| `DrawerClose`       | Button that closes the drawer                                      |
| `useDrawer`         | Hook to access drawer context (direction, snap state, etc.)        |

### Nested Scrollable Content

Use `DrawerBody` for scrollable content inside the drawer. The component handles overflow automatically and adapts its padding based on surrounding elements (header, footer).

```tsx
<DrawerContent>
  <DrawerHandle />
  <DrawerHeader>
    <DrawerTitle>Long List</DrawerTitle>
  </DrawerHeader>
  <DrawerBody>{/* Your scrollable content */}</DrawerBody>
  <DrawerFooter>
    <DrawerClose render={<Button />}>Done</DrawerClose>
  </DrawerFooter>
</DrawerContent>
```

### Animating Content Based on Snap Position

The drawer exposes a `--drawer-snap-progress` CSS custom property that animates from 0 (first snap) to 1 (last snap) as the drawer moves between snap points. This works in all browsers:

- **Chrome 115+**: GPU-accelerated CSS scroll-driven animation (no React re-renders)
- **Other browsers**: JavaScript fallback sets the variable automatically

#### Using the CSS Variable

Use `--drawer-snap-progress` directly in your styles for crossfade effects:

```tsx
<Drawer snapPoints={["92px", 1]}>
  <DrawerTrigger>Open</DrawerTrigger>
  <DrawerContent>
    {/* Mini player fades out as drawer expands */}
    <div style={{ opacity: "calc(1 - var(--drawer-snap-progress, 0))" }}>
      Mini Player
    </div>
    {/* Full player fades in as drawer expands */}
    <div style={{ opacity: "var(--drawer-snap-progress, 0)" }}>
      Full Player
    </div>
  </DrawerContent>
</Drawer>
```

Or with Tailwind's arbitrary value syntax:

```tsx
<div className="opacity-(calc(1-var(--drawer-snap-progress,0)))">Mini Player</div>
<div className="opacity-(--drawer-snap-progress,0)">Full Player</div>
```

#### Conditional Logic with Render Props

CSS variables work great for visual properties like `opacity`, but some properties like `pointer-events` need conditional logic. Use the render prop pattern for these:

```tsx
<Drawer snapPoints={["92px", 1]}>
  {({ snapProgress }) => (
    <DrawerContent>
      {/* Opacity via CSS variable, pointer-events via JS */}
      <div
        style={{
          opacity: "calc(1 - var(--drawer-snap-progress, 0))",
          pointerEvents: snapProgress > 0.7 ? "none" : "auto",
        }}
      >
        Mini Player
      </div>
      <div
        style={{
          opacity: "var(--drawer-snap-progress, 0)",
          pointerEvents: snapProgress < 0.3 ? "none" : "auto",
        }}
      >
        Full Player
      </div>
    </DrawerContent>
  )}
</Drawer>
```

#### Render Prop Values

| Value             | Description                                                  |
| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `snapProgress`    | Progress between snap points (0 = first snap, 1 = last snap) |
| `dragProgress`    | Progress toward closed (0 = open, 1 = closed)                |
| `isDragging`      | Whether currently being dragged/scrolled                     |
| `activeSnapPoint` | Current active snap point value                              |

---

# fancy-button.mdx

# filters.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(composables)/filters.mdx

title: Filters
description: A filter bar of segmented pills with per-field operators and value controls
type: composable
builtOn: ["button-group", "combobox", "dropdown-menu", "input"]

import { Filters } from "@/registry/default/filters/filters";
import FiltersBasic from "@/registry/examples/filters/filters-basic";
import FiltersControlled from "@/registry/examples/filters/filters-controlled";
import FiltersFieldTypes from "@/registry/examples/filters/filters-field-types";
import FiltersOperators from "@/registry/examples/filters/filters-operators";
import FiltersMultiselect from "@/registry/examples/filters/filters-multiselect";
import FiltersManual from "@/registry/examples/filters/filters-manual";
import FiltersSizes from "@/registry/examples/filters/filters-sizes";
import FiltersAffixes from "@/registry/examples/filters/filters-affixes";
import FiltersShortcut from "@/registry/examples/filters/filters-shortcut";
import FiltersNuqs from "@/registry/examples/filters/filters-nuqs";

The filter bar shows active filters as segmented pills, each pairing a field, an operator, and a value, plus an "Add filter" button that opens a searchable field picker. Use it for list and table views where users refine results by several conditions at once, the pattern you see in Linear, Notion, and Stripe.

For a single dropdown of options tied to a form field, use [`Combobox`](/docs/components/combobox) instead.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="filters" example="filters-basic">
  <FiltersBasic />
</ComponentPreview>

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="filters" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="filters" />

## Composition

```text
Filters                 (FiltersProvider + FiltersBar)
└── FiltersBar
    ├── FilterChips
    │   └── FilterChip
    │       ├── FilterChipField
    │       ├── FilterChipOperator
    │       ├── FilterChipValue
    │       └── FilterChipRemove
    ├── FilterAddButton
    ├── FilterActiveCount
    └── FilterClearButton
```

Drive the bar with a `fields` config and a `value` array of active filters. Each field's `type` picks the value control and its default operators. Without `children`, the bar renders `FilterChips`, `FilterAddButton`, and a `FilterClearButton` once filters exist; pass `children` to compose the same parts in any order.

```tsx
const fields: FilterField[] = [
  {
    id: "status",
    label: "Status",
    type: "select",
    options: [
      { value: "todo", label: "Todo" },
      { value: "done", label: "Done" },
    ],
  },
  { id: "title", label: "Title", type: "text" },
];

const [value, setValue] = React.useState<FilterValue[]>([]);

return <Filters fields={fields} value={value} onValueChange={setValue} />;
```

## Features

- Per-type operators with sensible defaults (`is`, `contains`, `between`, `is empty`), overridable or hideable per field.
- Operators declare a value `shape` (`"none"` / `"scalar"` / `"range"`), so custom operators get the right control automatically; `is empty` drops the value segment, and any `"range"` operator gets paired min/max inputs.
- Adding a filter opens its value picker (or focuses its input) right away, so you pick in one gesture.
- Colored dots or icons on options keep a dense bar scannable; fields accept an optional `icon` too.
- `prefix` / `suffix` on text and number fields for currency, units, or symbols; `maxSelections` caps a multiselect.
- Number fields are spinner-free (Base UI) with arrow-key stepping and wheel scrubbing (scroll to adjust while focused).
- An optional `shortcut` key opens the add-filter menu, with a `Kbd` hint on the button.
- Controlled and uncontrolled: pass `value` + `onValueChange`, or `defaultValue`. Because it is controlled, syncing to the URL (nuqs) is trivial.
- The `custom` field type renders any control through `renderValue`, for dates, sliders, or bespoke inputs.
- Searchable, keyboard-navigable field and value pickers, inherited from `Combobox`.

## Examples

### Controlled

Pass `value` and `onValueChange` to own the state; the serialized filters update as you edit. This example also composes a `FilterActiveCount` badge into the bar.

<ComponentPreview component="filters" example="filters-controlled">
  <FiltersControlled />
</ComponentPreview>

### Field types

Use `type` to pick the value control. `select` and `multiselect` open a searchable list, `text` and `number` render inline inputs, and `custom` renders your own control through `renderValue`.

| Type            | Value control                              | Value shape                     |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------- |
| `"select"`      | Searchable single-select list.             | `string \| null`                |
| `"multiselect"` | Searchable multi-select list.              | `string[]`                      |
| `"text"`        | Inline text input.                         | `string`                        |
| `"number"`      | Inline number input, paired for `between`. | `number \| null \| NumberRange` |
| `"custom"`      | Your control via `renderValue`.            | `unknown`                       |

<ComponentPreview component="filters" example="filters-field-types">
  <FiltersFieldTypes />
</ComponentPreview>

### Prefix and suffix

Add a `prefix` or `suffix` to text and number fields for currency, units, or symbols. The value input stays inline; the affix sits alongside it.

<ComponentPreview component="filters" example="filters-affixes">
  <FiltersAffixes />
</ComponentPreview>

### Operators

Use `operators` to replace the default set for a field, or `disabledOperators` to remove specific ones. Each operator declares a `shape`: `"none"` hides the value segment (`valueless: true` is sugar for it), `"range"` renders paired min/max inputs on number fields, and `"scalar"` (the default) renders the field's normal control.

<ComponentPreview component="filters" example="filters-operators">
  <FiltersOperators />
</ComponentPreview>

### Multiselect

A `multiselect` field collapses its selection to the first label plus a count. Set `maxSelections` to cap how many options can be picked; the rest disable once the cap is hit.

<ComponentPreview component="filters" example="filters-multiselect">
  <FiltersMultiselect />
</ComponentPreview>

### Manual layout

Pass `children` to lay the bar out yourself with `FilterChips`, `FilterAddButton`, `FilterActiveCount`, and `FilterClearButton`, which read the shared state from context.

<ComponentPreview component="filters" example="filters-manual">
  <FiltersManual />
</ComponentPreview>

### Sizes

Use `size` to set the height of every pill in the bar.

<ComponentPreview component="filters" example="filters-sizes">
  <FiltersSizes />
</ComponentPreview>

### Keyboard shortcut

Set `shortcut` to a key (here `"f"`) to open the add-filter menu from the keyboard; a `Kbd` hint appears on the button. The key is ignored while typing or while a popup is open.

<ComponentPreview component="filters" example="filters-shortcut">
  <FiltersShortcut />
</ComponentPreview>

### URL state with nuqs

Because `Filters` is controlled, syncing to the query string is just wiring `value` / `onValueChange` to a state hook. This uses [`nuqs`](https://nuqs.dev) to persist the filters in `?filters=`. Mount `NuqsAdapter` once at your app root.

<ComponentPreview component="filters" example="filters-nuqs">
  <FiltersNuqs />
</ComponentPreview>

### State outside the bar

`Filters` is `FiltersProvider` + `FiltersBar` composed. Use them separately when UI outside the flex row (a results count, saved views, an apply button) should read or mutate the same state through `useFilters`.

```tsx
<FiltersProvider fields={fields} value={value} onValueChange={setValue}>
  <PageHeader>
    <FilterSummary /> {/* reads useFilters() */}
  </PageHeader>
  <FiltersBar />
  <ResultsCount />
</FiltersProvider>
```

## Accessibility

The field picker and value lists are `Combobox` instances, so type-to-search, arrow-key navigation, and selection follow the ARIA combobox pattern. The operator menu is a `DropdownMenu` radio group. Each pill is a group labeled with its full filter (for example, "Status is In progress"), and every segment is self-describing: the operator trigger is named "[field] operator: [operator]", value triggers and inputs are named "[field] value: ..." (including string affixes), and the remove control is "Remove [field] filter". Pressing `Backspace` or `Delete` on one of a pill's button segments removes the filter, and focus moves to the neighboring pill (or the add button) instead of dropping to the page.

The Backspace removal and focus rescue rely on the `data-slot` attributes (`filter-chip`, `filter-chip-remove`, `filter-add`); custom chip children should preserve those slots to keep the keyboard behavior.

## API Reference

Filters is a custom component composed from Cubby UI primitives. It has no Base UI root of its own; the value and field pickers are [`Combobox`](/docs/components/combobox) and the operator menu is [`DropdownMenu`](/docs/components/dropdown-menu).

### Props

#### Filters

`FiltersProvider` + `FiltersBar` composed, for the common case. All props below except `shortcut` belong to the provider; `shortcut` and div props flow to the bar.

<ApiProp name="fields" fullType="FilterField[]">
  Field definitions the bar can filter on. Each field's `type` determines its
  value control and default operators.

<ApiProp name="value" fullType="FilterValue[]">
  Controlled list of active filters. Pair with `onValueChange`.

<ApiProp name="defaultValue" fullType="FilterValue[]" defaultValue="[]">
  Initial filters in uncontrolled mode. Seed entries with `createFilter` so each
  has a stable id.

<ApiProp name="onValueChange" fullType="(value: FilterValue[]) => void">
  Called whenever a filter is added, edited, or removed.

<ApiProp
  name="size"
  fullType='"sm" | "default" | "lg"'
  defaultValue='"default"'
>
  Height of every pill and the add-filter button.

<ApiProp name="allowDuplicateFields" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Allows the same field to be added more than once. When `false`, used fields
  are disabled in the picker.

<ApiProp name="shortcut" fullType="string">
  Key that opens the add-filter menu, forwarded to the default
  `FilterAddButton`. Ignored while typing or while a popup is open; shows a
  `Kbd` hint on the button.

<ApiProp name="labels" fullType="Partial<FiltersLabels>">
  Overrides for the bar's copy: `add`, `clear`, `searchFields`, `searchValues`,
  `noFields`, `noResults`, `selectValue`, `enterValue`, `value`, `min`, `max`,
  `operator`, and `removeFilter` (a function building the remove button's
  accessible label). Inline objects with string labels are fine (the memo
  compares values, not identity); hoist the object only if you override
  `removeFilter`, since an inline arrow is a new function every render.

#### FiltersProvider

Owns filter state and provides it via context without rendering layout. Takes the state props from `Filters` (`fields`, `value`, `defaultValue`, `onValueChange`, `size`, `allowDuplicateFields`, `labels`) plus `children`.

#### FiltersBar

The flex row. Renders the default layout (`FilterChips`, `FilterAddButton`, `FilterClearButton`) unless `children` is passed. Takes `shortcut` and div props.

#### FilterClearButton

Clears every filter. Renders nothing while no filters are active, so compositions don't need to wrap it in a conditional.

#### FilterChips

Renders a `FilterChip` for every active filter, in order. Use it in `children` mode to place the chip list among your own chrome.

#### FilterChip

A single pill. Without `children` it renders the field, operator, value, and remove segments; pass `children` to compose the segments yourself.

<ApiProp name="filter" fullType="FilterValue">
  The active filter this pill represents.

<ApiProp name="field" fullType="FilterField">
  The field definition. Resolved from the `Filters` context by `filter.field`
  when omitted.

#### FilterAddButton

The searchable field picker. Renders the dashed trigger and the popup.

<ApiProp name="shortcut" fullType="string">
  Key that opens this menu from the keyboard (e.g. `"f"`). Adds a `Kbd` hint to
  the trigger.

### Hooks

`useFilters()` exposes the bar's state and actions (`filters`, `fieldsById`, `addFilter`, `updateFilter`, `removeFilter`, `clearAll`) to anything rendered inside a `FiltersProvider`. It re-renders on every filter edit; performance-sensitive leaves can subscribe to `useFiltersState()` (just `filters`) or `useFiltersActions()` (config and actions, stable while a value is being typed) instead. `useFilterChip()` exposes the current pill's `filter`, `field`, and `size` inside a `FilterChip`.

State merging uses [useControllableState](/docs/hooks/use-controllable-state), installed as a shared hook.

### Types

#### FilterField

A discriminated union keyed on `type`. Every variant has `id`, `label`, and optional `icon`, `operators`, and `disabledOperators`. `select` and `multiselect` add `options` (`multiselect` also takes `maxSelections`); `text` and `number` take `prefix` / `suffix`; `custom` adds `renderValue` and optional `defaultValue`.

#### FilterValue

```ts
interface FilterValue {
  id: string;
  field: string;
  operator: string;
  value: unknown;
}
```

### Helpers

#### createFilter

Creates a `FilterValue` with a stable id, the field's first operator, and a typed empty value. Pass a partial to override any of them.

```ts
createFilter(statusField, { value: "in_progress" });
```

#### patchFilter

Applies a partial update to a filter, reseeding the value when an operator change alters the value shape (e.g. `eq` to `between`).

#### asFilterValues

Coerces unknown JSON (e.g. a parsed URL param) into a `FilterValue[]`, dropping entries with a malformed envelope. Pair it with the controlled API when restoring filters from untrusted sources; see the nuqs example.

#### formatFilterValue / describeFilter

`formatFilterValue` renders a filter's value as a human-readable string; `describeFilter` prepends the field and operator ("Status is In progress"). The pill's `aria-label` uses `describeFilter`, so custom UIs can stay consistent with it.

#### resolveOperators

Returns the operators available for a field, applying `operators` and `disabledOperators`.

---

# input-group.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(composables)/input-group.mdx

title: Input Group
description: Combine input fields with buttons, icons, or text for enhanced functionality
type: composable
builtOn: ["input"]

import { InputGroup } from "@/registry/default/input-group/input-group";
import InputGroupPassword from "@/registry/examples/input-group/input-group-password";
import InputGroupWithSuffix from "@/registry/examples/input-group/input-group-with-suffix";
import InputGroupKeyboardShortcut from "@/registry/examples/input-group/input-group-keyboard-shortcut";
import InputGroupValidation from "@/registry/examples/input-group/input-group-validation";

The input group wraps an input or textarea together with icons, text, or buttons as a single bordered control. Use it for search fields with a leading icon, password fields with a visibility toggle, inputs with unit suffixes, or any field that needs inline addons.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="input-group" example="input-group-demo" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="input-group" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="input-group" />

## Composition

```text
InputGroup
├── InputGroupInput      (or InputGroupTextarea)
└── InputGroupAddon
    ├── InputGroupButton
    └── InputGroupText
```

Place one or more `InputGroupAddon` blocks alongside the input and position each with its `align` prop.

## Examples

### Password Toggle

Use `InputGroupButton` to create a visibility toggle for password fields.

<ComponentPreview component="input-group" example="input-group-password">
  <InputGroupPassword />
</ComponentPreview>

### With Suffix

Add unit labels or currency codes using `align="inline-end"`.

<ComponentPreview component="input-group" example="input-group-with-suffix">
  <InputGroupWithSuffix />
</ComponentPreview>

### Keyboard Shortcut

Display keyboard shortcuts using the `Kbd` component inside an addon.

<ComponentPreview component="input-group" example="input-group-keyboard-shortcut">
  <InputGroupKeyboardShortcut />
</ComponentPreview>

### Validation State

Use `aria-invalid="true"` on the input to show error styling on the group.

<ComponentPreview component="input-group" example="input-group-validation">
  <InputGroupValidation />
</ComponentPreview>

### Elevated Variant

Use `variant="elevated"` on `InputGroup` so the group reads correctly on a Card, Dialog, or popover surface. The inner input is transparent, so the container's variant controls the whole group. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs.

<ComponentPreview component="input-group" example="input-group-elevated" />

| Value      | Description                                                       |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `default`  | Opaque `bg-input` container for standard backgrounds.             |
| `elevated` | Translucent `bg-input-elevated` container for layered surfaces.   |

## API Reference

The Input Group is a custom layout component for combining inputs with addons. All props listed below are custom to this implementation.

### Props

#### InputGroup

Container that combines inputs with addons. Renders a `div` with `role="group"`. Accepts standard `div` props.

<ApiProp
  name="variant"
  fullType='"default" | "elevated"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"default"'
>
  Surface appearance of the group container. `default` uses opaque `bg-input`. `elevated` uses translucent `bg-input-elevated` for use inside Card, Dialog, or popover surfaces. The inner Input/Textarea inherits visually (it's transparent inside the group). See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs.

#### InputGroupAddon

Container for icons, text, or buttons positioned relative to the input.

<ApiProp
  name="align"
  fullType='"inline-start" | "inline-end" | "block-start" | "block-end"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"inline-start"'
>
  Position of the addon relative to the input. Use `inline-start` for left side, `inline-end` for right side, `block-start` for above, and `block-end` for below.

#### InputGroupButton

Styled button for use inside addons. Wraps the [Button](/docs/components/button) component with size variants optimized for input groups. Accepts all Button props except `size`.

<ApiProp
  name="variant"
  fullType='"primary" | "neutral" | "secondary" | "outline" | "ghost" | "link" | "destructive"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"ghost"'
>
  Visual style variant of the button. Inherits from the Button component.

<ApiProp
  name="size"
  fullType='"xs" | "sm" | "icon_xs" | "icon_sm"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"xs"'
>
  Size of the button. Use `icon_xs` or `icon_sm` for icon-only buttons.

#### InputGroupText

Styled text container for labels or static content inside addons. Renders a `span`. Accepts standard `span` props.

#### InputGroupInput

Styled input for use inside the group. Wraps the [Input](/docs/components/input) component with transparent styling. Accepts all Input props.

#### InputGroupTextarea

Styled textarea for multi-line inputs. Wraps the [Textarea](/docs/components/textarea) component with transparent styling. Accepts all Textarea props.

# marching-border.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(composables)/marching-border.mdx

title: Marching Border
description: Animated dashed border overlay that conforms to its parent's corner radius
type: composable

import { MarchingBorder } from "@/registry/default/marching-border/marching-border";

`MarchingBorder` is an animated dashed border overlay that conforms to its parent's corner radius. Use it to signal edit states, pending changes, or drag-over targets without shifting layout, since it sits outside the parent's box model.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="marching-border" example="marching-border-basic" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="marching-border" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="marching-border" />

`MarchingBorder` is an absolutely-positioned SVG overlay. Put it inside a positioned parent (anything with `position: relative`, or another positioned ancestor) and it picks up that element's `border-radius` automatically, so the dashes follow rounded corners. It sits outside the parent's box model, so showing or hiding it never shifts layout. Handy for edit states, pending changes, and drag-over indicators.

The stroke uses `currentColor`, so set the color the same way you'd set text color: a `text-*` class, a `color` style, or inheriting from an ancestor.

## Examples

### Variants

Adjust `dash`, `gap`, `strokeWidth`, and `duration` to tune the pattern; `dash` and `gap` are percentages of the perimeter, so it tiles evenly at any size.

<ComponentPreview component="marching-border" example="marching-border-variants" />

### Overriding the radius

Set a `border-radius` on the overlay itself when it should differ from the parent, or when the parent has none (a `canvas`, a square panel); by default it inherits the parent's corners.

<ComponentPreview component="marching-border" example="marching-border-explicit-radius" />

## API Reference

`MarchingBorder` is a single SVG component. It accepts any native `<svg>` prop in addition to those documented below; spread props land on the root `<svg>` element.

### Props

<ApiProp
  name="strokeWidth"
  fullType="number"
  defaultValue="2"
>
  Stroke thickness in pixels. The stroke is inset by half its width so it sits inside the SVG's bounding box without being clipped.

<ApiProp
  name="dash"
  fullType="number"
  defaultValue="1"
>
  Dash length as a percentage of the path's perimeter. Combined with `gap`, this defines the dash pattern that tiles around the border.

<ApiProp
  name="gap"
  fullType="number"
  defaultValue="0.75"
>
  Gap length as a percentage of the path's perimeter.

<ApiProp
  name="duration"
  fullType="number"
  defaultValue="0.75"
>
  Seconds per dash cycle (one dash plus one gap). Lower values march faster, higher values march slower.

### Notes

- **Parent positioning.** The SVG is `absolute inset-0`, so the parent needs to be positioned (`relative`, `absolute`, `fixed`, or `sticky`). Otherwise the border attaches to the nearest positioned ancestor.
- **Seam-free loop.** `pathLength` is rounded to a whole multiple of `dash + gap`, so the pattern tiles an exact number of times at any size. The path starts at the middle of the top edge, so any subpixel seam lands on a straight side instead of a corner.
- **Shared keyframe.** One `@keyframes dash-march` rule is shared across every instance. The end offset comes from a per-instance CSS variable, so changing `dash` or `gap` doesn't generate new keyframes.
- **Reduced motion.** Under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` the animation stops but the dashes still render, since the static border is the actual signal and shouldn't vanish.
- **Color.** The stroke is `currentColor`. Set the color like text color, for example a `text-*` class such as `text-primary` or `text-destructive` on the component.

---

<ApiProp name="isDisabled" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
