# qr-code.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(composables)/qr-code.mdx

title: QR Code
description: From-scratch, zero-dependency QR generator rendered as pure scalable SVG
type: composable

import { QRCode } from "@/registry/default/qr-code/qr-code";

The QR code encodes a URL or string into a scannable symbol rendered as pure SVG. Use it for links, Wi-Fi credentials, payment codes, or any value a phone camera should read, with optional styled modules, custom finder eyes, and a center logo. It ships its own encoder, so it has no runtime dependencies.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="qr-code" example="qr-code-branded" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="qr-code" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="qr-code" />

## Examples

### Dot styles

Use `dotStyle` to control how the data modules are drawn.

<ComponentPreview component="qr-code" example="qr-code-dot-styles" />

| Value       | Description                                                            |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `"square"`  | Solid square modules (default).                                       |
| `"circle"`  | Each module as an isolated dot.                                       |
| `"rounded"` | Neighbor-aware: adjacent runs merge into "snake" shapes, isolated modules become dots. |

### Custom finders

Use `finder` to style the three corner "eyes" independently from the data modules.

<ComponentPreview component="qr-code" example="qr-code-custom-finders" />

Pass a single object to style all three, or a `[topLeft, topRight, bottomLeft]` tuple to style each. The outer ring and inner eye each take their own `style` and `color`.

### With a logo

Use `logo` to embed an image or React element in the center; the modules behind it are cleared and a quiet area is knocked out to keep the symbol scannable.

<ComponentPreview component="qr-code" example="qr-code-with-logo" />

When a logo is present, the error correction level is automatically raised to `"H"` (about 30% recovery) unless you explicitly request `"Q"` or `"H"`.

### Export & download

Use the imperative `ref` handle to export the code with `toSVGString()`, `toDataURL()`, or `getMatrix()`.

<ComponentPreview component="qr-code" example="qr-code-download" />

`toDataURL()` rasterizes PNG or JPEG through an offscreen canvas at export time (the display itself stays pure SVG), or returns a vector SVG data URL with `type: "svg"`.

## Accessibility

The symbol is decorative SVG with no inherent label. Give it an accessible name with `aria-label` (or `role="img"` plus `aria-label`) describing where the code leads, and provide the same destination as visible text or a fallback link so it is reachable without a camera.

## API Reference

`QRCode` is an original composable with no underlying Base UI primitive. The QR encoder is implemented from scratch per ISO/IEC 18004, supporting Numeric, Alphanumeric, and Byte (UTF-8) modes across versions 1–40 and all four error correction levels, with automatic mode, version, and mask selection. The symbol is rendered entirely as SVG `<path>` elements, so it scales crisply at any size.

### Props

#### QRCode

Renders an `<svg>` element and accepts any native SVG prop (`className`, `style`, `aria-*`, `data-*`, etc.) in addition to those below. The `ref` exposes a [`QRCodeHandle`](#qrcodehandle) rather than the DOM node.

<ApiProp name="value" fullType="string" required>
  The data to encode: a URL, text, or any string.

<ApiProp
  name="dotStyle"
  fullType='"square" | "circle" | "rounded"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"square"'
>
  Visual style of the data modules. `"rounded"` is the neighbor-connected "snake" style.

<ApiProp
  name="ecLevel"
  fullType='"L" | "M" | "Q" | "H"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"M"'
>
  Error correction level (≈7% / 15% / 25% / 30% recovery). Automatically raised to `"H"` when a `logo` is set and a higher level was not requested. The encoder also boosts the level for free when the chosen version has spare capacity.

<ApiProp name="foreground" fullType="string" defaultValue='"currentColor"'>
  Color of the dark modules. Defaults to `currentColor`, so it inherits the surrounding text color.

<ApiProp name="background" fullType="string" defaultValue='"transparent"'>
  Background color. Omitted from the SVG entirely when transparent.

<ApiProp
  name="finder"
  fullType="QRFinderStyle | [QRFinderStyle, QRFinderStyle, QRFinderStyle]"
  simpleType="object"
>
  Independent styling for the finder patterns. A single object styles all three; a tuple styles `[topLeft, topRight, bottomLeft]`. Each accepts `outerStyle`, `outerColor`, `innerStyle`, and `innerColor`.

<ApiProp
  name="logo"
  fullType="{ src: string; width?: number; height?: number; alt?: string } | React.ReactNode"
  simpleType="node"
>
  A center logo. An object with `src` renders an `<image>` (serialized by `toSVGString()`); any other React node renders in a `<foreignObject>`.

<ApiProp name="logoSize" fullType="number" defaultValue="0.22">
  Fraction of the symbol width occupied by the logo, clamped to a maximum of `0.3`.

<ApiProp name="logoPadding" fullType="number" defaultValue="1">
  Quiet area, in modules, knocked out around the logo.

<ApiProp name="margin" fullType="number" defaultValue="4">
  Quiet-zone width around the symbol, in modules.

<ApiProp name="minVersion" fullType="number">
  Minimum QR version (1–40). The encoder still grows beyond this if the data requires it.

<ApiProp name="size" fullType="number | string">
  Rendered pixel size, applied as the SVG `width`/`height`. The `viewBox` stays in module units, so the code scales independently.

<ApiProp name="ref" fullType="React.Ref<QRCodeHandle>">
  Receives the imperative [`QRCodeHandle`](#qrcodehandle).

#### QRCodeHandle

The object exposed through `ref`.

<ApiProp name="toSVGString" fullType="() => string">
  Returns the rendered SVG markup as a string. Identical to the on-screen output (React-element logos are not serialized).

<ApiProp
  name="toDataURL"
  fullType='(options?: { type?: "png" | "jpeg" | "svg"; quality?: number; pixelSize?: number }) => Promise<string>'
  simpleType="function"
>
  Resolves to a data URL. PNG/JPEG rasterize via an offscreen canvas (`pixelSize` defaults to `1024`); `"svg"` returns a vector data URL with no canvas.

<ApiProp name="getMatrix" fullType="() => QRMatrix">
  Returns the underlying encoded matrix (`{ size, modules, version, ecLevel, mode, maskPattern }`).

### Utilities

These named exports are framework-agnostic and tree-shakeable.

<ApiProp name="encode" fullType="(data: string, options?: EncodeOptions) => QRMatrix">
  The standalone encoder. Returns the raw module matrix for custom rendering.

<ApiProp
  name="toSVGString"
  fullType="(options: QRExportOptions) => string"
  simpleType="function"
>
  Pure, SSR-safe SVG string builder. Usable in route handlers, server components, and Node scripts.

<ApiProp
  name="toDataURL"
  fullType="(options: QRDataURLOptions & { value: string }) => Promise<string>"
  simpleType="function"
>
  Standalone data URL generator. PNG/JPEG output requires a browser environment.

### Notes

- **Pure SVG.** The display is rendered entirely as SVG paths (no canvas, no raster images), so it stays sharp at any resolution. A canvas is used only momentarily inside `toDataURL()` to produce PNG/JPEG bytes.
- **Logos and scannability.** Keep `logoSize` modest (≤ `0.3`) and prefer a light `background` behind the logo. The automatic `"H"` error correction compensates for the cleared center, but very large logos can still defeat a scanner.
- **`toSVGString()` and React-element logos.** Image (`src`) logos are serialized into the string output; arbitrary React-element logos are not (only the knockout area is). Use an image logo when you need identical string/DOM output.
- **Cross-origin logos and PNG/JPEG export.** Rasterizing a code whose logo points to another origin would taint the canvas. `toDataURL()` automatically fetches and inlines a cross-origin logo before rasterizing (this works only if the image host sends CORS headers); if it can't, it throws a clear error. Prefer same-origin or data-URI logos, or export with `type: "svg"`. For raster export, set explicit `foreground`/`background` colors, since `currentColor` resolves to black during rasterization.
- **Styling hook.** The root carries `data-slot="qr-code"`; `foreground` defaults to `currentColor` so the code themes with surrounding text.

---

# resizable.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(composables)/resizable.mdx

title: Resizable
description: Adjustable panels with draggable handles for flexible layouts
type: composable

import { ResizablePanelGroup, ResizableHandle, ResizablePanel } from "@/registry/default/resizable/resizable";

Resizable splits a layout into panels separated by draggable handles, so users can size regions to taste. Use it for split editors, sidebars beside content, or any pane layout the user should control. It is built on react-resizable-panels.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="resizable" example="resizable-basic" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="resizable" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="resizable" />

## Composition

```text
ResizablePanelGroup
├── ResizablePanel
├── ResizableHandle
└── ResizablePanel
```

Set `direction` on `ResizablePanelGroup` to lay panels out horizontally or vertically, and place a `ResizableHandle` between each pair.

| Value          | Description                              |
| -------------- | ---------------------------------------- |

| `vertical`     | Panels stack, drag up/down.              |

## Examples

### Vertical Layout

Set `direction="vertical"` on `ResizablePanelGroup` to stack panels.

<ComponentPreview component="resizable" example="resizable-vertical" />

### Three Panels

Add more `ResizablePanel` and `ResizableHandle` pairs for additional sections.

<ComponentPreview component="resizable" example="resizable-three-panels" />

### Min and Max Size

Use `minSize` and `maxSize` on `ResizablePanel` to clamp how far it can resize.

<ComponentPreview component="resizable" example="resizable-min-max-size" />

### Custom Handle

Pass `withHandle` to `ResizableHandle` to render a visible drag grip.

<ComponentPreview component="resizable" example="resizable-with-handle" />

### Nested Panels

Nest a `ResizablePanelGroup` inside a `ResizablePanel` for grid-like layouts.

<ComponentPreview component="resizable" example="resizable-nested" />

## Accessibility

`ResizableHandle` is keyboard operable: focus it and use the arrow keys to resize, with a focus ring on `:focus-visible`. The underlying separators expose the appropriate `role` and value attributes from react-resizable-panels.

## API Reference

Resizable is built on top of [react-resizable-panels](https://github.com/bvaughn/react-resizable-panels). All props pass through to the underlying `PanelGroup`, `Panel`, and `PanelResizeHandle`. The documentation below covers the key props and the custom prop on `ResizableHandle`.

For the complete API, see the [react-resizable-panels documentation](https://github.com/bvaughn/react-resizable-panels#api).

### Props

#### ResizablePanelGroup

Container that lays out panels and tracks their sizes. Wraps `PanelGroup`.

<ApiProp
  name="direction"
  fullType='"horizontal" | "vertical"'
  simpleType="string"
  required
>
  Axis the panels resize along. `"horizontal"` drags left and right, `"vertical"` drags up and down.

<ApiProp name="autoSaveId" fullType="string | null">
  Persists panel sizes to storage under this id so the layout is restored on reload.

#### ResizablePanel

A single resizable region. Wraps `Panel`.

<ApiProp name="defaultSize" fullType="number">
  Initial size as a percentage of the group (`0` to `100`).

<ApiProp name="minSize" fullType="number">
  Smallest size the panel can shrink to, as a percentage.

<ApiProp name="maxSize" fullType="number">
  Largest size the panel can grow to, as a percentage.

<ApiProp name="collapsible" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Allows the panel to collapse below `minSize` to `collapsedSize`.

<ApiProp name="collapsedSize" fullType="number" defaultValue="0">
  Size the panel snaps to when collapsed. Requires `collapsible`.

#### ResizableHandle

Draggable divider between two panels. Wraps `PanelResizeHandle`.

<ApiProp name="withHandle" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Renders a visible grip in the center of the handle. Custom prop not available in react-resizable-panels.

# sheet.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(composables)/sheet.mdx

title: Sheet
description: Sliding panel from screen edge for navigation, forms, or content
type: composable
builtOn: ["dialog"]

import { Sheet, SheetContent, SheetDescription, SheetHeader, SheetTitle, SheetTrigger } from "@/registry/default/sheet/sheet";

The sheet is a panel that slides in from a screen edge for navigation, forms, or supplementary content. Use it for a mobile nav menu, a side filter panel, a detail pane, or an action sheet. For a panel the user drags between snap-point heights, use [`Drawer`](/docs/components/drawer) instead.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="sheet" example="sheet-basic" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="sheet" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="sheet" />

## Composition

```text
Sheet
├── SheetTrigger
└── SheetContent
    ├── SheetHeader
    │   ├── SheetTitle
    │   └── SheetDescription
    ├── SheetBody
    └── SheetFooter
        └── SheetClose
```

`SheetContent` composes the portal, viewport, and popup, and renders a backdrop when the sheet is modal. Use `SheetBody` for scrollable content.

## Examples

### Positions

Use `side` on `SheetContent` to choose which edge the sheet slides in from.

<ComponentPreview component="sheet" example="sheet-positions" />

| Value      | Description                       |
| ---------- | --------------------------------- |
| `"right"`  | Slides in from the right (default). |
| `"left"`   | Slides in from the left.          |
| `"top"`    | Slides down from the top.         |
| `"bottom"` | Slides up from the bottom.        |

### Floating Variant

Use `variant="floating"` for a card-like sheet with rounded corners and margins from the screen edges.

<ComponentPreview component="sheet" example="sheet-variants" />

### With Form

Place form fields inside `SheetBody`, with actions in `SheetFooter`.

<ComponentPreview component="sheet" example="sheet-with-form" />

### Nested Sheets

Open a sheet from inside another; the parent scales down and shifts toward its edge behind the nested sheet.

<ComponentPreview component="sheet" example="sheet-nested" />

### Inset Footer

Use `footerVariant="inset"` to give the footer a muted background with a top border.

<ComponentPreview component="sheet" example="sheet-inset-footer" />

### Detached Trigger

Use `createSheetHandle()` to place the trigger outside the `Sheet`.

<ComponentPreview component="sheet" example="sheet-detached-trigger" />

### Non-Modal

Pass `modal={false}` to keep the page interactive: the backdrop is hidden, pointer events pass through the empty area, and outside clicks don't dismiss the sheet.

<ComponentPreview component="sheet" example="sheet-non-modal" />

## Accessibility

Include a `SheetTitle` inside every `SheetContent` so the dialog is named for assistive technology; add a `SheetDescription` when extra context helps. When a modal sheet opens, focus moves into it and is trapped until it closes, and the built-in close button is labeled for screen readers. With `modal={false}`, the page stays interactive and focus is not trapped, so make sure the sheet can still be closed from the keyboard.

## API Reference

The Sheet component is built on top of [Base UI's Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog). All Base UI props are supported. The documentation below only covers custom props specific to our implementation.

For the complete Base UI API, see the [Base UI Dialog documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog).

### Utilities

#### createSheetHandle

Creates a handle that connects a sheet to one or more external `SheetTrigger` components. Useful when the triggers need to live outside the `Sheet`, for example when each row in a list has its own trigger but they all share one sheet.

```tsx
import { createSheetHandle } from "@/registry/default/sheet/sheet";

const handle = createSheetHandle();
```

##### Passing data from the trigger to the sheet

The handle accepts an optional `<Payload>` generic that types a value each trigger can pass along. The sheet reads it through a render-prop child, so you can render different content per trigger without duplicating the sheet markup.

```tsx
type Skill = { id: string; name: string };

const handle = createSheetHandle<Skill>();

// Multiple triggers, each with its own payload:
skills.map((skill) => (
  <SheetTrigger key={skill.id} handle={handle} payload={skill}>
    View {skill.name}
  </SheetTrigger>
));

// One shared sheet that renders based on the active trigger:
<Sheet handle={handle}>
  <SheetContent>
    {({ payload: skill }) => (
      <SheetHeader>
        <SheetTitle>{skill?.name}</SheetTitle>
      </SheetHeader>
    )}
  </SheetContent>
</Sheet>;
```

Without the `<Skill>` generic, `payload` inside the render prop resolves to `unknown`.

### Props

#### Sheet

Root component. Forwards all props to Base UI's `Dialog.Root`, with modified defaults for the `modal` prop.

<ApiProp
  name="modal"
  fullType='boolean | "trap-focus"'
  simpleType="boolean"
  defaultValue="true"
>
  Behavior is unchanged from Base UI, but when set to `false` or
  `"trap-focus"`, `SheetContent` skips the backdrop and wires
  `pointer-events` so the page remains interactive. Also changes the default
  of `disablePointerDismissal` to `true` so clicks on the page don't close
  the sheet. Pass `disablePointerDismissal={false}` explicitly to opt back
  into outside-click dismissal.

#### SheetContent

Sliding panel container with positioning. Composes `Dialog.Portal`, `Dialog.Viewport`, and `Dialog.Popup`. Also renders `Dialog.Backdrop` when the sheet is modal. Props are forwarded to `Dialog.Popup`.

<ApiProp name="side" fullType='"top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left"' simpleType="string" defaultValue='"right"'>
  Which side of the screen the sheet slides in from. Custom prop not available in Base UI.

<ApiProp name="variant" fullType='"default" | "floating"' simpleType="string" defaultValue='"default"'>
  Visual style variant. `"floating"` adds margins from screen edges and rounded corners for a card-like appearance.

<ApiProp name="footerVariant" fullType='"default" | "inset"' simpleType="string" defaultValue='"default"'>
  Footer style variant. `"inset"` gives the footer a muted background with a top border for visual separation.

<ApiProp name="showCloseButton" fullType="boolean" simpleType="boolean" defaultValue="true">
  Whether to show the close button in the top-right corner.

<ApiProp name="level" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="5">
  Surface elevation level. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs. The `default` (viewport-flush) variant uses a single-edge rim on the inner-facing side; the `popup` variant uses the full four-edge rim.

<ApiProp name="shadowLevel" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="5">
  Shadow weight.

#### SheetBody

Scrollable content area within the sheet.

<ApiProp
  name="nativeScroll"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Use native browser scrolling instead of Base UI's ScrollArea. Fade edges still
  work using CSS scroll-driven animations (Chrome 115+, with static fallback).
  Note: `persistScrollbar` is not supported with `nativeScroll`.

<ApiProp
  name="fadeEdges"
  fullType="boolean | 'top' | 'bottom' | 'left' | 'right' | 'x' | 'y' | FadeEdge[]"
  defaultValue="true"
>
  Controls the fade effect on scroll edges. See [ScrollArea](/docs/components/scroll-area#custom-props) for all options.

<ApiProp
  name="scrollbarGutter"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Reserves space for the scrollbar when content overflows, preventing layout shift.

<ApiProp
  name="persistScrollbar"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Always show the scrollbar instead of fading it in on hover or scroll.

<ApiProp
  name="hideScrollbar"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Hides the scrollbar while keeping scroll functionality.

# transition-panel.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(composables)/transition-panel.mdx

title: Transition Panel
description: Direction-aware animated swap between named views with auto-animated height
type: composable

import { TransitionPanel, TransitionPanelView } from "@/registry/default/transition-panel/transition-panel";

The transition panel animates the swap between named views and grows or shrinks its height to fit the active one. Use it for multi-step wizards, settings panels, and popover or dialog content that changes in place, where you want a direction-aware slide or an in-place crossfade between states.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="transition-panel" example="transition-panel-basic" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="transition-panel" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="transition-panel" />

## Composition

```text
TransitionPanel
└── TransitionPanelView
```

Match each `TransitionPanelView`'s `viewKey` to the panel's `activeKey` to control which view is visible. Set `transition` on `TransitionPanel` to choose how views swap.

| Value   | Description                                                       |
| ------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `slide` | Direction-aware horizontal slide (forward right, back left). Default. |
| `fade`  | Non-directional crossfade with a subtle `0.96` to `1` scale.     |

## Examples

### Crossfade

Set `transition="fade"` to swap views with a non-directional crossfade instead of a slide, for in-place swaps like dialogs, popovers, or settings panels.

<ComponentPreview component="transition-panel" example="transition-panel-crossfade" />

### Multi-step dialog

Give each step its own `TransitionPanelView` so the surface crossfades and the [Dialog](/docs/components/dialog) resizes to fit the active step, with focus moving to the active view's first tabbable element on each swap.

<ComponentPreview component="transition-panel" example="transition-panel-dialog" />

## API Reference

`TransitionPanel` is a pure-CSS compound component with no underlying Base UI primitive. Views register through context, so `TransitionPanelView` doesn't need to be a direct child. Wrappers, fragments, conditional rendering, and Suspense boundaries all work.

The entrance animation uses `@starting-style`. Browsers that lack it fall back to an instant swap with no slide, which is harmless: no broken state, just no motion. The exit defers `display:none` with `transition-behavior: allow-discrete` where it's honored (Chrome, Safari) and uses a JS-deferred hide in Firefox (which doesn't honor `allow-discrete` on exit), so the exit animation runs in every modern engine. The component also respects `prefers-reduced-motion`.

### Props

#### TransitionPanel

Outer container. Renders a `<div>` and accepts any native div prop (`id`, `role`, `aria-label`, `ref`, `data-*`, `style`, etc.). Composes a consumer `ref` with the internal ref used for height measurement.

<ApiProp
  name="activeKey"
  fullType="string"
  required
>
  The `viewKey` of the currently visible view. Must match the `viewKey` of one of the `TransitionPanelView` descendants. Changing this value triggers the slide and height animation.

<ApiProp
  name="transition"
  fullType='"slide" | "fade"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"slide"'
>
  Transition style. `"slide"` slides views horizontally and is direction-aware (forward enters from the right, back from the left). `"fade"` crossfades with a subtle `0.96 → 1` scale, is non-directional, and uses `--tp-fade-duration` for the opacity / scale (size-adaptive by default, so the fade speed tracks the height change).

<ApiProp
  name="render"
  fullType="ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)"
  simpleType="element"
>
  Replace the root element or merge it with another component (Base UI's render-prop polymorphism). The internal height-measurement ref and the consumer `ref` are composed onto whatever element you render.

##### Data attributes

Set on the root element so consumers can style based on transition state.

<ApiProp
  name="data-slot"
  fullType='"transition-panel"'
>
  Styling hook for the root element.

<ApiProp
  name="data-transition"
  fullType='"slide" | "fade"'
>
  Mirrors the `transition` prop.

<ApiProp
  name="data-activation-direction"
  fullType='"left" | "right" | "none"'
>
  Direction of the most recent swap. `"none"` before any activation has happened (first render). Matches Base UI's `Tabs.Panel` vocabulary. In `fade` mode the built-in animation is non-directional, but this still reports the logical forward (`"right"`) / back (`"left"`) direction for consumers who want to drive their own directional styling.

##### CSS custom properties

Set on the root and inherited by view wrappers. Override via the `style` prop or a CSS rule.

<ApiProp
  name="--tp-duration"
  fullType="time"
  defaultValue="240ms"
>
  Duration of the height transition, plus the slide / opacity transition on views in `slide` mode.

<ApiProp
  name="--tp-fade-duration"
  fullType="time"
  defaultValue="adaptive (~0.15s–0.27s)"
>
  Duration of the opacity / scale transition on views in `fade` mode. Defaults to a size-adaptive value (the height observer adapts it to the size change between views, clamped to roughly `0.15s`–`0.27s`, so larger height changes fade a little slower). Set it to a fixed time to opt out of the adaptive behavior. Not used in `slide` mode.

<ApiProp
  name="--tp-ease"
  fullType="easing-function"
  defaultValue="cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1)"
>
  Easing for the height transition and, in `slide` mode, the slide / opacity transition.

<ApiProp
  name="--tp-fade-ease"
  fullType="easing-function"
  defaultValue="cubic-bezier(0.26, 0.08, 0.25, 1)"
>
  Easing for the crossfade in `fade` mode.

<ApiProp
  name="--tp-clip-margin"
  fullType="length"
  defaultValue="0px"
>
  Bleed area for the panel's overflow clip. Defaults to `0` because the recommended composition (frame on the panel, padding inside each view) keeps focus rings and shadows well inside the clip box. Bump it (e.g. `8px`) only when the panel is nested inside a padded container where view content sits flush with the clip edge.

#### TransitionPanelView

A single view registered with the parent panel. Renders a `<div>` and accepts any native div prop (`className`, `style`, `id`, `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, `ref`, `data-*`, etc.) alongside those documented below; spread props land on the view wrapper. The consumer `ref` is composed with the internal ref used for registration. Visibility, slide offset, and `inert` state come from the parent's `activeKey`. Inactive views stay mounted (their internal state survives swaps) but are marked `inert` and `aria-hidden` so focus and assistive tech skip them.

<ApiProp
  name="viewKey"
  fullType="string"
  required
>
  Identifier matched against the parent's `activeKey` to determine when this view is visible.

<ApiProp
  name="initialFocus"
  fullType="boolean | React.RefObject<HTMLElement | null>"
  defaultValue="true"
>
  What to focus when this view becomes active after a swap. `true` focuses the first tabbable element inside the view, `false` opts out, and a ref focuses that specific element. Skipped on the initial render, since the parent surface (popover, dialog, sheet, page) owns first-mount focus. Focus uses `{ preventScroll: true }` so the entrance animation can finish without scroll-jank.

<ApiProp
  name="render"
  fullType="ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)"
  simpleType="element"
>
  Render the view as a different element or merge it with another component (e.g. a `Card`) instead of the default `<div>` wrapper. The registration ref and consumer `ref` are composed onto the rendered element.

##### Data attributes

<ApiProp
  name="data-slot"
  fullType='"transition-panel-view"'
>
  Styling hook for the view wrapper.

<ApiProp
  name="data-active"
  fullType="present when active"
>
  Present on the currently visible view.

<ApiProp
  name="data-viewkey"
  fullType="string"
>
  Mirrors the `viewKey` prop. Used internally to re-derive view order from DOM position on each registration.

### Notes

- **Composability.** Views can be wrapped in HOCs, fragments, error boundaries, or Suspense boundaries, or rendered via `.map()` and conditional logic. Registration routes through context, not React children.
- **Direction inference.** Direction is computed by comparing the new and previous `activeKey` against the registered view order, so back-navigation slides the opposite way automatically. Re-deriving from DOM position on each registration means a view that unmounts and remounts (e.g. `{isPro && <TransitionPanelView ...>}`) keeps its source-order slot.
- **Focus management.** Focus moves in a `useLayoutEffect`, before the browser paints, to minimize the gap between the outgoing view becoming `inert` and the incoming view receiving focus.
- **Height animation.** Animates the real `height` property (via `ResizeObserver`) rather than `transform: scale`, so descendant layout doesn't warp. The transition runs **only while swapping views**, so content that animates its own height inside the active view (an expanding error, an accordion) drives a single height tween the panel tracks exactly, instead of the panel running a second, competing one. That's fine for typical panels. If you need compositor-only height animation for a high-frequency surface, fork to a Motion / FLIP implementation.

---

# tree.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(composables)/tree.mdx

title: Tree
description: A hierarchical tree view component with support for selection, expansion, checkboxes, and keyboard navigation.
type: composable

The tree displays nested data as an expandable hierarchy with selection, checkboxes, and keyboard navigation. Use it for file explorers, nav menus, category pickers, or any parent-child structure. It renders each node through a child function, so you control the markup of every row.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="tree" example="tree-basic" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="tree" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="tree" />

## Composition

```text
Tree                      (data + render function)
└── TreeItem
    ├── TreeItemIcon
    ├── TreeItemLabel
    └── TreeItemBadge
```

`Tree` takes a `data` array and a child function that returns a `TreeItem` for each node. Compose the row from `TreeItemIcon`, `TreeItemLabel`, and `TreeItemBadge`.

## Examples

### Variants

Use `variant` to set the tree's surface treatment.

<ComponentPreview component="tree" example="tree-variants" />

| Value     | Description                          |
| --------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `default` | Minimal styling, no container.       |
| `filled`  | Card-like with a background.         |
| `outline` | Bordered card with a shadow.         |

### With Icons

Set `icon` on a node and `iconOpen` for a different icon while it is expanded.

<ComponentPreview component="tree" example="tree-with-icons" />

### With Lines

Use `showLines` to draw connecting lines between parent and child nodes.

<ComponentPreview component="tree" example="tree-with-lines" />

### With Badges

Set `badge` on a node and render it with `TreeItemBadge`.

<ComponentPreview component="tree" example="tree-with-badges" />

### With Checkboxes

Use `mode="multiple"` to add checkboxes; parent state reflects child selection automatically.

<ComponentPreview component="tree" example="tree-with-checkboxes" />

### Controlled State

Use `expanded`/`onExpandedChange` and `selectedNode`/`onNodeSelect` to drive state externally.

<ComponentPreview component="tree" example="tree-controlled" />

### Disabled & Loading States

Set `disabled` or `loading` on individual nodes, or `mode="none"` for a read-only tree.

<ComponentPreview component="tree" example="tree-disabled-loading" />

### Async Loading

Use `onLoadChildren` on a node to fetch children on first expand; the tree shows a spinner and caches the result.

<ComponentPreview component="tree" example="tree-async-loading" />

## Accessibility

The tree is operable from the keyboard: arrow keys move between and expand/collapse nodes, and `Enter` or `Space` selects. Selection and expansion state are reflected via `aria` attributes on each node, and disabled nodes are skipped during navigation.

## API Reference

The Tree component is built with [Base UI's Collapsible](https://base-ui.com/react/components/collapsible) internally for expand/collapse functionality. All Collapsible props are supported on tree nodes. The documentation below only covers custom props specific to our Tree implementation.

For the complete Base UI Collapsible API, see the [Base UI Collapsible documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/collapsible).

### Props

#### Tree

Hierarchical view for displaying nested data with selection and expansion. Uses Base UI's `Collapsible` internally.

<ApiProp name="data" fullType="TreeNode<TData>[]" simpleType="array" required>
  The hierarchical data structure to display.

<ApiProp name="children" fullType="(item: TreeNode<TData>) => React.ReactElement" simpleType="function" required>
  Render function for each node.

<ApiProp name="selectedNode" fullType="string | null" simpleType="string">
  Selected node ID (controlled).

<ApiProp name="onNodeSelect" fullType="(nodeId: string) => void" simpleType="function">
  Callback when node is selected.

<ApiProp name="defaultExpanded" fullType="string[]" simpleType="array" defaultValue="[]">
  Initially expanded node IDs (uncontrolled).

<ApiProp name="expanded" fullType="string[]" simpleType="array">
  Expanded node IDs (controlled).

<ApiProp name="onExpandedChange" fullType="(expanded: string[]) => void" simpleType="function">
  Callback when expanded nodes change.

<ApiProp name="checkedNodes" fullType="string[]" simpleType="array">
  Checked node IDs for checkbox mode.

<ApiProp name="onCheckedNodesChange" fullType="(checked: string[]) => void" simpleType="function">
  Callback when checked nodes change.

<ApiProp name="variant" fullType='"default" | "filled" | "outline"' simpleType="string" defaultValue='"default"'>
  Visual style variant.

<ApiProp name="showLines" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Show connecting lines between nodes.

<ApiProp name="mode" fullType='"single" | "multiple" | "none"' simpleType="string" defaultValue='"single"'>
  Selection mode.

#### TreeNode Interface

TypeScript interface defining the shape of each tree node:

<ApiProp name="id" fullType="string" required>
  Unique identifier for the node.

<ApiProp name="name" fullType="string" required>
  Display name for the node.

<ApiProp name="children" fullType="TreeNode[]" simpleType="array">
  Array of child nodes.

<ApiProp name="onLoadChildren" fullType="() => Promise<TreeNode[]>" simpleType="function">
  Async callback to load children on demand.

<ApiProp name="disabled" fullType="boolean">
  Whether this node is disabled.

<ApiProp name="loading" fullType="boolean">
  Whether this node is in a loading state.

<ApiProp name="icon" fullType="ReactNode" simpleType="node">
  Icon to display for this node.

<ApiProp name="iconOpen" fullType="ReactNode" simpleType="node">
  Alternative icon when node is expanded.

<ApiProp name="badge" fullType="ReactNode" simpleType="node">
  Badge content to display at the end of the node.

# accordion.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/accordion.mdx

title: Accordion
description: Vertically stacked set of interactive headings that reveal or hide associated content sections
type: primitive

import { Accordion, AccordionContent, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger } from "@/registry/default/accordion/accordion";

The accordion stacks collapsible sections, each with a header that toggles its content. Use it for FAQs, settings groups, or any list where showing one section at a time keeps the page short.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="accordion" example="accordion-demo" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="accordion" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="accordion" />

## Composition

```text
Accordion
└── AccordionItem
    ├── AccordionTrigger
    └── AccordionContent
```

`AccordionTrigger` renders its own `AccordionHeader` internally, so you compose only these four parts.

## Examples

### Multiple Open Items

Set `multiple` on `Accordion` to keep more than one item open at once.

<ComponentPreview component="accordion" example="accordion-multiple" />

### Default Expanded

Pass `defaultValue` on `Accordion` to expand items on first render.

<ComponentPreview component="accordion" example="accordion-default-expanded" />

### Disabled Items

Set `disabled` on an `AccordionItem` to prevent it from toggling.

<ComponentPreview component="accordion" example="accordion-disabled" />

### Chevron Indicator

Set `indicatorType="chevron"` on `AccordionTrigger` to use a chevron instead of the plus.

<ComponentPreview component="accordion" example="accordion-chevron-indicator" />

### Indicator at Start

Set `indicatorPosition="start"` on `AccordionTrigger` to move the indicator before the label.

<ComponentPreview component="accordion" example="accordion-indicator-start" />

### Without Indicator

Set `showIndicator={false}` on `AccordionTrigger` to hide the indicator.

<ComponentPreview component="accordion" example="accordion-without-indicator" />

### With Icon

Use the `icon` prop on `AccordionTrigger` to render a custom icon before the label.

<ComponentPreview component="accordion" example="accordion-with-icon" />

### With Subtitle

Use the `subtitle` prop on `AccordionTrigger` to render secondary text below the label.

<ComponentPreview component="accordion" example="accordion-with-subtitle" />

### Variants

Use `variant` on `Accordion` to change how items are framed and separated.

<ComponentPreview component="accordion" example="accordion-outline-variant" />

| Variant                    | Description                                                       |
| -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `default`                  | Borderless items divided by a bottom rule.                       |
| `split`                    | Each item is its own bordered card.                              |
| `outline`                  | Items grouped inside one bordered card.                          |
| `nested`                   | Indented items inside a muted, rounded container.                |
| `isolated-bordered`        | Bordered items that detach and round when opened.                |
| `isolated-filled`          | Filled items that detach and round when opened.                  |
| `isolated-filled-bordered` | Filled items with dividers that detach and round when opened.    |

<ComponentPreview component="accordion" example="accordion-split-variant" />

<ComponentPreview component="accordion" example="accordion-isolated-bordered-variant" />

<ComponentPreview component="accordion" example="accordion-isolated-filled-variant" />

<ComponentPreview component="accordion" example="accordion-isolated-filled-bordered-variant" />

<ComponentPreview component="accordion" example="accordion-nested-varaint" />

## API Reference

The Accordion component is built on top of [Base UI's Accordion](https://base-ui.com/react/components/accordion). All Base UI props are supported. The documentation below only covers custom props and modified defaults specific to our implementation.

For the complete Base UI API, see the [Base UI Accordion documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/accordion).

### Props

#### Accordion

Collapsible container that groups expandable content sections. Wraps Base UI's `Accordion.Root`.

<ApiProp
  name="variant"
  fullType='"default" | "split" | "outline" | "nested" | "isolated-bordered" | "isolated-filled" | "isolated-filled-bordered"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"default"'
>
  Visual styling variant for the accordion.

<ApiProp
  name="multiple"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Allow multiple accordion items to be expanded at the same time. Base UI doesn't set a default.

#### AccordionTrigger

Clickable header that toggles content visibility. Wraps Base UI's `Accordion.Trigger`.

<ApiProp
  name="showIndicator"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="true"
>
  Show or hide the expand/collapse indicator icon. Custom prop not available in Base UI.

<ApiProp
  name="indicatorType"
  fullType='"chevron" | "plus"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"plus"'
>
  Type of indicator icon to display. Custom prop not available in Base UI.

<ApiProp
  name="indicatorPosition"
  fullType='"start" | "end"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"end"'
>
  Position of the indicator icon relative to the trigger text. Custom prop not available in Base UI.

<ApiProp
  name="icon"
  fullType="ReactNode"
>
  Custom icon to display at the start of the trigger. Custom prop not available in Base UI.

<ApiProp
  name="subtitle"
  fullType="ReactNode"
>
  Subtitle text to display below the trigger text. Custom prop not available in Base UI.

# alert-dialog.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/alert-dialog.mdx

title: Alert Dialog
description: Modal dialog that interrupts the user with important content and requires an action
type: primitive

import { AlertDialog, AlertDialogClose, AlertDialogContent, AlertDialogDescription, AlertDialogFooter, AlertDialogHeader, AlertDialogTitle, AlertDialogTrigger } from "@/registry/default/alert-dialog/alert-dialog";

An alert dialog is a modal that interrupts the user to confirm a consequential action. Use it for destructive or irreversible choices such as deleting an account, where the user must explicitly confirm or cancel.

For non-blocking dialogs the user can dismiss freely, use [`Dialog`](/docs/components/dialog) instead.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="alert-dialog" example="alert-dialog-basic" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="alert-dialog" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="alert-dialog" />

## Composition

```text
AlertDialog
├── AlertDialogTrigger
└── AlertDialogContent
    ├── AlertDialogHeader
    │   ├── AlertDialogTitle
    │   └── AlertDialogDescription
    ├── AlertDialogBody
    └── AlertDialogFooter
        └── AlertDialogClose
```

## Examples

### Controlled

Use the `open` and `onOpenChange` props on `AlertDialog` to control the open state.

<ComponentPreview component="alert-dialog" example="alert-dialog-controlled" />

### Nested

Nest alert dialogs to chain multi-step confirmations.

<ComponentPreview component="alert-dialog" example="alert-dialog-nested" />

### Detached Trigger

Use `createAlertDialogHandle()` to drive one dialog from triggers rendered outside it.

<ComponentPreview component="alert-dialog" example="alert-dialog-detached-trigger" />

## API Reference

The AlertDialog component is built on top of [Base UI's AlertDialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/alert-dialog). All Base UI props are supported. The documentation below only covers custom props specific to our implementation.

For the complete Base UI API, see the [Base UI AlertDialog documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/alert-dialog).

### Utilities

#### createAlertDialogHandle

Creates a handle that connects an alert dialog to one or more external `AlertDialogTrigger` components. Useful when the triggers need to live outside the `AlertDialog`, for example when each row in a list has its own delete button but they all share one confirmation dialog.

```tsx
import { createAlertDialogHandle } from "@/registry/default/alert-dialog/alert-dialog";

const handle = createAlertDialogHandle();
```

##### Passing data from the trigger to the alert dialog

The handle accepts an optional `<Payload>` generic that types a value each trigger can pass along. The alert dialog reads it through a render-prop child, so you can render different content (or target different resources) per trigger without duplicating the dialog markup.

```tsx
type User = { id: string; name: string };

const handle = createAlertDialogHandle<User>();

// Multiple triggers, each with its own payload:
users.map((user) => (
  <AlertDialogTrigger key={user.id} handle={handle} payload={user}>
    Delete {user.name}
  </AlertDialogTrigger>
));

// One shared alert dialog that renders based on the active trigger:
<AlertDialog handle={handle}>
  <AlertDialogContent>
    {({ payload: user }) => (
      <AlertDialogHeader>
        <AlertDialogTitle>Delete {user?.name}?</AlertDialogTitle>
      </AlertDialogHeader>
    )}
  </AlertDialogContent>
</AlertDialog>;
```

Without the `<User>` generic, `payload` inside the render prop resolves to `unknown`.

### Props

#### AlertDialogContent

Modal container for important messages requiring user action. Composes `AlertDialog.Portal`, `AlertDialog.Backdrop`, and `AlertDialog.Popup`. Props are forwarded to `AlertDialog.Popup`.

<ApiProp name="showCloseButton" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Whether to show a close button in the top-right corner of the dialog.

<ApiProp name="variant" fullType='"default" | "inset"' defaultValue='"default"'>
  The visual variant of the dialog. The `inset` variant adds a muted background with a top border to the footer.

<ApiProp name="level" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="5">
  Surface elevation level. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs.

<ApiProp name="shadowLevel" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="5">
  Shadow weight.

#### AlertDialogBody

Scrollable content area within the alert dialog.

<ApiProp
  name="nativeScroll"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Use native browser scrolling instead of Base UI's ScrollArea. Fade edges still
  work using CSS scroll-driven animations (Chrome 115+, with static fallback).
  Note: `persistScrollbar` is not supported with `nativeScroll`.

<ApiProp
  name="fadeEdges"
  fullType="boolean | 'top' | 'bottom' | 'left' | 'right' | 'x' | 'y' | FadeEdge[]"
  defaultValue="true"
>
  Controls the fade effect on scroll edges. See [ScrollArea](/docs/components/scroll-area#custom-props) for all options.

<ApiProp
  name="scrollbarGutter"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Reserves space for the scrollbar when content overflows, preventing layout shift.

<ApiProp
  name="persistScrollbar"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Always show the scrollbar instead of fading it in on hover or scroll.

<ApiProp
  name="hideScrollbar"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Hides the scrollbar while keeping scroll functionality.

### Notes

#### AlertDialogClose

Use `AlertDialogClose` with the `render` prop to create action buttons that close the dialog. Wraps Base UI's `AlertDialog.Close`.

```tsx
<AlertDialogFooter>
  <AlertDialogClose render={<Button variant="outline">Cancel</Button>} />
  <AlertDialogClose render={<Button variant="destructive">Delete</Button>} />
</AlertDialogFooter>
```

---

# alert.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/alert.mdx

title: Alert
description: Display important messages and notifications to users with various severity levels
type: primitive

import { Alert, AlertDescription, AlertTitle } from "@/registry/default/alert/alert";

An alert is a callout that surfaces a short, important message inline with the page content. Use it for form-level errors, status banners, or warnings that need to stay visible, not for transient toasts.

For dismissible messages that auto-disappear, use [`Toast`](/docs/components/toast) instead.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="alert" example="alert-demo" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="alert" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="alert" />

## Composition

```text
Alert
├── AlertTitle
├── AlertDescription
└── AlertAction
```

## Examples

### Info

Use `variant="info"` for informational messages.

<ComponentPreview component="alert" example="alert-info" />

### Success

Use `variant="success"` to confirm a completed action.

<ComponentPreview component="alert" example="alert-success" />

### Warning

Use `variant="warning"` for messages that need attention.

<ComponentPreview component="alert" example="alert-warning" />

### Danger

Use `variant="danger"` for errors and critical messages.

<ComponentPreview component="alert" example="alert-danger" />

| Variant   | Description                              |
| --------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `default` | A neutral, low-emphasis message.         |
| `info`    | An informational message.                |
| `success` | A completed or successful action.        |
| `warning` | A condition that needs attention.        |
| `danger`  | An error or critical message.            |

### With Icon

Place an SVG as the first child of `Alert` to show an icon beside the message.

<ComponentPreview component="alert" example="alert-with-icon" />

### With Actions

Use `AlertAction` to add buttons alongside the message.

<ComponentPreview component="alert" example="alert-with-actions" />

### Without Title

Omit `AlertTitle` to render a description-only alert.

<ComponentPreview component="alert" example="alert-without-title" />

## Accessibility

Each `Alert` has `role="alert"`, so screen readers announce its content when it appears. Because the variants signal severity through color, pair `danger` and `warning` alerts with an icon or explicit wording (such as "Error:") so the meaning carries without color.

## API Reference

The Alert is built on top of Base UI's [`useRender`](https://base-ui.com/react/utils/use-render), so every part accepts a `render` prop for polymorphic rendering. The documentation below covers the custom props specific to our implementation.

### Props

#### Alert

Callout container that surfaces an inline message. Sets `role="alert"` and accepts a `render` prop.

<ApiProp
  name="variant"
  fullType='"default" | "info" | "success" | "warning" | "danger"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"default"'
>
  Severity style of the alert, applied to the accent bar and icon color.

<ApiProp name="render" fullType="ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)" simpleType="element">
  Element or function used to render the alert in place of the default `div`.

#### AlertTitle

Heading line of the alert. Renders an `h4` by default and accepts a `render` prop.

<ApiProp name="render" fullType="ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)" simpleType="element">
  Element or function used to render the title in place of the default `h4`.

#### AlertDescription

Body text of the alert. Renders a `div` by default and accepts a `render` prop.

<ApiProp name="render" fullType="ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)" simpleType="element">
  Element or function used to render the description in place of the default `div`.

#### AlertAction

Container for buttons placed alongside the message. Renders a `div` by default and accepts a `render` prop.

<ApiProp name="render" fullType="ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)" simpleType="element">
  Element or function used to render the action container in place of the default `div`.

# aspect-ratio.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/aspect-ratio.mdx

title: Aspect Ratio
description: Maintains a consistent width-to-height ratio for responsive content
type: primitive

import { AspectRatio } from "@/registry/default/aspect-ratio/aspect-ratio";

Aspect Ratio constrains its content to a fixed width-to-height ratio as the container resizes. Use it to reserve space for images, video embeds, and media cards so the layout doesn't shift while they load.

## Preview

## Examples

### Square Ratio

Set `ratio="1/1"` for a square container.

<ComponentPreview component="aspect-ratio" example="aspect-ratio-square" />

### Portrait Orientation

Use a `ratio` below `1` (such as `3/4`) for taller-than-wide content.

<ComponentPreview component="aspect-ratio" example="aspect-ratio-portrait-orientation" />

### Multiple Ratios

Pass different `ratio` values to compare common aspect ratios side by side.

<ComponentPreview component="aspect-ratio" example="aspect-ratio-multiple-ratios" />

### Video Embed

Wrap an iframe in `ratio="16/9"` for a responsive video embed.

<ComponentPreview component="aspect-ratio" example="aspect-ratio-video-embed" />

## API Reference

Aspect Ratio is a custom styled `div` wrapper. All props are custom or standard `div` attributes passed through.

### Props

#### AspectRatio

Wraps its content in a `div` that holds a fixed width-to-height ratio.

<ApiProp
  name="ratio"
  fullType="number | `${number}/${number}`"
  defaultValue="1"
>
  Width-to-height ratio of the container. Accepts a number (such as `1.7778`) or a string fraction (such as `"16/9"`), which is divided into a number.

# autocomplete.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/autocomplete.mdx

title: Autocomplete
description: Text input with intelligent suggestions and auto-completion functionality
type: primitive

import { Autocomplete } from "@/registry/default/autocomplete/autocomplete";

Autocomplete is a text input that suggests matching options as the user types, while still accepting free-form text. Use it for search fields, tag entry, or any input where suggestions speed things up but the value isn't restricted to the list.

For selecting a single required value from a fixed list, use [`Combobox`](/docs/components/combobox) instead.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="autocomplete" example="autocomplete-basic" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="autocomplete" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="autocomplete" />

## Composition

```text
AutocompleteRoot
├── AutocompleteInput
│   ├── AutocompleteTrigger
│   └── AutocompleteClear
└── AutocompletePortal
    └── AutocompletePositioner
        └── AutocompletePopup
            ├── AutocompleteEmpty
            └── AutocompleteList
                ├── AutocompleteGroup
                │   ├── AutocompleteGroupLabel
                │   └── AutocompleteItem
                └── AutocompleteItem
```

## Examples

### Async Loading

Fetch suggestions from an API as the query changes.

<ComponentPreview component="autocomplete" example="autocomplete-async" />

### Auto Highlight

Set `autoHighlight` on `AutocompleteRoot` to highlight the first suggestion automatically.

<ComponentPreview
  component="autocomplete"
  example="autocomplete-auto-highlight"
/>

### Clearable Input

Set `showClear` on `AutocompleteInput` to add a button that resets the value.

<ComponentPreview component="autocomplete" example="autocomplete-clear" />

### Trigger and Clear

Set `showTrigger` and `showClear` on `AutocompleteInput` to show a popup toggle and a clear button. Same anatomy as the [Combobox](/docs/components/combobox).

<ComponentPreview component="autocomplete" example="autocomplete-trigger" />

### Fuzzy Search

Pass a fuzzy matcher as the `filter` to match suggestions loosely.

<ComponentPreview component="autocomplete" example="autocomplete-fuzzy" />

### Grouped Options

Wrap items in `AutocompleteGroup` with an `AutocompleteGroupLabel` to organize them into categories.

<ComponentPreview component="autocomplete" example="autocomplete-grouped" />

### Inline Suggestions

Set `mode="both"` on `AutocompleteRoot` to complete the input inline with the highlighted suggestion.

<ComponentPreview component="autocomplete" example="autocomplete-inline" />

### Limited Results

Use `limit` on `AutocompleteRoot` to cap the number of suggestions shown.

<ComponentPreview component="autocomplete" example="autocomplete-limit" />

### Virtualized

Use virtualization for large lists (100+ items) so only the items in view are rendered, keeping the list smooth.

<ComponentPreview component="autocomplete" example="autocomplete-virtualized" />

**Key concepts:**

1. **Use `useListVirtualizer` hook** - Handles scroll positioning, keyboard navigation, and item measurement. See [useListVirtualizer docs](/docs/hooks/use-list-virtualizer) for full API reference.
2. **Use `useAutocompleteFilteredItems()` inside Root** - Call `useAutocompleteFilteredItems()` in a child component of `AutocompleteRoot` to get internally filtered items without manual filtering boilerplate.
3. **Replace `AutocompleteList` with `AutocompleteVirtualizedList`** - Accepts `scrollRef` and `totalSize` from the hook.
4. **Pass `virtualized` and `items` on Root** - Enables virtualized mode with your full item list.
5. **Use `useHighlightHandler`** - Pass a `virtualizerRef` to the child and use `useHighlightHandler(virtualizerRef)` on Root so keyboard navigation scrolls to the highlighted item.
6. **Override item margins** - Pass `className="mt-0! mb-0!"` to `AutocompleteItem` since virtualized items are absolutely positioned and the virtualizer handles padding.

> **Manual filtering still works.** If you need custom filter logic (fuzzy search, server-side filtering), you can still compute `filteredItems` externally, pass `filter={null}` to `Autocomplete.Root`, and spread `rootProps` from `useListVirtualizer`. See [useAutocompleteFilter](#useautocompletefilter).

### Elevated Variant

On a Card, Dialog, or popover surface, the opaque `default` input collapses into its parent. Use `variant="elevated"` on `AutocompleteInput` for a translucent overlay that adapts to the substrate. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs.

<ComponentPreview component="autocomplete" example="autocomplete-elevated" />

### Form Integration

Use [Field](/docs/components/field) with `FieldLabel` for labeling. See the [Forms guide](/docs/getting-started/forms) for more patterns.

<ComponentPreview component="autocomplete" example="autocomplete-field" />

## API Reference

The Autocomplete component is built on top of [Base UI's Autocomplete](https://base-ui.com/react/components/autocomplete). All Base UI props are supported. The documentation below only covers custom props and modified defaults specific to our implementation.

For the complete Base UI API, see the [Base UI Autocomplete documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/autocomplete).

### Props

#### AutocompleteInput

Text input with optional trigger and clear buttons. When `showTrigger` or `showClear` is enabled, wraps the input inside an `Autocomplete.InputGroup`.

<ApiProp name="showTrigger" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Show a trigger button to open the popup.

<ApiProp name="showClear" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Show a clear button to reset the input value. Only visible when the input has a value.

<ApiProp name="variant" fullType='"default" | "elevated"' defaultValue='"default"'>
  Surface appearance of the input. `default` uses opaque `bg-input`. `elevated` uses translucent `bg-input-elevated` for use inside Card, Dialog, or popover surfaces. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs.

#### AutocompletePositioner

Positions the suggestions dropdown relative to the input. Wraps Base UI's `Autocomplete.Positioner`.

<ApiProp name="sideOffset" fullType="number" defaultValue="6">
  Distance between the trigger and the popup. Base UI defaults to `0`.

#### AutocompletePopup

The popup container. Wraps Base UI's `Autocomplete.Popup`.

<ApiProp name="level" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="3">
  Surface elevation level for the popup. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs. Uses `elevatedSurface` (rim on `::after`) so sticky group labels stay below the rim edge.

<ApiProp name="shadowLevel" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="3">
  Shadow weight. Controls drop-shadow intensity independently of substrate color.

#### AutocompleteList

Scrollable container for suggestion items. Wraps Base UI's `Autocomplete.List`.

<ApiProp name="nativeScroll" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Use native browser scrolling with styled scrollbars instead of Base UI's
  scroll virtualization. Enables CSS scroll-driven animations for fade edges.

<ApiProp
  name="fadeEdges"
  fullType="boolean | 'top' | 'bottom' | 'left' | 'right' | 'x' | 'y' | FadeEdge[]"
  defaultValue="true"
>
  Controls the fade effect on scroll edges. See
  [ScrollArea](/docs/components/scroll-area#custom-props) for all options.

<ApiProp name="scrollbarGutter" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Reserves space for the scrollbar when content overflows, preventing layout
  shift.

<ApiProp name="persistScrollbar" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Always show the scrollbar instead of fading it in on hover or scroll.

<ApiProp name="hideScrollbar" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Hides the scrollbar while keeping scroll functionality.

#### AutocompleteVirtualizedList

Virtualized scrollable container for large lists. Use with `useListVirtualizer` hook for optimal performance with 100+ items.

<ApiProp
  name="scrollRef"
  fullType="(element: HTMLDivElement | null) => void"
  required
>
  Ref callback from `useListVirtualizer` for the scroll container.

<ApiProp name="totalSize" fullType="number" required>
  Total height of all virtual items in pixels. Provided by `useListVirtualizer`.

<ApiProp
  name="emptyMessage"
  fullType="ReactNode"
  simpleType="node"
  defaultValue='"No results found."'
>
  Message shown when no results are found.

<ApiProp
  name="fadeEdges"
  fullType="boolean | 'x' | 'y' | FadeEdge[]"
  defaultValue='"y"'
>
  Controls the fade effect on scroll edges.

<ApiProp name="nativeScroll" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Use native browser scrolling instead of custom scrollbars. Recommended for
  best virtualization performance.

### Utilities

#### highlightText

Highlights matching portions of text by wrapping them in `<mark>` tags. Useful for showing which parts of a suggestion match the user's input.

See [highlightText](/docs/utils/highlight-text) for full documentation and API reference.

### Hooks

#### useAutocompleteFilter

```ts
function useAutocompleteFilter(): {
  contains: (
    item: T,
    query: string,
    getItemLabel: (item: T) => string,
  ) => boolean;
  startsWith: (
    item: T,
    query: string,
    getItemLabel: (item: T) => string,
  ) => boolean;
  endsWith: (
    item: T,
    query: string,
    getItemLabel: (item: T) => string,
  ) => boolean;
};
```

Exposes Base UI's built-in filter matchers for external filtering. Required when using virtualization since you must compute `filteredItems` yourself.

**Returns**

| Property     | Type                                     | Description                                                  |
| ------------ | ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `contains`   | `(item, query, getItemLabel) => boolean` | Returns true if item label contains query (case-insensitive) |
| `startsWith` | `(item, query, getItemLabel) => boolean` | Returns true if item label starts with query                 |
| `endsWith`   | `(item, query, getItemLabel) => boolean` | Returns true if item label ends with query                   |

```tsx
import { useAutocompleteFilter } from "@/registry/default/autocomplete/autocomplete";

const { contains } = useAutocompleteFilter();
const getItemLabel = (item: Item | null) => item?.name ?? "";

const filteredItems = useMemo(
  () => items.filter((item) => contains(item, query, getItemLabel)),
  [contains, query],
);
```

#### useAutocompleteFilteredItems

```ts
function useAutocompleteFilteredItems<T>(): T[];
```

Returns the internally filtered items from the Autocomplete Root. Must be called inside `AutocompleteRoot`. Simplifies virtualized implementations by eliminating the need for manual query state, `useDeferredValue`, `useFilter()`, and `useMemo` filtering.

```tsx
import { useAutocompleteFilteredItems } from "@/registry/default/autocomplete/autocomplete";

function VirtualizedListContent() {
  // Must be called inside AutocompleteRoot
  const filteredItems = useAutocompleteFilteredItems<MyItem>();

  const virtualizer = useListVirtualizer({
    items: allItems,
    filteredItems,
  });
  // ...
}
```

#### useFuzzyFilter

Provides fuzzy matching capabilities for flexible searching across multiple fields. Returns filter functions compatible with Base UI's Autocomplete.

See [useFuzzyFilter](/docs/hooks/use-fuzzy-filter) for full documentation and API reference.

#### useListVirtualizer

Provides virtualization for large autocomplete lists using TanStack Virtual. Abstracts scroll handling, item positioning, and keyboard navigation.

See [useListVirtualizer](/docs/hooks/use-list-virtualizer) for full documentation and API reference.

---

# avatar.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/avatar.mdx

title: Avatar
description: Display user profile images with fallback support and status indicators

import { Avatar, AvatarImage, AvatarFallback } from "@/registry/default/avatar/avatar";

An avatar shows a user's profile image, falling back to initials or an icon when the image is missing or fails to load. Use it in comment threads, member lists, navbars, and anywhere you identify a person or account.

# base-drawer.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/base-drawer.mdx

title: Base Drawer
description: A swipe-gesture drawer built on Base UI's official Drawer component with snap points, nested stacking, and indent effects
type: primitive

import {
  BaseDrawer,
  BaseDrawerBar,
  BaseDrawerClose,
  BaseDrawerContent,
  BaseDrawerDescription,
  BaseDrawerFooter,
  BaseDrawerHeader,
  BaseDrawerPanel,
  BaseDrawerPopup,
  BaseDrawerTitle,
  BaseDrawerTrigger,
} from "@/registry/default/base-drawer/base-drawer";

Base Drawer is a panel that slides in from a screen edge and responds to swipe gestures, with support for snap points, nested stacking, and an indent effect on the background. Use it for mobile-first navigation, filters, or detail panels where dragging to dismiss feels natural.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="base-drawer" example="base-drawer-basic" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="base-drawer" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="base-drawer" />

## Composition

```text
BaseDrawer
├── BaseDrawerTrigger
└── BaseDrawerPopup
    ├── BaseDrawerBar
    ├── BaseDrawerHeader
    │   ├── BaseDrawerTitle
    │   └── BaseDrawerDescription
    ├── BaseDrawerPanel
    └── BaseDrawerFooter
        └── BaseDrawerClose
```

## Examples

### Side Drawer

Use `position="right"` to slide the drawer in from the side.

<ComponentPreview component="base-drawer" example="base-drawer-side" />

### Directions

Use `position` to open the drawer from any screen edge.

<ComponentPreview component="base-drawer" example="base-drawer-directions" />

| Position | Description                          |
| -------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `bottom` | Slides up from the bottom (default). |
| `top`    | Slides down from the top.            |
| `left`   | Slides in from the left.             |
| `right`  | Slides in from the right.            |

### Controlled

Use the `open` and `onOpenChange` props on `BaseDrawer` to control the open state.

<ComponentPreview component="base-drawer" example="base-drawer-controlled" />

### Snap Points

Use `snapPoints` on `BaseDrawer` to let the drawer rest at multiple heights. Numbers from 0 to 1 are viewport fractions, strings support `px` and `rem` units.

<ComponentPreview component="base-drawer" example="base-drawer-snap-points" />

### Floating Variant

Use `variant="floating"` on `BaseDrawerPopup` for inset spacing and fully rounded corners on desktop.

<ComponentPreview component="base-drawer" example="base-drawer-floating" />

### Inset Footer

Use `variant="inset"` on `BaseDrawerFooter` to separate the footer with a top border and muted background.

<ComponentPreview component="base-drawer" example="base-drawer-inset-footer" />

### Nested Drawers

Nest drawers to stack them with scale and translate animations, each independently focus managed.

<ComponentPreview component="base-drawer" example="base-drawer-nested" />

### Indent Effect

Use `BaseDrawerProvider`, `BaseDrawerIndentBackground`, and `BaseDrawerIndent` to scale and round the background content when a drawer opens.

<ComponentPreview component="base-drawer" example="base-drawer-indent" />

### With Form

Use `BaseDrawerPanel` to hold form elements; it wraps content in `Drawer.Content` so text selection works without triggering swipe gestures.

<ComponentPreview component="base-drawer" example="base-drawer-with-form" />

### Scrollable Content

Use `BaseDrawerPanel` for scrollable content that coexists with swipe gestures.

<ComponentPreview component="base-drawer" example="base-drawer-with-scroll" />

## API Reference

Built on [Base UI's Drawer](https://base-ui.com/react/components/drawer). All Base UI Drawer props are supported.

### Props

#### BaseDrawer

Root component that manages drawer state. Wraps Base UI's `Drawer.Root`.

<ApiProp
  name="position"
  fullType='"top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"bottom"'
>
  Which edge of the screen the drawer slides in from.

<ApiProp
  name="snapPoints"
  fullType='(number | string)[]'
  simpleType="array"
>
  Snap points for the drawer. Numbers 0-1 are viewport fractions, strings
  support `px`/`rem` units.

<ApiProp name="open" fullType="boolean">
  Controlled open state.

<ApiProp
  name="onOpenChange"
  fullType="(open: boolean, eventDetails: ChangeEventDetails) => void"
  simpleType="function"
>
  Callback fired when the drawer opens or closes.

<ApiProp
  name="modal"
  fullType='boolean | "trap-focus"'
  simpleType="boolean | string"
  defaultValue="true"
>
  Controls modal behavior.

#### BaseDrawerPopup

Convenience composite that renders Portal + Backdrop + Viewport + Popup. This is the main content wrapper.

<ApiProp
  name="variant"
  fullType='"default" | "floating"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"default"'
>
  Visual style. `"floating"` adds inset spacing and rounded corners on desktop.

<ApiProp name="showBar" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Whether to show the drag handle bar. Automatically adapts orientation based on
  position.

<ApiProp name="showCloseButton" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Whether to show an X close button in the top-right corner.

<ApiProp
  name="position"
  fullType='"top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left"'
  simpleType="string"
>
  Override the position from context. Usually inherited from `BaseDrawer`.

<ApiProp name="level" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="5">
  Surface elevation level. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs. The default (viewport-flush) variant uses a single-edge rim on the inner-facing side.

<ApiProp name="shadowLevel" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="5">
  Shadow weight.

#### BaseDrawerPanel

Scrollable content area. Wraps `ScrollArea` and `Drawer.Content` for text selection support.

<ApiProp name="scrollable" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="true">
  Whether to wrap content in a ScrollArea.

<ApiProp name="scrollFade" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="true">
  Whether to show fade edges on scroll.

<ApiProp name="allowSelection" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="true">
  When true, wraps in `Drawer.Content` so text selection works without
  triggering swipe gestures.

#### BaseDrawerFooter

<ApiProp
  name="variant"
  fullType='"default" | "inset"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"default"'
>
  `"default"` is minimal padding. `"inset"` adds a border-top and muted
  background.

<ApiProp name="allowSelection" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="true">
  When true, wraps in `Drawer.Content` for text selection support.

### Components

| Component                        | Description                                                       |
| -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `BaseDrawer`                     | Root component with position context                              |
| `BaseDrawerTrigger`              | Button that opens the drawer                                      |
| `BaseDrawerPopup`                | Convenience composite (Portal + Backdrop + Viewport + Popup)      |
| `BaseDrawerBar`                  | Drag handle indicator (adapts orientation per position)            |
| `BaseDrawerHeader`               | Container for title and description                               |
| `BaseDrawerTitle`                | Accessible title element                                          |
| `BaseDrawerDescription`          | Accessible description element                                    |
| `BaseDrawerPanel`                | Scrollable content area with text selection support                |
| `BaseDrawerFooter`               | Container for action buttons                                      |
| `BaseDrawerClose`                | Button that closes the drawer                                     |
| `BaseDrawerContent`              | Pass-through to `Drawer.Content` for text selection in custom layouts |
| `BaseDrawerMenu`                 | Navigation menu container                                         |
| `BaseDrawerMenuItem`             | Menu item button                                                  |
| `BaseDrawerMenuTrigger`          | Menu item that opens a nested drawer                              |
| `BaseDrawerMenuSeparator`        | Menu divider                                                      |
| `BaseDrawerMenuGroup`            | Menu item group                                                   |
| `BaseDrawerMenuGroupLabel`       | Group label                                                       |
| `BaseDrawerMenuCheckboxItem`     | Checkbox menu item (default or switch variant)                    |
| `BaseDrawerMenuRadioGroup`       | Radio group container                                             |
| `BaseDrawerMenuRadioItem`        | Radio menu item                                                   |
| `BaseDrawerProvider`             | Shared context for indent effect                                  |
| `BaseDrawerIndent`               | App content wrapper for indent/scale effect                       |
| `BaseDrawerIndentBackground`     | Background layer behind indent                                    |
| `BaseDrawerSwipeArea`            | Invisible area for swipe-to-open gestures                         |

### CSS Variables

Base UI's Drawer exposes CSS custom properties on the popup element:

| Variable                        | Description                                                    |
| ------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--drawer-swipe-progress`       | Progress toward dismissed (0 = open, 1 = dismissed)            |
| `--drawer-swipe-movement-x`     | Horizontal swipe offset in pixels                              |
| `--drawer-swipe-movement-y`     | Vertical swipe offset in pixels                                |
| `--drawer-swipe-strength`       | Velocity-based strength (scales exit animation duration)        |
| `--drawer-snap-point-offset`    | Vertical offset for snap point positioning                     |
| `--drawer-height`               | Current drawer height                                          |
| `--drawer-frontmost-height`     | Height of the frontmost drawer in a nested stack               |
| `--nested-drawers`              | Number of nested drawers open                                  |
