# breadcrumbs.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/breadcrumbs.mdx

title: Breadcrumbs
description: Navigation component that shows the current location within a hierarchy
type: primitive

import { Breadcrumb, BreadcrumbItem, BreadcrumbSeparator } from "@/registry/default/breadcrumbs/breadcrumbs";

Breadcrumbs show where the current page sits in a site's hierarchy and let users jump back to any ancestor. Use them on deep, nested routes such as docs sections, dashboards, or file paths.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="breadcrumbs" example="breadcrumbs-basic" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="breadcrumbs" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="breadcrumbs" />

## Composition

```text
Breadcrumb
└── BreadcrumbList
    ├── BreadcrumbItem
    │   ├── BreadcrumbLink
    │   └── BreadcrumbPage
    ├── BreadcrumbSeparator
    └── BreadcrumbEllipsis
```

## Examples

### Variants

Use `variant` on `Breadcrumb` to switch between the plain default and a framed `surface` style.

<ComponentPreview component="breadcrumbs" example="breadcrumbs-variants" />

| Variant   | Description                                                      |
| --------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `default` | A plain inline trail. The simplest, most common style.          |
| `surface` | A framed track with the current page lifted onto a raised pill. |

### Size Variants

Use `size` on `Breadcrumb` to scale the text and spacing.

<ComponentPreview component="breadcrumbs" example="breadcrumbs-size-variants" />

| Size | Description           |
| ---- | --------------------- |
| `sm` | A compact breadcrumb. |
| `md` | The default size.     |
| `lg` | A larger breadcrumb.  |

### Custom Separator

Pass children to `BreadcrumbSeparator` to replace the default chevron.

<ComponentPreview component="breadcrumbs" example="breadcrumbs-custom-separator" />

### Custom Separator with Prop

Use the `separator` prop on `BreadcrumbSeparator` to set the divider element.

<ComponentPreview component="breadcrumbs" example="breadcrumbs-custom-separator-with-prop" />

### With Icons

Place an icon inside `BreadcrumbLink` to add context to an item.

<ComponentPreview component="breadcrumbs" example="breadcrumbs-with-icons" />

### With Ellipsis

Use `BreadcrumbEllipsis` to collapse the middle of a long path.

<ComponentPreview component="breadcrumbs" example="breadcrumbs-with-ellipsis-for-long-paths" />

### Dropdown

Compose a `BreadcrumbItem` with a [DropdownMenu](/docs/components/dropdown-menu) to collapse part of the path into a menu.

<ComponentPreview component="breadcrumbs" example="breadcrumbs-dropdown" />

### With Next.js Link

Use the `render` prop on `BreadcrumbLink` to render a Next.js `Link`.

<ComponentPreview component="breadcrumbs" example="breadcrumbs-with-next-js-link" />

### With Accessibility Features

Add `aria-label` to items and the nav to clarify the trail for assistive tech.

<ComponentPreview component="breadcrumbs" example="breadcrumbs-with-accessibility-features" />

## Accessibility

The `Breadcrumb` nav defaults to `aria-label="breadcrumb"`. `BreadcrumbPage` marks the current location with `role="link"`, `aria-disabled="true"`, and `aria-current="page"`, so assistive tech announces it as the current, non-actionable page. `BreadcrumbLink` shows a visible focus ring on keyboard focus. Separators are hidden with `aria-hidden`, and `BreadcrumbEllipsis` carries a screen-reader label ("More pages" by default) for the collapsed items.

### Labeling a collapsed trigger

When you collapse items into a [DropdownMenu](/docs/components/dropdown-menu), give the icon-only trigger an accessible name. `BreadcrumbEllipsis` is hidden from assistive tech, so the button has no name on its own.

```tsx showLineNumbers
<DropdownMenuTrigger render={<Button variant="ghost" size="icon_sm" />}>
  <BreadcrumbEllipsis />
  <span className="sr-only">Toggle menu</span>
</DropdownMenuTrigger>
```

## API Reference

Breadcrumbs are custom styled components built on native HTML elements (`nav`, `ol`, `li`, `a`, `span`). `BreadcrumbLink` is polymorphic through Base UI's `render` prop; the other parts pass through standard attributes for their element.

### Props

#### Breadcrumb

Navigation landmark that wraps the trail. Renders a `nav`.

<ApiProp name="variant" fullType='"default" | "surface"' simpleType="string" defaultValue='"default"'>
  Visual style of the trail. `default` is a plain inline trail; `surface` frames it in a raised track with the current page lifted onto a pill. Applied through a `data-variant` attribute that descendants read.

<ApiProp name="size" fullType='"sm" | "md" | "lg"' simpleType="string" defaultValue='"md"'>
  Scale of the text and spacing for the whole trail, applied through a `data-size` attribute that descendants read.

<ApiProp name="aria-label" fullType="string" defaultValue='"breadcrumb"'>
  Accessible label for the navigation landmark.

#### BreadcrumbLink

Interactive ancestor link. Renders an `a` by default.

<ApiProp name="render" fullType="ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)" simpleType="element">
  Render the link as a different element, such as a Next.js `Link`. Pass the element and its props are merged in, for example `render={<Link href="/" />}`.

#### BreadcrumbSeparator

Divider between items. Renders an `li` marked `aria-hidden`, defaulting to a chevron icon.

<ApiProp name="separator" fullType="ReactNode" simpleType="node">
  Custom divider element. Used when no `children` are provided, in place of the default chevron.

#### BreadcrumbEllipsis

Collapsed indicator for the middle of a long path. Renders a `span` marked `aria-hidden` with a screen-reader label.

<ApiProp name="aria-label" fullType="string" defaultValue='"More pages"'>
  Screen-reader label announced for the collapsed items.

---

# button.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/button.mdx

title: Button
description: Clickable button with various styles and sizes
type: primitive

import { Button } from "@/registry/default/button/button";

Buttons trigger an action or event: submitting a form, opening a dialog, or
confirming a choice. Use them for in-page actions, not for navigation between
pages.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="button" example="button-demo" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="button" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="button" />

## Examples

### Variants

Use `variant` to change the button's visual weight and color.

<ComponentPreview component="button" example="button-variants" />

| Variant            | Description                                              |
| ------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `primary`          | The default, highest-emphasis action.                   |
| `primary-soft`     | A tinted primary for a lower-emphasis branded action.   |
| `neutral`          | A solid neutral action with no brand color.             |
| `secondary`        | The standard lower-emphasis action.                     |
| `outline`          | A bordered action for secondary actions.                |
| `ghost`            | A borderless action for toolbars and dense UI.          |
| `link`             | Renders as inline text, like a link.                    |
| `destructive`      | A destructive action such as delete.                    |
| `destructive-soft` | A tinted destructive for a lower-emphasis warning.      |

### Sizes

Use `size` to set the button's height and padding.

<ComponentPreview component="button" example="button-sizes" />

### With Icons

Use `leftSection` and `rightSection` to place an icon beside the label.

<ComponentPreview component="button" example="button-with-icons" />

### As Link

Use the `render` prop to render as a Next.js Link, and set `nativeButton` to `false`.

<ComponentPreview component="button" example="button-with-link" />

## Accessibility

### Label icon-only buttons

An icon-only button has no text for a screen reader to announce. Give it an
`aria-label` describing the action.

```tsx showLineNumbers
<Button size="icon" aria-label="Delete item">
  <TrashIcon />
</Button>
```

### Loading state

The `loading` prop disables the button but keeps it focusable
(`focusableWhenDisabled`), so keyboard users don't lose their place while an
action is in flight.

## API Reference

The Button component is built on top of [Base UI's Button](https://base-ui.com/react/components/button). All Base UI props are supported. The documentation below only covers custom props and modified defaults specific to our implementation.

For the complete Base UI API, see the [Base UI Button documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/button).

### Props

#### Button

Clickable element that triggers actions. Wraps Base UI's `Button`.

<ApiProp
  name="variant"
  fullType='"primary" | "primary-soft" | "neutral" | "secondary" | "outline" | "ghost" | "link" | "destructive" | "destructive-soft"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"primary"'
>
  Visual style variant of the button. The `-soft` variants are tinted-background versions of their solid counterparts, for less-prominent CTAs that still need to read as branded or destructive. Custom prop not available in Base UI.

<ApiProp
  name="size"
  fullType='"xs" | "sm" | "default" | "lg" | "icon" | "icon_xs" | "icon_sm" | "icon_lg"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"default"'
>
  Size of the button. Use icon variants for icon-only buttons with proper square
  dimensions. Custom prop not available in Base UI.

<ApiProp name="loading" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Display loading state with spinner. Automatically disables the button and sets `focusableWhenDisabled` to `true` for keyboard accessibility.

<ApiProp name="leftSection" fullType="ReactNode" simpleType="node">
  Content (typically icon) to display before the button text. Custom prop not available in Base UI.

<ApiProp name="rightSection" fullType="ReactNode" simpleType="node">
  Content (typically icon) to display after the button text. Custom prop not available in Base UI.

---

# card.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/card.mdx

title: Card
description: A versatile container component with header and content areas
type: primitive

import {
  Card,
  CardHeader,
  CardTitle,
  CardDescription,
  CardContent,
  CardFooter,
} from "@/registry/default/card/card";
import { Button } from "@/registry/default/button/button";

The card groups related content on a single surface with optional header, body, and footer regions. Use it for dashboard tiles, list rows, article previews, or any self-contained block that needs its own elevation.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="card" example="card-demo" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="card" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="card" />

## Composition

```text
Card
├── CardHeader
│   ├── CardTitle
│   ├── CardDescription
│   └── CardAction
├── CardContent
└── CardFooter
```

## Examples

### With Footer and Action

Use `CardFooter` for actions below the content and `CardAction` to place a control in the header.

<ComponentPreview component="card" example="card-article" />

### Variants

Use `variant` to change how the card is framed.

<ComponentPreview component="card" example="card-variant" />

| Value     | Description                                                  |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `default` | A single elevated surface, the standard card.               |
| `inset`   | A gray-framed outer with a lifted inner card.               |

## API Reference

The Card is a custom component that does not extend Base UI.

### Props

#### Card

Container component for grouping related content with optional header, body, and footer sections.

<ApiProp
  name="variant"
  fullType='"default" | "inset"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"default"'
>
  Visual style variant of the card.

  - `"default"`: a single elevated surface (the standard card).
  - `"inset"`: a gray-framed outer with a lifted inner card. Reads as "a Default Card wrapped in a tray."

<ApiProp name="level" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="3">
  Surface elevation level for the card. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs. For the `inset` variant, only the outer frame's shadow/rim tracks this prop; the gray-frame bg and the inner card's level are pinned for the visual idiom to hold.

<ApiProp name="shadowLevel" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="1">
  Shadow weight. Defaults to `1`, a flat outlined card (rim only, no drop shadow). Matches the rest of the flat-card family (Table, DataTable, code-block, ComponentPreview).

# combobox.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/combobox.mdx

title: Combobox
description: Searchable dropdown for selecting from a list of options with keyboard navigation
type: primitive

import { Combobox } from "@/registry/default/combobox/combobox";

The combobox is a text input paired with a filtered, keyboard-navigable list of options. Use it for searchable selects, tag pickers, async autocompletes, or any select-from-many flow with more options than a dropdown comfortably holds.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="combobox" example="combobox-basic" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="combobox" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="combobox" />

## Composition

```text
Combobox
├── ComboboxLabel
├── ComboboxInput
└── ComboboxPopup
    ├── ComboboxEmpty
    └── ComboboxList
        ├── ComboboxGroup
        │   ├── ComboboxGroupLabel
        │   └── ComboboxItem
        └── ComboboxItem
```

## Examples

### Creatable

Let users add an option that isn't in the list from their typed input.

<ComponentPreview component="combobox" example="combobox-creatable" />

### Multiple Selection

Pass `multiple` on `Combobox` to select more than one option.

<ComponentPreview component="combobox" example="combobox-multiple" />

### Input Inside Popup

Move `ComboboxInput` inside `ComboboxPopup` so the search field sits in the dropdown.

<ComponentPreview component="combobox" example="combobox-input-inside-popup" />

### Async Search

Load options from a remote source by fetching on input changes. The `useAsyncCombobox` hook handles request cancellation, loading states, and keeps the selected value visible while new results stream in.

<ComponentPreview component="combobox" example="combobox-async" />

### Async Search (Multiple)

Combine async search with `multiple`; selected items stay visible in the dropdown while new matches load.

<ComponentPreview component="combobox" example="combobox-async-multiple" />

### Grouped

Wrap items in `ComboboxGroup` with a `ComboboxGroupLabel` for sticky section headers.

<ComponentPreview component="combobox" example="combobox-grouped" />

### Virtualized

Use `ComboboxVirtualizedList` for large lists (100+ items); it only renders items in the viewport, dramatically reducing DOM nodes.

<ComponentPreview component="combobox" example="combobox-virtualized" />

**Key concepts:**

1. **Use `useListVirtualizer` hook** - Handles scroll positioning, keyboard navigation, and item measurement. See [useListVirtualizer docs](/docs/hooks/use-list-virtualizer) for full API reference.
2. **Use `useComboboxFilteredItems()` inside Root** - Call `useComboboxFilteredItems()` in a child component of `Combobox` to get internally filtered items without manual filtering boilerplate.
3. **Replace `ComboboxList` with `ComboboxVirtualizedList`** - Accepts `scrollRef` and `totalSize` from the hook.
4. **Pass `virtualized` and `items` on Root** - Enables virtualized mode with your full item list.
5. **Use `useHighlightHandler`** - Pass a `virtualizerRef` to the child and use `useHighlightHandler(virtualizerRef)` on Root so keyboard navigation scrolls to the highlighted item.
6. **Override item margins** - Pass `className="mt-0! mb-0!"` to `ComboboxItem` since virtualized items are absolutely positioned and the virtualizer handles padding.

### Elevated Variant

Use `variant="elevated"` on `ComboboxInput` for a Card, Dialog, or popover surface, where the opaque `default` input would collapse into its parent. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs.

<ComponentPreview component="combobox" example="combobox-elevated" />

| Value      | Description                                                       |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `default`  | Opaque `bg-input`, for standard page backgrounds.                |
| `elevated` | Translucent `bg-input-elevated`, for Card, Dialog, or popovers.  |

### Form Integration

Use [Field](/docs/components/field) with `FieldLabel` for labeling. See the [Forms guide](/docs/getting-started/forms) for more patterns.

<ComponentPreview component="combobox" example="combobox-field" />

## API Reference

The Combobox component is built on top of [Base UI's Combobox](https://base-ui.com/react/components/combobox). All Base UI props are supported. The documentation below only covers custom props and modified defaults specific to our implementation.

For the complete Base UI API, see the [Base UI Combobox documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/combobox).

### Props

#### ComboboxInput

Text input with built-in trigger and clear buttons. Wraps Base UI's `Combobox.Input` inside a `Combobox.InputGroup`.

<ApiProp name="showTrigger" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="true">
  Show a chevron trigger button to open the popup.

<ApiProp name="showClear" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="true">
  Show a clear button to reset the input value. Only visible when the input has a value.

<ApiProp name="variant" fullType='"default" | "elevated"' defaultValue='"default"'>
  Surface appearance of the input. `default` uses opaque `bg-input`. `elevated` uses translucent `bg-input-elevated` for use inside Card, Dialog, or popover surfaces. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs.

#### ComboboxTriggerLabel

Accessible label for the input-inside-popup pattern, where the trigger is the form control. Wraps Base UI's `Combobox.Label`. Renders a `<div>`; clicking it focuses the trigger without opening the popup.

For the standard combobox pattern (input outside popup), use `ComboboxLabel` which renders a native `<label>` associated with the input.

#### ComboboxPopup

Dropdown container for the option list with positioning. Composes Base UI's `Combobox.Positioner` and `Combobox.Popup`. Props are forwarded to `Combobox.Popup`.

<ApiProp
  name="sideOffset"
  fullType="number"
  defaultValue="6"
>
  Distance in pixels between the popup and the anchor element. Convenience prop that passes through to the internal Positioner component. Type is inferred from Base UI's Positioner component.

<ApiProp
  name="backdrop"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Show a backdrop overlay behind the popup. Custom prop not available in Base UI.

<ApiProp name="level" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="3">
  Surface elevation level for the popup. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs. Uses `elevatedSurface` (rim on `::after`) so sticky group labels stay below the rim edge.

<ApiProp name="shadowLevel" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="3">
  Shadow weight. Controls drop-shadow intensity independently of substrate color.

#### ComboboxList

Scrollable list of selectable options. Wraps Base UI's `Combobox.Listbox`.

<ApiProp
  name="nativeScroll"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Use native browser scrolling instead of the custom ScrollArea component. Useful for custom layouts where you need more control over scroll behavior, or when nesting the list inside your own scroll container.

<ApiProp
  name="fadeEdges"
  fullType="boolean | 'top' | 'bottom' | 'left' | 'right' | 'x' | 'y' | FadeEdge[]"
  defaultValue="true"
>
  Controls the fade effect on scroll edges. See [ScrollArea](/docs/components/scroll-area#custom-props) for all options.

<ApiProp
  name="scrollbarGutter"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Reserves space for the scrollbar when content overflows, preventing layout shift.

<ApiProp
  name="persistScrollbar"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Always show the scrollbar instead of fading it in on hover or scroll.

<ApiProp
  name="hideScrollbar"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Hides the scrollbar while keeping scroll functionality.

#### ComboboxVirtualizedList

Virtualized scrollable container for large lists. Use with `useListVirtualizer` hook for optimal performance with 100+ items.

<ApiProp
  name="scrollRef"
  fullType="(element: HTMLDivElement | null) => void"
  required
>
  Ref callback from `useListVirtualizer` for the scroll container.

<ApiProp name="totalSize" fullType="number" required>
  Total height of all virtual items in pixels. Provided by `useListVirtualizer`.

<ApiProp
  name="emptyMessage"
  fullType="ReactNode"
  simpleType="node"
  defaultValue='"No results found."'
>
  Message shown when no results are found.

<ApiProp
  name="fadeEdges"
  fullType="boolean | 'x' | 'y' | FadeEdge[]"
  defaultValue='"y"'
>
  Controls the fade effect on scroll edges.

<ApiProp name="nativeScroll" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Use native browser scrolling instead of custom scrollbars. Recommended for
  best virtualization performance.

### Hooks

#### useComboboxFilteredItems

```ts
function useComboboxFilteredItems<T>(): T[];
```

Returns the internally filtered items from the Combobox Root. Must be called inside `Combobox` (Root). Simplifies virtualized implementations by eliminating manual query state, `useDeferredValue`, `useFilter()`, and `useMemo` filtering.

```tsx
import { useComboboxFilteredItems } from "@/registry/default/combobox/combobox";

function VirtualizedListContent() {
  // Must be called inside Combobox root
  const filteredItems = useComboboxFilteredItems<MyItem>();

  const virtualizer = useListVirtualizer({
    items: allItems,
    filteredItems,
  });
  // ...
}
```

<ApiProp name="shadowLevel" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="3">
  Shadow weight. Kept at `3` since submenus are still small popups.

### Additional Props

# dialog.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/dialog.mdx

title: Dialog
description: Modal window that overlays content and requires user interaction
type: primitive

import {
  Dialog,
  DialogContent,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogTrigger,
} from "@/registry/default/dialog/dialog";

A dialog is a modal window that overlays the page and waits for the user to act. Use it for focused tasks like confirming a destructive action, editing a record, or completing a short form without leaving the current view.

## Preview

## Examples

### Non-Modal

Pass `modal={false}` for a floating dialog that keeps the page interactive. The backdrop is hidden, pointer events pass through the empty area around the popup, and outside clicks don't dismiss the dialog.

<ComponentPreview component="dialog" example="dialog-non-modal" />

### Elements Outside Popup

Place elements visually outside the popup card while keeping them inside the popup component for accessibility (tab order, screen reader support). The popup uses `pointer-events: none` so backdrop clicks work, while inner content uses `pointer-events: auto`.

<ComponentPreview component="dialog" example="dialog-elements-outside" />

## API Reference

The Dialog component is built on top of [Base UI's Dialog](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog). All Base UI props are supported. The documentation below only covers custom props and modified defaults specific to our implementation.

For the complete Base UI API, see the [Base UI Dialog documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/dialog).

### Utilities

#### createDialogHandle

Creates a handle that connects a dialog to one or more external `DialogTrigger` components. Useful when the triggers need to live outside the `Dialog`, for example when each row in a list has its own trigger but they all share one dialog.

```tsx
import { createDialogHandle } from "@/registry/default/dialog/dialog";

const handle = createDialogHandle();
```

##### Passing data from the trigger to the dialog

The handle accepts an optional `<Payload>` generic that types a value each trigger can pass along. The dialog reads it through a render-prop child, so you can render different content per trigger without duplicating the dialog markup.

```tsx
type User = { id: string; name: string };

const handle = createDialogHandle<User>();

// Multiple triggers, each with its own payload:
users.map((user) => (
  <DialogTrigger key={user.id} handle={handle} payload={user}>
    Edit {user.name}
  </DialogTrigger>
));

// One shared dialog that renders based on the active trigger:
<Dialog handle={handle}>
  <DialogContent>
    {({ payload: user }) => (
      <DialogHeader>
        <DialogTitle>{user?.name}</DialogTitle>
      </DialogHeader>
    )}
  </DialogContent>
</Dialog>;
```

Without the `<User>` generic, `payload` inside the render prop resolves to `unknown`.

### Props

#### Dialog

Root component. Forwards all props to Base UI's `Dialog.Root`, with modified defaults for the `modal` prop.

<ApiProp
  name="modal"
  fullType='boolean | "trap-focus"'
  simpleType="boolean"
  defaultValue="true"
>
  Behavior is unchanged from Base UI, but when set to `false` or
  `"trap-focus"`, `DialogContent` skips the backdrop and wires
  `pointer-events` so the page remains interactive. Also changes the default
  of `disablePointerDismissal` to `true` so clicks on the page don't close
  the dialog. Pass `disablePointerDismissal={false}` explicitly to opt back
  into outside-click dismissal.

#### DialogContent

Dialog container with centered positioning. Composes `Dialog.Portal`, `Dialog.Viewport`, and `Dialog.Popup`. Also renders `Dialog.Backdrop` when the dialog is modal. Props are forwarded to `Dialog.Popup`.

<ApiProp name="showCloseButton" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="true">
  Show or hide the X close button in the dialog header. Custom prop not
  available in Base UI.

<ApiProp name="variant" fullType='"default" | "inset"' defaultValue='"default"'>
  Visual variant of the dialog. The `inset` variant applies a muted background
  to the footer that extends to the dialog edges.

<ApiProp name="level" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="5">
  Surface elevation level. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs. Dialogs default to `5`, comfortably above popovers and dropdowns at level 3.

<ApiProp name="shadowLevel" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="5">
  Shadow weight. Defaults to `5` for the typical dialog-sized element (~400 to 800px).

#### DialogBody

Scrollable content area within the dialog.

<ApiProp
  name="nativeScroll"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Use native browser scrolling instead of Base UI's ScrollArea. Fade edges still
  work using CSS scroll-driven animations (Chrome 115+, with static fallback).
  Note: `persistScrollbar` is not supported with `nativeScroll`.

<ApiProp
  name="fadeEdges"
  fullType="boolean | 'top' | 'bottom' | 'left' | 'right' | 'x' | 'y' | FadeEdge[]"
  defaultValue="true"
>
  Controls the fade effect on scroll edges. See [ScrollArea](/docs/components/scroll-area#custom-props) for all options.

<ApiProp
  name="scrollbarGutter"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Reserves space for the scrollbar when content overflows, preventing layout shift.

<ApiProp
  name="persistScrollbar"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Always show the scrollbar instead of fading it in on hover or scroll.

<ApiProp
  name="hideScrollbar"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Hides the scrollbar while keeping scroll functionality.

# dropdown-menu.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/dropdown-menu.mdx

title: Dropdown Menu
description: Toggleable menu for displaying lists of links or actions
type: primitive

import { DropdownMenu, DropdownMenuContent, DropdownMenuItem, DropdownMenuTrigger } from "@/registry/default/dropdown-menu/dropdown-menu";

A menu of actions or links that opens from a trigger button. Use it for row actions, a "more options" overflow button, account menus, or any compact list of commands. For a horizontal bar of menus (File, Edit, View), use [Menubar](/docs/components/menubar) instead.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="dropdown-menu" example="dropdown-menu-basic" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="dropdown-menu" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="dropdown-menu" />

## Composition

```text
DropdownMenu
├── DropdownMenuTrigger
└── DropdownMenuContent
    ├── DropdownMenuGroup
    │   ├── DropdownMenuGroupLabel
    │   └── DropdownMenuItem
    ├── DropdownMenuLinkItem
    ├── DropdownMenuLabel
    ├── DropdownMenuCheckboxItem
    ├── DropdownMenuRadioGroup
    │   └── DropdownMenuRadioItem
    ├── DropdownMenuShortcut   (inside an item)
    ├── DropdownMenuSeparator
    └── DropdownMenuSub
        ├── DropdownMenuSubTrigger
        └── DropdownMenuSubContent
```

`DropdownMenuContent` composes the portal, positioner, and popup internally, so you place items directly inside it.

## Examples

### With Icons and Shortcuts

Place an icon beside the label and a `DropdownMenuShortcut` at the end of an item.

<ComponentPreview component="dropdown-menu" example="dropdown-menu-with-icons-and-shortcuts" />

### With Checkboxes

Use `DropdownMenuCheckboxItem` for toggleable options.

<ComponentPreview component="dropdown-menu" example="dropdown-menu-with-checkboxes" />

### With Radio Group

Use `DropdownMenuRadioGroup` with `DropdownMenuRadioItem` for mutually exclusive options.

<ComponentPreview component="dropdown-menu" example="dropdown-menu-with-radio-group" />

### With Sub Menu

Nest a `DropdownMenuSub` to open a submenu on hover.

<ComponentPreview component="dropdown-menu" example="dropdown-menu-with-sub-menu" />

### Animated (Detached Triggers)

Multiple triggers share one menu that moves between them and slides content in or out based on activation direction.

<ComponentPreview component="dropdown-menu" example="dropdown-menu-animated" />

## API Reference

The DropdownMenu component is built on top of [Base UI's Menu](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menu). All Base UI props are supported. The documentation below only covers custom props and modified defaults specific to our implementation.

For the complete Base UI API, see the [Base UI Menu documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menu).

### Props

#### DropdownMenuContent

Dropdown container with positioning and animations. Composes `Menu.Portal`, `Menu.Positioner`, and `Menu.Popup`. Props are forwarded to `Menu.Popup`.

<ApiProp
  name="side"
  fullType='"top" | "right" | "bottom" | "left"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"bottom"'
>
  Which side of the trigger to position the menu. This prop is flattened from
  the Positioner component for convenience.

<ApiProp
  name="align"
  fullType='"start" | "center" | "end"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"center"'
>
  How to align the menu relative to the trigger. This prop is flattened from the
  Positioner component for convenience.

<ApiProp name="sideOffset" fullType="number" defaultValue="4">
  Distance in pixels between trigger and menu. This prop is flattened from the
  Positioner component for convenience.

<ApiProp name="level" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="3">
  Surface elevation level. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs. Bump higher when the menu lives inside an already-elevated parent (e.g., `level={7}` inside a Dialog).

<ApiProp name="shadowLevel" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="3">
  Shadow weight. Controls drop-shadow intensity independently of substrate color.

#### DropdownMenuItem

Individual menu item. Wraps Base UI's `Menu.Item`.

<ApiProp name="inset" fullType="boolean">
  Add left padding to align with items that have icons, creating consistent
  visual alignment.

<ApiProp
  name="variant"
  fullType='"default" | "destructive"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"default"'
>
  Visual style variant. Use `"destructive"` for dangerous actions like delete or
  remove operations.

#### DropdownMenuLinkItem

Menu item that renders as an anchor (`<a>`) for navigation links. Wraps Base UI's `Menu.LinkItem`.

<ApiProp name="inset" fullType="boolean">
  Add left padding to align with items that have icons, creating consistent
  visual alignment.

#### DropdownMenuLabel

Non-interactive label for grouping items.

<ApiProp name="inset" fullType="boolean">
  Add left padding to align with items that have icons, creating consistent
  visual alignment.

#### DropdownMenuGroupLabel

Label for a menu group. Wraps Base UI's `Menu.GroupLabel`.

<ApiProp name="inset" fullType="boolean">
  Add left padding to align with items that have icons, creating consistent
  visual alignment.

#### DropdownMenuSubTrigger

Item that opens a submenu on hover. Wraps Base UI's `Menu.SubmenuTrigger`.

<ApiProp name="inset" fullType="boolean">
  Add left padding to align with items that have icons, creating consistent
  visual alignment.

<ApiProp name="delay" fullType="number" defaultValue="0">
  Delay in milliseconds before opening the submenu on hover.

<ApiProp name="closeDelay" fullType="number" defaultValue="0">
  Delay in milliseconds before closing the submenu when hovering away.

#### DropdownMenuSubContent

Submenu container with positioning. Composes `Menu.Portal`, `Menu.Positioner`, and `Menu.Popup`. Props are forwarded to `Menu.Popup`.

<ApiProp name="sideOffset" fullType="number" defaultValue="0">
  Distance in pixels for positioning the submenu relative to its trigger.

<ApiProp
  name="align"
  fullType='"start" | "center" | "end"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"start"'
>
  How to align the submenu relative to its trigger.

<ApiProp name="alignOffset" fullType="number" defaultValue="-5">
  Vertical offset to align the first submenu item with its trigger. Defaults to
  `-5` when `align` is not `"center"`.

<ApiProp name="level" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="5">
  Surface elevation level. Submenus default to `5` so they pop above the parent dropdown at level 3.

<ApiProp name="shadowLevel" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="3">
  Shadow weight. Kept at `3` (same as parent dropdown), since submenus are still small popups.

---

# field.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/field.mdx

title: Field
description: Form field with automatic label association, validation, and error display
type: primitive

import {
  Field,
  FieldLabel,
  FieldControl,
  FieldDescription,
  FieldError,
  FieldItem,
  FieldValidity,
} from "@/registry/default/field/field";

Wraps a single form control to give it an associated label, a description, and validation messages, all wired together for accessibility automatically. Reach for it around any input, select, checkbox, switch, or radio group that needs a label or error display. To group several fields under one legend, use [Fieldset](/docs/components/fieldset); to wrap and submit the whole form, use [Form](/docs/components/form).

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="field" example="field-demo" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="field" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="field" />

## Composition

```text
Field
├── FieldLabel
├── FieldControl
├── FieldDescription
├── FieldError
│   └── FieldErrorSlot   (optional wrapper)
├── FieldItem            (per option in a checkbox/radio group)
└── FieldValidity        (render prop, no DOM)
```

## Examples

### With Description

Display helper text below the control.

<ComponentPreview component="field" example="field-with-description" />

### Constraint Validation

Use native HTML validation attributes (`required`, `pattern`, `minLength`, `type`, etc.) with a single `FieldError` that displays the browser's native error message.

<ComponentPreview component="field" example="field-validation" />

### Per-State Messages

Customize messages for specific validity states by pairing multiple `FieldError` components with different `match` props. Useful for i18n or overriding the browser's default messages.

<ComponentPreview component="field" example="field-per-state-messages" />

For other ways to customize messages, see [Custom Validation](#custom-validation) (via a `validate` function) and server-side errors via the [Form](/docs/components/form) component's `errors` prop.

### Custom Validation

Run custom validation logic with the `validate` prop. Supports async functions and debouncing.

<ComponentPreview component="field" example="field-custom-validation" />

### With Select

Wrap a Select component with Field for labeling and validation.

<ComponentPreview component="field" example="field-with-select" />

### With Checkbox

Use implicit labeling by placing a Checkbox inside `FieldLabel`.

<ComponentPreview component="field" example="field-with-checkbox" />

### With Switch

Use implicit labeling by placing a Switch inside `FieldLabel`.

<ComponentPreview component="field" example="field-with-switch" />

### With Radio Group

Compose Field with Fieldset and RadioGroup using `FieldItem` for each option.

<ComponentPreview component="field" example="field-with-radio-group" />

### With Checkbox Group

Compose Field with Fieldset and CheckboxGroup using `FieldItem` for each option.

<ComponentPreview component="field" example="field-with-checkbox-group" />

### With Slider

Wrap a Slider component with Field. Use `SliderLabel` (not `FieldLabel`) since Slider is a trigger-based control.

<ComponentPreview component="field" example="field-with-slider" />

### Disabled

Disable the entire field, cascading to all child components.

<ComponentPreview component="field" example="field-disabled" />

### Animating Error Visibility

Wrap `FieldError` in `FieldErrorSlot` to smoothly animate the error's height and opacity on mount/unmount. When empty, the slot collapses to zero space, so there is no extra gap in the layout when no error is present.

<ComponentPreview component="field" example="field-with-error-slot" />

<Callout type="info">
  The height animation relies on CSS `interpolate-size: allow-keywords`, which at the time of writing is only supported in Chromium 129+ (Chrome, Edge, Arc, Brave). Safari and Firefox do not yet support it, so on those browsers the error appears/disappears instantly (opacity still cross-fades). The component still works; only the height tween is degraded.
</Callout>

<Callout type="warn">
  Keep the slot in normal **block** flow. `interpolate-size` animates the slot's height from `0` to `auto`, but flex and grid items have an automatic `min-height: auto` that clamps them to their content's height, so the moment the error mounts the slot jumps straight to full height instead of animating. Don't put `display: flex`/`grid` on the `Field`; if you need to center or lay out the field's contents, wrap the inner controls (e.g. an OTP field) in their own flex container. If the slot genuinely must be a flex/grid item, give it `min-h-0` (`min-height: 0`) to remove the clamp.
</Callout>

## API Reference

The Field component is built on top of [Base UI's Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field). All Base UI props are supported.

For the complete Base UI API, see the [Base UI Field documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/field).

### Props

#### Field

Groups all parts of the field. Renders a `<div>` element.

<ApiProp name="name" fullType="string">
  Identifies the field when a form is submitted.

<ApiProp name="validate" fullType="(value: unknown, formValues: Record<string, any>) => string | string[] | null | Promise<...>">
  Custom validation function. Return a string with the error message if invalid, or `null` if valid. Supports async.

<ApiProp name="validationMode" fullType="'onSubmit' | 'onBlur' | 'onChange'" defaultValue="'onSubmit'">
  When validation is triggered. Takes precedence over the Form's `validationMode`.

<ApiProp name="validationDebounceTime" fullType="number" defaultValue="0">
  Debounce delay in milliseconds for the `validate` function.

<ApiProp name="disabled" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Disables the field and all its children.

<ApiProp name="invalid" fullType="boolean">
  Externally control the invalid state. Useful with third-party form libraries.

<ApiProp name="dirty" fullType="boolean">
  Externally control the dirty state. Useful with third-party form libraries.

<ApiProp name="touched" fullType="boolean">
  Externally control the touched state. Useful with third-party form libraries.

#### FieldLabel

An accessible label automatically associated with the field control. Renders a `<label>` element. Use for input-type controls (Input, NumberField, OTPField, Autocomplete, Combobox) and toggle controls (Checkbox, Radio, Switch). For trigger-based controls like Select, use `SelectLabel` instead.

<ApiProp name="nativeLabel" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="true">
  Whether to render a native `<label>`. Set to `false` when the labeled element is a button (e.g., Select trigger) to avoid inheriting label hover/click behaviors. When `false`, you must also provide a `render` prop with a non-label element (e.g., `render={<div />}`).

#### FieldControl

The form control to label and validate. Renders an `<input>` element. You can omit this and use any Base UI input component directly inside Field instead.

`FieldControl` inherits its visual styling from the [Input](/docs/components/input) component (`inputVariants`). Changes to Input's variant styles propagate to every `FieldControl`, so keep that in mind when customizing either.

#### FieldDescription

A paragraph with additional information about the field. Renders a `<p>` element.

#### FieldError

An error message displayed when the field fails validation. Renders a `<div>` element.

<ApiProp name="match" fullType="boolean | keyof ValidityState">
  Show the error based on a specific validity state (`valueMissing`, `typeMismatch`, `patternMismatch`, `tooShort`, `tooLong`, `rangeUnderflow`, `rangeOverflow`, `stepMismatch`, `badInput`, `customError`). Pass `true` to always show when invalid.

#### FieldErrorSlot

Optional wrapper for `FieldError` that animates the error's height (via `interpolate-size`) and opacity on mount/unmount. When empty, uses a negative top margin to collapse to zero space, so there's no layout difference versus not using a slot at all. When switching between multiple match-specific `FieldError` components, the switch is instant (no cross-fade). Renders a `<div>` element.

Assumes the parent `Field` uses the default `space-y-2` spacing. If you customize the Field's spacing, override the slot's margin classes to match. Keep the slot in block flow: flex/grid items have an automatic `min-height: auto` that clamps the slot to its content height and breaks the `interpolate-size` height tween (the error jumps instead of animating). Don't put `display: flex`/`grid` on the `Field`; if the slot must be a flex/grid item, add `min-h-0` to it.

#### FieldItem

Groups individual items in a checkbox group or radio group with a label and description. Renders a `<div>` element.

#### FieldValidity

Render prop component for custom validity display. Does not render any DOM element.

---

# fieldset.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/fieldset.mdx

title: Fieldset
description: Groups related form fields with a shared legend
type: primitive

import { Fieldset, FieldsetLegend } from "@/registry/default/fieldset/fieldset";

Groups related controls under a shared legend, the way a native `<fieldset>` does. Use it to label a set of radio buttons, checkboxes, or a cluster of inputs that belong together. To label and validate a single control, use [Field](/docs/components/field); to wrap the whole form, use [Form](/docs/components/form).

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="fieldset" example="fieldset-demo" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="fieldset" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="fieldset" />

## Composition

```text
Fieldset
└── FieldsetLegend
```

## Examples

### With Radio Group

Use the `render` prop to merge `Fieldset` onto a `RadioGroup`.

<ComponentPreview component="fieldset" example="fieldset-with-radio-group" />

### With Checkbox Group

Use the `render` prop to merge `Fieldset` onto a `CheckboxGroup`.

<ComponentPreview component="fieldset" example="fieldset-with-checkbox-group" />

## API Reference

The Fieldset component is built on top of [Base UI's Fieldset](https://base-ui.com/react/components/fieldset). All Base UI props are supported.

For the complete Base UI API, see the [Base UI Fieldset documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/fieldset).

### Props

#### Fieldset

Groups a shared legend with related controls. Renders a `<fieldset>` element. Supports the `render` prop for composing with other components like RadioGroup or CheckboxGroup.

#### FieldsetLegend

An accessible label automatically associated with the fieldset. Renders a `<div>` element (not a native `<legend>` to avoid browser styling issues).

# form.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/form.mdx

title: Form
description: Form wrapper with consolidated error handling and validation
type: primitive

import { Form } from "@/registry/default/form/form";

Wraps a native `<form>` and consolidates validation: it collects values from the [Field](/docs/components/field) components inside it, surfaces server-side errors through the `errors` prop, and hands you parsed values via `onFormSubmit`. Use it as the outermost element of any multi-field form. For a single labeled control, [Field](/docs/components/field) alone is enough.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="form" example="form-demo" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="form" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="form" />

## Examples

### Submit as JavaScript Object

Use `onFormSubmit` instead of `onSubmit` to receive form values as a JavaScript object.

<ComponentPreview component="form" example="form-on-form-submit" />

### Constraint Validation

Use native HTML validation attributes (`required`, `pattern`, `minLength`, `type`, `min`, `max`, etc.) with a single `FieldError` that displays the browser's native error message.

<ComponentPreview component="form" example="form-constraint-validation" />

### Server-side Validation

Display errors returned by server-side validation via the `errors` prop.

<ComponentPreview component="form" example="form-server-validation" />

### Server Function with useActionState

Submit with a Server Function using `useActionState` and the `action` prop.

<ComponentPreview component="form" example="form-use-action-state" />

### Zod Validation

Use Zod schemas with `z.flattenError` to map validation errors to fields.

<ComponentPreview component="form" example="form-zod-validation" />

### React Hook Form

Integrate with React Hook Form using `Controller` and Base UI Field's external state props.

<ComponentPreview component="form" example="form-react-hook-form" />

### TanStack Form

Integrate with TanStack Form using `useForm` and `form.Field` render props.

<ComponentPreview component="form" example="form-tanstack-form" />

### Complete Form

Combine multiple field types in one validated form.

<ComponentPreview component="form" example="form-complete" />

## API Reference

The Form component is built on top of [Base UI's Form](https://base-ui.com/react/components/form). All Base UI props are supported.

For the complete Base UI API, see the [Base UI Form documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/form).

### Props

#### Form

A native form element with consolidated error handling. Renders a `<form>` element.

<ApiProp name="onFormSubmit" fullType="(formValues: Record<string, any>, eventDetails: SubmitEventDetails) => void">
  Called when the form is submitted. Receives form values as a JavaScript object. `preventDefault()` is automatically called on the native submit event.

<ApiProp name="errors" fullType="Record<string, string | string[]>">
  Server-side validation errors. Keys correspond to field `name` attributes. Errors are cleared from a field when its value changes.

<ApiProp name="validationMode" fullType="'onSubmit' | 'onBlur' | 'onChange'" defaultValue="'onSubmit'">
  When fields should be validated. Individual fields can override this with their own `validationMode`.

# input.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/input.mdx

title: Input
description: Text input field for user data entry with various states and styling
type: primitive

import { Input } from "@/registry/default/input/input";

A single-line text input for collecting short user data: names, emails, search queries, or any free-form value. For labeling, validation, and error messages, wrap it in [Field](/docs/components/field).

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="input" example="input-demo" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="input" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="input" />

## Examples

### With Label

Pair the input with a `<label>` to describe what it collects.

<ComponentPreview component="input" example="input-with-label" />

### Disabled

Set `disabled` to prevent interaction and dim the input.

<ComponentPreview component="input" example="input-disabled" />

### Elevated Variant

On a Card, Dialog, or popover surface, the opaque `default` input collapses into its parent. Use `variant="elevated"` for a translucent overlay that adapts to the substrate. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs for the full reasoning.

<ComponentPreview component="input" example="input-elevated" />

### Form Integration

Use [Field](/docs/components/field) for labeling, validation, and error display. See the [Forms guide](/docs/getting-started/forms) for more patterns.

<ComponentPreview component="input" example="input-field" />

## API Reference

The Input component is built on top of [Base UI's Input](https://base-ui.com/react/components/input). All Base UI props are supported. The documentation below only covers custom props specific to our implementation.

For the complete Base UI API, see the [Base UI Input documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/input).

### Props

<ApiProp
  name="size"
  fullType="'sm' | 'default'"
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"default"'
>
  Size variant of the input field.

<ApiProp
  name="variant"
  fullType="'default' | 'elevated'"
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"default"'
>
  Surface appearance. `default` uses opaque `bg-input` (clean "lifted card" feel on the page). `elevated` uses translucent `bg-input-elevated`; use this when the input sits inside a Card, Dialog, popover, or any elevated surface where the opaque default would visually collapse into its parent. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs.

# kbd.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/kbd.mdx

title: Kbd
description: Display keyboard shortcuts and key combinations with proper styling
type: primitive

import { Kbd } from "@/registry/default/kbd/kbd";

Kbd renders a keyboard key or shortcut with key-cap styling. Use it in docs, tooltips, command menus, and shortcut lists to show combinations like `⌘ K` or `Ctrl + S`. Pass `keys` to render a combination, and it converts named keys to platform symbols automatically.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="kbd" example="kbd-single-keys" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="kbd" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="kbd" />

## Examples

### Size Variants

Use `size` to set the key's height and text size.

<ComponentPreview component="kbd" example="kbd-size-variants" />

| Size | Description                  |
| ---- | ---------------------------- |
| `sm` | Compact key for dense UI.    |
| `md` | The default key size.        |
| `lg` | Larger key for emphasis.     |

### Color Variants

Use `variant` to set the key's color scheme.

<ComponentPreview component="kbd" example="kbd-color-variants" />

| Variant     | Description                              |
| ----------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| `default`   | Card-colored key with a subtle border.   |
| `primary`   | Solid primary-colored key.               |
| `secondary` | Solid secondary-colored key.             |
| `outline`   | Borderless, transparent key.             |
| `ghost`     | Muted key with no border or shadow.      |
| `danger`    | Destructive-colored key.                 |

### Manual Key Combinations

Compose multiple `Kbd` elements to build a combination by hand.

<ComponentPreview component="kbd" example="kbd-manual-key-combinations" />

### Key Combinations with Props

Use `keys` to render a combination from an array, joined by `separator`.

<ComponentPreview component="kbd" example="kbd-key-combinations-with-props" />

### Special Keys with Auto Conversion

Named keys like `cmd` and `shift` convert to symbols automatically.

<ComponentPreview component="kbd" example="kbd-special-keys-with-auto-conversion" />

### Platform Detection

Use `platform` to force `mac` or `windows` symbols, or leave it `auto` to detect the user's OS.

<ComponentPreview component="kbd" example="kbd-platform-detection" />

### In Context

Place `Kbd` inline within prose to reference a shortcut.

<ComponentPreview component="kbd" example="kbd-in-context" />

### Keyboard Shortcuts List

Pair labels with `Kbd` to document a set of shortcuts.

<ComponentPreview component="kbd" example="kbd-keyboard-shortcuts-list" />

### Live Keyboard Input Detection

Reflect the keys the user is pressing in real time.

<ComponentPreview component="kbd" example="kbd-live-keyboard-input-detection" />

### States

Use `pressed` and `disabled` to show active or unavailable keys.

<ComponentPreview component="kbd" example="kbd-states" />

## API Reference

Kbd is a custom styled `kbd` element. All props are custom or standard `kbd` attributes passed through.

### Props

#### Kbd

Keyboard key or shortcut with key-cap styling.

<ApiProp name="size" fullType='"sm" | "md" | "lg"' simpleType="string" defaultValue='"md"'>
  Height and text size of the key.

<ApiProp
  name="variant"
  fullType='"default" | "primary" | "secondary" | "outline" | "ghost" | "danger"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"default"'
>
  Color scheme of the key.

<ApiProp name="pressed" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Shows the key in a pressed-down state.

<ApiProp name="keys" fullType="string[]" simpleType="array">
  Keys to render as a combination, joined by `separator`. When set, `children` is ignored. Named keys convert to platform symbols.

<ApiProp name="separator" fullType="string" defaultValue='"+"'>
  Symbol placed between keys when rendering a `keys` combination.

<ApiProp name="platform" fullType='"mac" | "windows" | "auto"' simpleType="string" defaultValue='"auto"'>
  Symbol set used for named keys. `"auto"` detects the user's OS.

<ApiProp name="disabled" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Dims the key and sets `aria-disabled` to mark it unavailable.

<ApiProp name="aria-label" fullType="string" simpleType="string">
  Accessible label for the key, useful when the visible content is a symbol.

# label.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/label.mdx

title: Label
description: Text label for form inputs and other interactive elements
type: primitive

A label is the text caption for a form control. Use it to name an input, select, checkbox, or switch, and associate it with `htmlFor` so clicking the label focuses the control.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="label" example="label-demo" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="label" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="label" />

## Accessibility

Set `htmlFor` to the `id` of the control the label names. This lets assistive technology announce the label when the control is focused, and lets users click the label to focus the control.

```tsx showLineNumbers
<Label htmlFor="email">Email</Label>
<input id="email" type="email" />
```

## API Reference

The Label component is a styled native HTML `<label>` element. All standard label attributes are supported.

---

# menubar.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/menubar.mdx

title: Menubar
description: Horizontal menu bar for organizing navigation and actions
type: primitive

import { Menubar, MenubarContent, MenubarItem, MenubarMenu, MenubarTrigger } from "@/registry/default/menubar/menubar";

A horizontal bar of top-level menus, like the File / Edit / View bar in a desktop app. Use it for application-style command surfaces where several menus sit side by side and moving between them keeps the next menu open. For a single menu opened from one button, use [Dropdown Menu](/docs/components/dropdown-menu) instead.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="menubar" example="menubar-basic" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="menubar" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="menubar" />

## Composition

```text
Menubar
└── MenubarMenu          (one per top-level menu)
    ├── MenubarTrigger
    └── MenubarContent
        ├── MenubarGroup
        ├── MenubarLabel
        ├── MenubarItem
        ├── MenubarLinkItem
        ├── MenubarCheckboxItem
        ├── MenubarRadioGroup
        │   └── MenubarRadioItem
        ├── MenubarShortcut   (inside an item)
        ├── MenubarSeparator
        └── MenubarSub
            ├── MenubarSubTrigger
            └── MenubarSubContent
```

## API Reference

The Menubar component is built on top of [Base UI's Menubar](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menubar). All Base UI props are supported. The documentation below only covers custom props and modified defaults specific to our implementation.

For the complete Base UI API, see the [Base UI Menubar documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/menubar).

### Custom Props

#### Menubar

The bar element itself is a subtle inline toolbar that sits visibly elevated above the page.

<ApiProp name="level" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="2">
  Surface elevation level for the bar. Defaults to `2`, a subtle toolbar that lifts gently from the page. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs.

<ApiProp name="shadowLevel" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="2">
  Shadow weight for the bar.

#### MenubarContent

<ApiProp
  name="align"
  fullType='"start" | "center" | "end"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"start"'
>
  How to align the menu. Flattened from Positioner. Base UI defaults to `'center'`.

<ApiProp
  name="alignOffset"
  fullType="number"
  defaultValue="-4"
>
  Offset along alignment axis. Flattened from Positioner.

<ApiProp
  name="sideOffset"
  fullType="number"
  defaultValue="8"
>
  Distance in pixels for positioning. Flattened from Positioner. Base UI defaults to `0`.

<ApiProp name="level" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="3">
  Surface elevation level for the dropdown popup.

<ApiProp name="shadowLevel" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="3">
  Shadow weight for the dropdown popup.

#### MenubarSubContent

<ApiProp name="level" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="5">
  Surface elevation level. Submenus default to `5` so they pop above the parent menu.

<ApiProp name="shadowLevel" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="3">
  Shadow weight. Kept at `3`, since submenus are still small popups.

#### MenubarItem

<ApiProp
  name="inset"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Add left padding to align with items that have icons. Custom prop not available in Base UI.

<ApiProp
  name="variant"
  fullType='"default" | "destructive"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"default"'
>
  Visual style variant for dangerous actions. Custom prop not available in Base UI.

#### MenubarLinkItem

Menu item that renders as an anchor (`<a>`) for navigation links. Wraps Base UI's `Menu.LinkItem`.

<ApiProp
  name="inset"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Add left padding to align with items that have icons. Custom prop not available in Base UI.

#### MenubarLabel

<ApiProp
  name="inset"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Add left padding to align with items that have icons. Custom prop not available in Base UI.

#### MenubarSubTrigger

<ApiProp
  name="inset"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Add left padding to align with items that have icons. Custom prop not available in Base UI.

### Modified Defaults

Our implementation changes the following Base UI prop defaults:

- **MenubarTrigger**: `delay` defaults to `0` (Base UI defaults to `600`)
- **MenubarTrigger**: `closeDelay` defaults to `0`
- **MenubarContent**: `align` defaults to `'start'` (Base UI defaults to `'center'`)
- **MenubarContent**: `alignOffset` defaults to `-4`
- **MenubarContent**: `sideOffset` defaults to `8` (Base UI defaults to `0`)
- **MenubarSubContent**: `sideOffset` defaults to `8`

---

# meter.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/meter.mdx

title: Meter
description: Display scalar measurements within a known range with visual indicators
type: primitive

import { Meter } from "@/registry/default/meter/meter";

A meter displays a scalar measurement within a known range, with optional thresholds that color the indicator by status. Use it for static readings like disk usage, battery level, or a score; for the changing completion of a task, use [`Progress`](/docs/components/progress) instead.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="meter" example="meter-basic" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="meter" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="meter" />

## Composition

```text
MeterRoot
├── MeterLabel
├── MeterValue
└── MeterTrack
    └── MeterIndicator
```

## Examples

### Different Sizes

Use `size` to set the track height and text size.

<ComponentPreview component="meter" example="meter-different-sizes" />

| Value | Description                       |
| ----- | --------------------------------- |
| `sm`  | Thin track with extra-small text. |
| `md`  | The default track and text.       |
| `lg`  | Thick track with larger text.     |

### With Labels

Add `MeterLabel` and `MeterValue` to caption the meter.

<ComponentPreview component="meter" example="meter-with-labels" />

### With Min and Max

Set `min` and `max` to scale the value to a custom range.

<ComponentPreview component="meter" example="meter-with-min-max" />

### With Optimum Range

Set `optimumMin` and `optimumMax` to mark the ideal range with tick markers.

<ComponentPreview component="meter" example="meter-with-optimum-range" />

### With Thresholds

Set `low` and `high` to color the indicator by status as the value crosses each threshold.

<ComponentPreview component="meter" example="meter-with-thresholds" />

### With Segments

Set `segments` on `MeterTrack` to divide the track into discrete blocks.

<ComponentPreview component="meter" example="meter-with-segments" />

## API Reference

The Meter component is built on top of [Base UI's Meter](https://base-ui.com/react/components/meter). All Base UI props are supported. The documentation below only covers custom props and modified defaults specific to our implementation.

For the complete Base UI API, see the [Base UI Meter documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/meter).

### Custom Props

#### MeterRoot

<ApiProp name="animated" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Custom prop not available in Base UI. Enable progress animations for the
  meter indicator.

<ApiProp name="size" fullType='"sm" | "md" | "lg"' simpleType="string" defaultValue='"md"'>
  Custom prop not available in Base UI. Size variant for the meter component.

<ApiProp name="low" fullType="number">
  Low threshold value. Values below this threshold are considered low and may
  trigger visual indicators.

<ApiProp name="high" fullType="number">
  High threshold value. Values above this threshold are considered high and may
  trigger visual indicators.

<ApiProp name="optimumMin" fullType="number">
  Optimum range minimum value. Defines the lower bound of the optimal value
  range.

<ApiProp name="optimumMax" fullType="number">
  Optimum range maximum value. Defines the upper bound of the optimal value
  range.

<ApiProp name="showOptimumMarkers" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="true">
  Custom prop not available in Base UI. Whether to show visual markers for the
  optimum range.

<ApiProp name="showThresholdColors" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="true">
  Custom prop not available in Base UI. Whether to apply threshold-based colors
  to the meter indicator.

#### MeterTrack

<ApiProp name="segments" fullType="number">
  Custom prop not available in Base UI. Number of segments to divide the track
  into for a segmented appearance.

<ApiProp name="striped" fullType="boolean">
  Custom prop not available in Base UI. Apply a striped background pattern to
  the track.

<ApiProp name="gradient" fullType="boolean">
  Custom prop not available in Base UI. Apply a gradient background to the
  track.

# navigation-menu.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/navigation-menu.mdx

title: Navigation Menu
description: Accessible dropdown navigation menu with support for nested submenus
type: primitive

import { NavigationMenu, NavigationMenuContent, NavigationMenuItem, NavigationMenuList, NavigationMenuTrigger } from "@/registry/default/navigation-menu/navigation-menu";

A navigation menu is a horizontal bar of links and dropdown panels for site-level navigation, with support for nested submenus. Use it for a primary site header; for a single dropdown of actions tied to a button, use [`DropdownMenu`](/docs/components/dropdown-menu) instead.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="navigation-menu" example="navigation-menu-basic" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="navigation-menu" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="navigation-menu" />

## Composition

```text
NavigationMenu
└── NavigationMenuList
    └── NavigationMenuItem
        ├── NavigationMenuTrigger
        │   └── NavigationMenuIcon
        ├── NavigationMenuContent
        │   └── NavigationMenuLink
        └── NavigationMenuSub
            ├── NavigationMenuSubTrigger
            └── NavigationMenuContent
```

`NavigationMenu` composes the viewport internally. Use `NavigationMenuLink` with `standalone` for top-level links that have no dropdown.

## Examples

### With Direct Links

Set `standalone` on `NavigationMenuLink` to mix plain links in with the dropdowns.

<ComponentPreview component="navigation-menu" example="navigation-menu-with-direct-links" />

### Nested Submenus

Use `NavigationMenuSub` inside a `NavigationMenuContent` to build multi-level menus.

<ComponentPreview component="navigation-menu" example="navigation-menu-nested-submenus" />

### Custom Styled Dropdown

Pass a `className` to `NavigationMenuContent` to restyle a dropdown panel.

<ComponentPreview component="navigation-menu" example="navigation-menu-custom-styled-dropdown" />

### With Next.js Link

Use the `render` prop on `NavigationMenuLink` to route through a Next.js Link.

<ComponentPreview component="navigation-menu" example="navigation-menu-flexible-nextjs-link" />

## API Reference

The Navigation Menu component is built on top of [Base UI's Navigation Menu](https://base-ui.com/react/components/navigation-menu). All Base UI props are supported. The documentation below only covers custom props and modified defaults specific to our implementation.

For the complete Base UI API, see the [Base UI Navigation Menu documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/navigation-menu).

### Props

#### NavigationMenu

Root navigation menu container. Composes `NavigationMenu.Root` with an internal viewport. Props are forwarded to `NavigationMenu.Root`.

<ApiProp name="sideOffset" fullType="number" defaultValue="10">
  Distance between the trigger and the popup. Base UI defaults to `0`.

<ApiProp name="collisionPadding" fullType="number | Padding" defaultValue="{ top: 5, bottom: 5, left: 20, right: 20 }">
  Space between the popup and viewport edges.

<ApiProp name="side" fullType='"top" | "bottom" | "left" | "right"'>
  Preferred side for the popup to appear.

<ApiProp name="align" fullType='"start" | "center" | "end"'>
  Alignment of the popup relative to the trigger.

<ApiProp name="alignOffset" fullType="number">
  Offset from the aligned edge.

<ApiProp name="collisionBoundary" fullType="Element | Element[]">
  Element(s) to use as collision boundaries.

<ApiProp name="arrow" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Shows an arrow pointing to the trigger.

<ApiProp name="level" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="2">
  Surface elevation level for the bar itself. Defaults to `2`, a subtle toolbar that sits visibly above the page. The Viewport and Sub popups have their levels (3 and 5) baked in. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs.

<ApiProp name="shadowLevel" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="2">
  Shadow weight for the bar.

#### NavigationMenuLink

Navigation link element. Wraps `NavigationMenu.Link`.

<ApiProp name="standalone" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Applies trigger button styling to make the link appear as a top-level navigation item.

#### NavigationMenuSub

Nested submenu container for multi-level navigation. Composes `NavigationMenu.Root` with internal positioning. Props are forwarded to `NavigationMenu.Root`.

<ApiProp name="side" fullType='"top" | "bottom" | "left" | "right"' defaultValue='"right"'>
  Preferred side for the submenu to appear.

<ApiProp name="sideOffset" fullType="number" defaultValue="24">
  Distance between the trigger and the submenu. Base UI defaults to `0`.

<ApiProp name="align" fullType='"start" | "center" | "end"' defaultValue='"end"'>
  Alignment of the submenu relative to the trigger.

<ApiProp name="alignOffset" fullType="number" defaultValue="-24">
  Offset from the aligned edge.

<ApiProp name="arrow" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Shows an arrow pointing to the trigger.

<ApiProp name="orientation" fullType='"horizontal" | "vertical"' defaultValue='"vertical"'>
  Navigation orientation. Base UI defaults to `"horizontal"`.

# number-field.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/number-field.mdx

title: Number Field
description: Numeric input with increment and decrement buttons and optional scrub area
type: primitive

import {
  NumberField,
  NumberFieldGroup,
  NumberFieldInput,
  NumberFieldIncrement,
  NumberFieldDecrement,
  NumberFieldStepper,
  NumberFieldScrubArea,
  NumberFieldScrubAreaCursor,
} from "@/registry/default/number-field/number-field";

A number field is a numeric input with increment and decrement buttons and an optional scrub area for dragging the value. Use it for bounded, steppable quantities like counts, prices, or percentages, where the value should stay numeric.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="number-field" example="number-field-demo" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="number-field" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="number-field" />

## Composition

```text
NumberField
└── NumberFieldGroup
    ├── NumberFieldDecrement
    ├── NumberFieldInput
    ├── NumberFieldIncrement
    ├── NumberFieldStepper
    └── NumberFieldScrubArea
        └── NumberFieldScrubAreaCursor
```

`NumberFieldStepper` is an alternative to the separate `NumberFieldDecrement` / `NumberFieldIncrement`, stacking both on the right edge.

## Examples

### Controlled

Use `value` and `onValueChange` on `NumberField` to drive the value yourself.

<ComponentPreview component="number-field" example="number-field-controlled" />

### Min / Max

Set `min` and `max` on `NumberField` to constrain the value to a range.

<ComponentPreview component="number-field" example="number-field-min-max" />

### Formatted Display

Pass `format` (an `Intl.NumberFormat` options object) to display the value as currency, a percentage, or another number format.

<ComponentPreview component="number-field" example="number-field-format" />

### Stacked steppers

Use `NumberFieldStepper` for a vertically-stacked increment/decrement cluster on the right, the styled equivalent of a native number spinner. The group detects the stepper and caps the input's left edge automatically.

<ComponentPreview component="number-field" example="number-field-stacked" />

### Scrub Area

Wrap a label in `NumberFieldScrubArea` to let the user drag horizontally to change the value.

<ComponentPreview component="number-field" example="number-field-scrub-area" />

### Disabled

Set `disabled` on `NumberField` to prevent interaction.

<ComponentPreview component="number-field" example="number-field-disabled" />

### Elevated Variant

On a Card, Dialog, or popover surface, the opaque `default` group collapses into its parent. Use `variant="elevated"` on `NumberFieldGroup` for a translucent overlay that adapts to the substrate. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs.

<ComponentPreview component="number-field" example="number-field-elevated" />

| Variant    | Description                                                  |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `default`  | Opaque `bg-input` group for page-level surfaces.            |
| `elevated` | Translucent group for use inside Card, Dialog, or popover.  |

### Form Integration

Use [Field](/docs/components/field) for labeling and form participation. See the [Forms guide](/docs/getting-started/forms) for more patterns.

<ComponentPreview component="number-field" example="number-field-field" />

## API Reference

The Number Field component is built on top of [Base UI's Number Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/number-field). All Base UI props are supported. The documentation below only covers the sub-components available.

For the complete Base UI API, see the [Base UI Number Field documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/number-field).

### Sub-components

#### NumberField

Groups all parts and manages state. Renders a `<div>` element. Accepts `defaultValue`, `value`, `onValueChange`, `min`, `max`, `step`, `format`, `name`, `required`, `disabled`, `readOnly`, and all other Base UI Number Field Root props.

#### NumberFieldGroup

Groups the input with increment and decrement buttons. Renders a `<div>` element. The group carries the field's surface (background, shadow, border) so the `[-][input][+]` cluster reads as a single lifted element.

<ApiProp
  name="variant"
  fullType='"default" | "elevated"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"default"'
>
  Surface appearance of the group. `default` uses opaque `bg-input` + soft `shadow-input` in light mode. `elevated` uses translucent `bg-input-elevated` for use inside Card, Dialog, or popover surfaces. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs.

#### NumberFieldInput

The numeric input control. Renders an `<input>` element. Inherits its surface from `NumberFieldGroup`, with no `variant` prop of its own.

#### NumberFieldIncrement

Button that increases the value when clicked. Renders a `<button>` element.

#### NumberFieldDecrement

Button that decreases the value when clicked. Renders a `<button>` element.

#### NumberFieldStepper

A vertically-stacked increment (top) and decrement (bottom) cluster for the group's right edge, with built-in chevron icons. Renders a `<div>` wrapping Base UI's `Increment` and `Decrement`. `NumberFieldGroup` detects it and rounds/borders the input's left edge automatically.

#### NumberFieldScrubArea

An interactive area where the user can click and drag to change the value. Renders a `<span>` element.

#### NumberFieldScrubAreaCursor

A custom cursor element displayed while scrubbing. Renders a `<span>` element.

---

# otp-field.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/otp-field.mdx

title: OTP Field
description: One-time password input with individual character slots, powered by Base UI
type: primitive

import {
  OTPField,
  OTPFieldInput,
  OTPFieldSeparator,
  OTPFieldGroup,
} from "@/registry/default/otp-field/otp-field";

An OTP field splits a one-time passcode across individual character slots, with paste and auto-advance handled for you. Use it for two-factor codes, email verification, or recovery codes.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="otp-field" example="otp-field-basic" />

## Installation

## Usage

## Composition

```text
OTPField
└── OTPFieldGroup
    ├── OTPFieldInput
    └── OTPFieldSeparator
```

## Examples

### Alphanumeric

Set `validationType="alphanumeric"` to accept letters and numbers for recovery or backup codes.

<ComponentPreview component="otp-field" example="otp-field-alphanumeric" />

### Grouped

Wrap inputs in `OTPFieldGroup` and place an `OTPFieldSeparator` between groups.

<ComponentPreview component="otp-field" example="otp-field-grouped" />

### Placeholder Hints

Set `placeholder` on each `OTPFieldInput` to show a hint that hides when the slot is focused.

<ComponentPreview component="otp-field" example="otp-field-placeholder" />

### Custom Sanitization

Restrict input to specific characters, with shake feedback on invalid input via the bundled `useInvalidFeedback` hook.

Set `mask` on `OTPField` to obscure entered characters for shared screens.
