### Elevated Variant

On a Card, Dialog, or popover surface, the opaque `default` slots collapse into the parent. Use `variant="elevated"` on each `OTPFieldInput` for a translucent overlay that adapts to the substrate. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs.

<ComponentPreview component="otp-field" example="otp-field-elevated" />

| Variant    | Description                                                 |
| ---------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- |
| `default`  | Opaque `bg-input` slots for page-level surfaces.           |
| `elevated` | Translucent slots for use inside Card, Dialog, or popover. |

### Form Integration

Use [Field](/docs/components/field) for labeling and form participation. See the [Forms guide](/docs/getting-started/forms) for more patterns.

<ComponentPreview component="otp-field" example="otp-field-field" />

## API Reference

The OTP Field is built on top of [Base UI's OTP Field](https://base-ui.com/react/components/otp-field). All Base UI props are supported. The documentation below only covers custom props and modified defaults specific to our implementation.

For the complete Base UI API, see the [Base UI OTP Field documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/otp-field).

### Props

#### OTPField

Groups all OTP field parts and manages their state. Wraps Base UI's `OTPField.Root`. Renders a `<div>`.

No custom props. All Base UI Root props are passed through, including `length`, `value`, `onValueChange`, `validationType`, `mask`, `normalizeValue`, and `onValueInvalid`.

#### OTPFieldInput

Individual character input slot. Wraps Base UI's `OTPField.Input`. Renders an `<input>`.

<ApiProp
  name="variant"
  fullType='"default" | "elevated"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"default"'
>
  Surface appearance of the slot. `default` uses opaque `bg-input`. `elevated` uses translucent `bg-input-elevated` for use inside Card, Dialog, or popover surfaces. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs.

#### OTPFieldSeparator

Visual separator between input groups. Wraps Base UI's `Separator`. Renders a `<div>`.

<ApiProp name="children" fullType="ReactNode" simpleType="node">
  Content to render inside the separator. Defaults to a horizontal dash icon when no children are provided.

#### OTPFieldGroup

Layout wrapper for grouping inputs together. Not a Base UI component; renders a plain `<div>` with `display: flex` and `gap`.

### Hooks

#### useInvalidFeedback

```ts
function useInvalidFeedback(options?: UseInvalidFeedbackOptions): UseInvalidFeedbackReturn;
```

Manages shake animation and screen reader feedback for invalid OTP input. Bundled with the component, installed automatically when you install `otp-field`.

Wire its handlers to `OTPField` and its className getter to each `OTPFieldInput`:

```tsx
import { useInvalidFeedback } from "@/components/ui/cubby-ui/otp-field/hooks/use-invalid-feedback";

const invalidFeedback = useInvalidFeedback();

<OTPField
  length={6}
  validationType="none"
  normalizeValue={myCustomNormalizer}
  onValueChange={invalidFeedback.handleValueChange}
  onValueInvalid={invalidFeedback.handleValueInvalid}
>
  {Array.from({ length: 6 }, (_, index) => (
    <OTPFieldInput
      key={index}
      className={invalidFeedback.getInvalidClassName(index)}
      onFocus={() => invalidFeedback.setFocusedIndex(index)}
    />
  ))}
</OTPField>
<span aria-live="polite" className="sr-only">
  {invalidFeedback.statusMessage}
</span>
```

##### Options

<ApiProp name="duration" fullType="number" defaultValue="400">
  Duration in milliseconds before the shake animation clears.

##### Returns

| Property | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `handleValueChange` | `() => void` | Clears invalid feedback. Wire to `OTPField`'s `onValueChange`. |
| `handleValueInvalid` | `(value: string) => void` | Triggers shake animation and status message. Wire to `OTPField`'s `onValueInvalid`. |
| `getInvalidClassName` | `(index: number) => string \| undefined` | Returns the shake animation className for the active invalid slot, or `undefined`. |
| `setFocusedIndex` | `(index: number) => void` | Tracks which slot is focused. Wire to each input's `onFocus`. |
| `statusMessage` | `string` | Screen reader announcement. Render inside an `aria-live="polite"` region. |

---

# popover.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/popover.mdx

title: Popover
description: Floating content that appears relative to a trigger element
type: primitive

import { Popover, PopoverContent, PopoverTrigger } from "@/registry/default/popover/popover";

A popover floats rich, interactive content next to a trigger. Use it for notification panels, quick forms, or detail cards; for a plain hover label, use [`Tooltip`](/docs/components/tooltip), and for picking from a list bound to a form field, use [`Select`](/docs/components/select).

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="popover" example="popover-demo" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="popover" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="popover" />

## Composition

```text
Popover
├── PopoverTrigger
└── PopoverContent
    ├── PopoverTitle
    └── PopoverDescription
```

`PopoverContent` composes the portal, positioner, popup, viewport, and optional arrow internally, so you place your content directly inside it.

## Examples

### Hover Trigger

Set `openOnHover` on `Popover` to open on hover instead of click.

<ComponentPreview component="popover" example="popover-hover" />

### With Backdrop

Render `PopoverBackdrop` for a dimmed overlay behind the open popover.

<ComponentPreview component="popover" example="popover-with-backdrop" />

### Detached Trigger

Use `createPopoverHandle()` to link a trigger outside the `Popover` component.

<ComponentPreview component="popover" example="popover-detached-trigger" />

### Animated Transitions

Animate the popover's position, size, and content when switching between multiple triggers with different payloads.

<ComponentPreview component="popover" example="popover-animated" />

### Controlled

Control the popover's open state externally using the `open` and `onOpenChange` props.

<ComponentPreview component="popover" example="popover-controlled" />

## API Reference

The Popover component is built on top of [Base UI's Popover](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover). All Base UI props are supported. The documentation below only covers custom props and modified defaults specific to our implementation.

For the complete Base UI API, see the [Base UI Popover documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/popover).

### Utilities

#### createPopoverHandle

Creates a handle that connects a popover to one or more external `PopoverTrigger` components. Useful when the triggers need to live outside the `Popover`, for example when each row in a list has its own trigger but they all share one popover.

```tsx
import { createPopoverHandle } from "@/registry/default/popover/popover";

const handle = createPopoverHandle();
```

##### Passing data from the trigger to the popover

The handle accepts an optional `<Payload>` generic that types a value each trigger can pass along. The popover reads it through a render-prop child, so you can render different content per trigger without duplicating the popover markup.

```tsx
type User = { id: string; name: string };

const handle = createPopoverHandle<User>();

// Multiple triggers, each with its own payload:
users.map((user) => (
  <PopoverTrigger key={user.id} handle={handle} payload={user}>
    {user.name}
  </PopoverTrigger>
));

// One shared popover that renders based on the active trigger:
<Popover handle={handle}>
  <PopoverContent>
    {({ payload: user }) => <p>{user?.name}</p>}
  </PopoverContent>
</Popover>;
```

Without the `<User>` generic, `payload` inside the render prop resolves to `unknown`.

### Props

#### PopoverContent

Composed component for common popover layouts. Combines `Popover.Portal`, `Popover.Positioner`, `Popover.Popup`, and `Popover.Viewport`. Optionally renders `Popover.Arrow`. Props are forwarded to the Positioner and Popup components.

<ApiProp
  name="arrow"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Show or hide the popover arrow pointing to the trigger. Custom prop not available in Base UI.

<ApiProp
  name="side"
  fullType="'top' | 'right' | 'bottom' | 'left' | 'inline-start' | 'inline-end'"
  defaultValue='"bottom"'
>
  Which side of the trigger to position the popover. Flattened from Positioner.

<ApiProp
  name="align"
  fullType="'start' | 'center' | 'end'"
  defaultValue='"center"'
>
  How to align the popover relative to the trigger. Flattened from Positioner.

<ApiProp
  name="sideOffset"
  fullType="number"
  defaultValue="8"
>
  Distance in pixels between trigger and popover. Flattened from Positioner. Base UI defaults to `0`.

<ApiProp
  name="alignOffset"
  fullType="number"
  defaultValue="0"
>
  Offset along the alignment axis. Flattened from Positioner.

<ApiProp
  name="collisionBoundary"
  fullType="Element | Element[] | 'clipping-ancestors'"
>
  Boundary for collision detection. Flattened from Positioner.

<ApiProp
  name="collisionPadding"
  fullType="number | Partial<Record<Side, number>>"
  defaultValue="10"
>
  Padding from collision boundary. Flattened from Positioner. Base UI defaults to `5`.

<ApiProp
  name="sticky"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Whether to keep the popover visible in the viewport after the trigger has scrolled out of view. Flattened from Positioner.

<ApiProp
  name="positionMethod"
  fullType="'absolute' | 'fixed'"
  defaultValue='"absolute"'
>
  CSS position method. Flattened from Positioner.

<ApiProp
  name="arrowPadding"
  fullType="number"
>
  Minimum padding between arrow and popover edges. Flattened from Positioner. Base UI defaults to `5`.

<ApiProp
  name="container"
  fullType="HTMLElement | undefined"
>
  Portal container element. Flattened from Portal.

<ApiProp
  name="level"
  fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8"
  defaultValue="3"
>
  Surface elevation level. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs. Bump higher when this popover lives inside an already-elevated parent (e.g., `level={7}` when nested inside a Dialog).

<ApiProp
  name="shadowLevel"
  fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8"
  defaultValue="3"
>
  Shadow weight. Controls drop-shadow intensity independently of substrate color.

import { PreviewCard } from "@/registry/default/preview-card/preview-card";

A preview card reveals a floating panel of supplementary content when the user hovers or focuses a trigger. Use it for link previews, profile cards, or any rich hover tooltip; for plain text on hover, use [`Tooltip`](/docs/components/tooltip) instead.


## API Reference

The PreviewCard component is built on top of [Base UI's PreviewCard](https://base-ui.com/react/components/preview-card). All Base UI props are supported. The documentation below only covers custom props and modified defaults specific to our implementation.

For the complete Base UI API, see the [Base UI PreviewCard documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/preview-card).

### Custom Props

#### PreviewCardContent

<ApiProp name="arrow" fullType="boolean" simpleType="boolean" defaultValue="true">
  Show or hide the arrow pointing to the trigger. Custom prop not available in Base UI.

<ApiProp name="align" fullType='"start" | "center" | "end"' simpleType="string">
  How to align the preview card. Flattened from Positioner for convenience.

<ApiProp name="sideOffset" fullType="number" simpleType="number">
  Distance in pixels for positioning. Flattened from Positioner for convenience.

### Modified Defaults

Our implementation changes the following Base UI prop defaults:

- **PreviewCardTrigger**: `delay` defaults to `0` (Base UI defaults to `600`)
- **PreviewCardTrigger**: `closeDelay` defaults to `0` (Base UI defaults to `300`)
- **PreviewCardContent**: `align` defaults to `"center"` (Base UI defaults to `"start"`)
- **PreviewCardContent**: `sideOffset` defaults to `8` (Base UI defaults to `0`)

# scroll-area.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/scroll-area.mdx

title: Scroll Area
description: Custom scrollable container with styled scrollbars
type: primitive

import { ScrollArea } from "@/registry/default/scroll-area/scroll-area";

The scroll area is a container with custom-styled scrollbars and optional edge fades. Use it for any overflowing region, like a sidebar, a chat log, or a long form, where the native scrollbar would look out of place.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="scroll-area" example="scroll-area-vertical-scroll" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="scroll-area" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="scroll-area" />

## Examples

### Fade Edges

Use `fadeEdges` to add a CSS-mask fade at the edges that appears only where content is scrollable.

<ComponentPreview component="scroll-area" example="scroll-area-scroll-fade" />

The fade depth defaults to `min(12%, 2.5rem)`, 12% of the container capped at `2.5rem` so tall scrollers stay subtle. Tune it per instance by setting the `--scroll-fade-size` CSS variable on `viewportClassName`:

```tsx
<ScrollArea fadeEdges viewportClassName="[--scroll-fade-size:2rem]" />
```

With `nativeScroll`, the fade eases in and out over a fixed scroll distance (`6rem` by default, clamped to the scroll range so short scrollers still fully reveal). Adjust it with `--scroll-fade-reveal`:

```tsx
<ScrollArea fadeEdges nativeScroll viewportClassName="[--scroll-fade-reveal:4rem]" />
```

### Native Scroll Fade

Add `nativeScroll` to drive the fade with CSS scroll-driven animations instead of Base UI's measured overflow, falling back to a static fade where unsupported.

<ComponentPreview component="scroll-area" example="scroll-area-native-fade" />

### Scroll Fade Without the Component

The same edge fade ships as a standalone CSS utility you can drop on any element with `overflow`, for scroll containers you didn't render with `ScrollArea` such as a code block, a table wrapper, or a third-party list. See [Scroll Fade](/docs/utils/scroll-fade).

### Scrollbar Gutter

Use `scrollbarGutter` to reserve space for the scrollbar so it doesn't shift the layout when it appears.

<ComponentPreview component="scroll-area" example="scroll-area-scrollbar-gutter" />

### Persistent Scrollbar

Use `persistScrollbar` to always show the scrollbar instead of fading it in on hover or scroll.

<ComponentPreview component="scroll-area" example="scroll-area-persist-scrollbar" />

### Horizontal Scroll

Let wide content scroll sideways instead of wrapping.

<ComponentPreview component="scroll-area" example="scroll-area-horizontal-scroll" />

### Both Scrollbars

When content overflows in both directions, both scrollbars appear automatically and the corner keeps them from intersecting.

<ComponentPreview component="scroll-area" example="scroll-area-both-scrollbars" />

## API Reference

The ScrollArea component is built on top of [Base UI's ScrollArea](https://base-ui.com/react/components/scroll-area). All Base UI props are supported. The documentation below only covers custom props and modified defaults specific to our implementation.

For the complete Base UI API, see the [Base UI ScrollArea documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/scroll-area).

### Props

#### ScrollArea

Container with styled scrollbars and optional fade effects. Wraps Base UI's `ScrollArea.Root`.

<ApiProp name="fadeEdges" fullType="boolean | 'top' | 'bottom' | 'left' | 'right' | 'x' | 'y' | FadeEdge[]" defaultValue="false">
  Adds a subtle fade effect at the scroll edges using CSS masks. The fade
  appears when content is scrollable in that direction and disappears at
  boundaries. Works over any background color or pattern.

  - `true` - fade all edges
  - `"y"` - fade top and bottom
  - `"x"` - fade left and right
  - `"top"`, `"bottom"`, `"left"`, `"right"` - fade specific edge
  - `["top", "left"]` - fade multiple specific edges

<ApiProp name="scrollbarGutter" fullType="boolean" simpleType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Reserves space for the scrollbar when content overflows. This prevents layout
  shift when the scrollbar appears or disappears.

<ApiProp name="persistScrollbar" fullType="boolean" simpleType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Always show the scrollbar instead of fading it in on hover or scroll. Useful
  for interfaces where constant scroll position awareness is needed.

<ApiProp name="hideScrollbar" fullType="boolean" simpleType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Hides the scrollbar while keeping scroll functionality. Useful for carousels,
  touch-first UIs, or when using custom scroll indicators. Cannot be used with
  `persistScrollbar`.

<ApiProp name="nativeScroll" fullType="boolean" simpleType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Uses native browser scrolling instead of Base UI's ScrollArea. The scrollbar
  is styled to match using CSS, and fade edges use CSS scroll-driven animations
  (Chrome 115+, with static fallback for other browsers). Useful when you need
  native scroll behavior or want to avoid Base UI's overhead.

  Note: `persistScrollbar` is not supported with `nativeScroll`. With `nativeScroll`,
  `scrollbarGutter` always reserves space (CSS `scrollbar-gutter: stable`), while the
  default only reserves space when content overflows.

<ApiProp name="overscrollBehavior" fullType="'auto' | 'contain' | 'none'" defaultValue="contain">
  Controls the scroll chaining behavior when reaching the scroll boundary.

  - `"auto"` - default browser behavior, scroll chains to parent containers
  - `"contain"` - prevents scroll chaining to parent containers
  - `"none"` - prevents scroll chaining and disables bounce/rubber-band effects

---

# select.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/select.mdx

title: Select
description: Dropdown selection control for choosing from a list of options
type: primitive

import {
  Select,
  SelectContent,
  SelectItem,
  SelectTrigger,
  SelectValue,
} from "@/registry/default/select/select";

A select lets the user pick one option (or several) from a list bound to a form field. Use it for a known, finite set of choices; for a searchable list of actions or a command palette, use [`Command`](/docs/components/command) instead.

## Preview

```text
├── SelectLabel

    └── SelectGroup
        ├── SelectGroupLabel
        ├── SelectItem
        └── SelectSeparator
```

<ComponentPreview component="select" example="select-elevated" />

| Variant    | Description                                                  |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |

| `elevated` | Translucent trigger for use inside Card, Dialog, or popover. |

### Form Integration

Use [Field](/docs/components/field) with `SelectLabel` for labeling. See the [Forms guide](/docs/getting-started/forms) for more patterns.

<ComponentPreview component="select" example="select-field" />

## API Reference

The Select component is built on top of [Base UI's Select](https://base-ui.com/react/components/select). All Base UI props are supported. The documentation below only covers custom props and modified defaults specific to our implementation.

For the complete Base UI API, see the [Base UI Select documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/select).

### Props

#### SelectLabel

Accessible label for the select trigger. Wraps Base UI's `Select.Label`. Renders a `<div>`: clicking it focuses the trigger without opening the popup.

#### SelectTrigger

Button that opens the dropdown when clicked. Wraps Base UI's `Select.Trigger`.

<ApiProp
  name="size"
  fullType="'sm' | 'default'"
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"default"'
>
  Size variant of the trigger button.

<ApiProp
  name="variant"
  fullType="'default' | 'elevated'"
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"default"'
>
  Surface appearance. `default` uses opaque `bg-input` with a soft drop shadow in light mode. `elevated` uses translucent `bg-input-elevated` for use inside Card, Dialog, or popover surfaces. Matches the same prop on Input, Combobox, and Autocomplete. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs.

<ApiProp name="hideChevronRotation" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Disable the chevron rotation animation when the select opens.

#### SelectContent

Dropdown container for the option list with positioning. Composes Base UI's `Select.Positioner` and `Select.Popup`. Props are forwarded to `Select.Popup`.

<ApiProp
  name="size"
  fullType="'sm' | 'default'"
  simpleType="string"
>
  Size variant for the popup items. Should match the trigger's size when using
  `alignItemWithTrigger` to ensure proper alignment.

<ApiProp name="alignItemWithTrigger" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Align the selected item with the trigger button position. Enables native-style
  scrolling with scroll arrows.

<ApiProp
  name="fadeEdges"
  fullType="boolean | 'top' | 'bottom' | 'left' | 'right' | 'x' | 'y' | FadeEdge[]"
  defaultValue="true"
>
  Controls the fade effect on scroll edges. See
  [ScrollArea](/docs/components/scroll-area#custom-props) for all options.

<ApiProp name="scrollbarGutter" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Reserves space for the scrollbar when content overflows, preventing layout
  shift.

<ApiProp name="persistScrollbar" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Always show the scrollbar instead of fading it in on hover or scroll.

<ApiProp name="hideScrollbar" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Hides the scrollbar while keeping scroll functionality.

<ApiProp name="nativeScroll" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Use native browser scrolling with styled scrollbars instead of Base UI's
  scroll virtualization. Enables CSS scroll-driven animations for fade edges.

<ApiProp name="sideOffset" fullType="number" defaultValue="6">
  Distance between the trigger and the popup. Base UI defaults to `0`.

<ApiProp name="level" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="3">
  Surface elevation level for the popup. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs. Uses `elevatedSurface` (rim on `::after`) so sticky group labels stay below the rim edge.

<ApiProp name="shadowLevel" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="3">
  Shadow weight. Controls drop-shadow intensity independently of substrate color.

A skeleton is a shimmering placeholder that holds an element's shape while its content loads. Use it for the initial load of cards, lists, tables, or text, in place of a spinner, to preview the layout that is about to appear.

## API Reference

### Props

#### Skeleton

Animated placeholder that displays a shimmer effect. Can be used standalone with explicit dimensions or as a wrapper around content.

<ApiProp name="visible" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="true">
  Controls skeleton visibility. When `false` and children are present, renders children directly without the skeleton wrapper.

<ApiProp name="animate" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="true">
  Enables the shimmer animation. When `false`, displays a static background.

<ApiProp name="inverted" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Inverts the shimmer highlight color. By default the sheen is light (white-tinted); when `true` it becomes dark (black-tinted). Use on surfaces where the default highlight is too bright.

<ApiProp name="multiline" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Renders the skeleton as an inline `<span>` so it can wrap across multiple lines of text. Uses `box-decoration-break: clone` so each line fragment carries the skeleton styling, and `color: transparent` so the underlying text reserves its natural dimensions while staying invisible.

<ApiProp name="children" fullType="ReactNode" simpleType="node">
  Content to wrap. When provided, children are rendered but hidden (`invisible`) while the skeleton overlay is visible. The skeleton inherits the children's dimensions.

---

# slider.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/slider.mdx

title: Slider
description: Interactive control for selecting a value or range from a continuous scale
type: primitive

import { Slider } from "@/registry/default/slider/slider";

The slider lets users pick a value, or a range, by dragging a thumb along a track. Use it for volume, brightness, price ranges, and other continuous settings where quick adjustment matters more than typing an exact number.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="slider" example="slider-basic" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="slider" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="slider" />

## Composition

```text
Slider
├── SliderLabel
└── SliderValue
```

`SliderLabel` and `SliderValue` are optional children that render **above** the track, so a header row (the label and value side by side) sits directly above the slider control:

```tsx
<Slider defaultValue={[50]}>
  <div className="flex items-center justify-between">
    <SliderLabel>Volume</SliderLabel>
    <SliderValue />
  </div>
</Slider>
```

For content *below* the track, render it as a sibling of `Slider` rather than a child (for example, a `<FieldDescription>` inside the enclosing `<Field>`).

## Examples

### Controlled

Use `value` and `onValueChange` to control the slider state.

<ComponentPreview component="slider" example="slider-controlled" />

### Range Slider

Pass an array value to render two thumbs and select a range.

<ComponentPreview component="slider" example="slider-range" />

### With Steps

Use `step` to snap to discrete values, and `showSteps` to mark them on the track.

<ComponentPreview component="slider" example="slider-with-steps" />

### With Value Display

Add `SliderValue` to show the current value beside the slider.

<ComponentPreview component="slider" example="slider-with-value" />

### Vertical Orientation

Set `orientation="vertical"` to lay the slider out vertically.

<ComponentPreview component="slider" example="slider-vertical" />

### Variants

Use `variant` to change the slider's visual style.

<ComponentPreview component="slider" example="slider-variant" />

| Variant       | Description                                          |
| ------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `default`     | A round thumb centered on the track.                |
| `contained`   | The thumb aligns to the track edges at min and max. |
| `squareThumb` | A square thumb in place of the round default.       |

### With Reference Scale

Render annotations like a reference scale as a sibling of `Slider`. Content outside the `Slider` root doesn't need slider context, so it skips the label/value composition rules; a `SliderLabel` child still keeps the visible label above the track.

<ComponentPreview component="slider" example="slider-with-scale" />

### Disabled State

Set `disabled` to prevent interaction.

<ComponentPreview component="slider" example="slider-disabled-state" />

### Form Integration

Slider works with two submission flows. With Base UI's `onFormSubmit`, values come from registered [Field](/docs/components/field)s, so wrap each slider in `<Field name="...">` (and compose with [Fieldset](/docs/components/fieldset) for multi-thumb groups so each thumb keeps its own `aria-label` under a shared legend). With a native `onSubmit`, Slider's hidden input makes `name` sufficient on its own. The example below shows both. See the [Forms guide](/docs/getting-started/forms) for more patterns.

<ComponentPreview component="slider" example="slider-field" />

## Accessibility

The slider is operable from the keyboard: focus a thumb, then use the arrow keys to adjust by `step`, `Home`/`End` to jump to the min and max, and `PageUp`/`PageDown` for larger increments.

Give the slider an accessible name when there is no visible `SliderLabel`. For a range slider, use `getAriaLabel` so each thumb gets its own label.

```tsx showLineNumbers
<Slider
  defaultValue={[20, 60]}
  getAriaLabel={(index) => (index === 0 ? "Minimum price" : "Maximum price")}
/>
```

## API Reference

### Slider

<ApiProp
  name="variant"
  fullType='"default" | "contained" | "squareThumb"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"default"'
>
  Visual style variant for the slider. Choose from default, contained (thumb
  aligned to edges), or squareThumb styles.

<ApiProp name="getAriaLabel" fullType="((index: number) => string) | null">
  A function that returns an accessible name for each thumb. Use for sliders without a visible label, or for range sliders where each thumb needs a distinct label.

<ApiProp name="showSteps" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Show step indicator dots along the slider track for discrete value
  visualization.

<ApiProp name="min" fullType="number" defaultValue="0">
  Minimum value of the slider range.

<ApiProp name="max" fullType="number" defaultValue="100">
  Maximum value of the slider range.

<ApiProp name="thumbAlignment" fullType='"center" | "edge"' simpleType="string">
  Alignment of the slider thumb. Automatically set to 'edge' when variant is
  'contained', otherwise defaults to 'center'.

### Additional Props

Slider inherits all props from [Base UI Slider](https://base-ui.com/react/components/slider#api-reference), including orientation, step, value, defaultValue, onChange, and accessibility props.

# switch.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/switch.mdx

title: Switch
description: Toggle control for binary on/off states with smooth animations
type: primitive

import { Switch } from "@/registry/default/switch/switch";

A switch toggles a single setting on or off and applies the change immediately. Use it for instant preferences like notifications or dark mode, not for choices a user submits later with a form (reach for [`Checkbox`](/docs/components/checkbox) there).

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="switch" example="switch-basic" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="switch" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="switch" />

## Examples

### Card

Wrap the switch in a `Label` to make a whole card row toggle the control.

<ComponentPreview component="switch" example="switch-card" />

### Pill Shape

Use `shape` to set the thumb's aspect ratio and travel distance.

<ComponentPreview component="switch" example="switch-pill" />

| Shape    | Description                                  |
| -------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `circle` | The default, a round thumb.                  |
| `pill`   | A wider, rectangular thumb.                  |

### Form Integration

Use [Field](/docs/components/field) for labeling and form participation. See the [Forms guide](/docs/getting-started/forms) for more patterns.

<ComponentPreview component="switch" example="switch-field" />

## API Reference

The Switch component is built on top of [Base UI's Switch](https://base-ui.com/react/components/switch). All Base UI props are supported. The documentation below only covers custom props specific to our implementation.

For the complete Base UI API, see the [Base UI Switch documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/switch).

### Props

#### Switch

Toggle control for binary on/off states. Wraps Base UI's `Switch.Root` and `Switch.Thumb`.

<ApiProp
  name="shape"
  fullType='"circle" | "pill"'
  simpleType="string"
  defaultValue='"circle"'
>
  Controls the aspect ratio and animation travel distance of the switch thumb. Use `"pill"` for a wider, more rectangular thumb.

Switch does not expose a `variant` prop like the other form fields. The unchecked track always uses `bg-input-elevated`, a translucent overlay that adapts to whatever substrate it sits on. This contrasts with both the thumb (white in light, page-dark in dark) AND the parent surface, so a single behavior works everywhere. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs.

# table.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/table.mdx

title: Table
description: Organized display of data in rows and columns with customizable styling
type: primitive

import { Table, TableBody, TableCaption, TableCell, TableFooter, TableHead, TableHeader, TableRow } from "@/registry/default/table/table";

A table presents rows and columns of structured data inside a scrollable, card-styled frame. Use it for records you compare across columns, like users, invoices, or transactions, where each row shares the same fields.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="table" example="table-basic" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="table" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="table" />

## Composition

```text
Table
├── TableCaption
├── TableHeader
│   └── TableRow
│       └── TableHead
├── TableBody
│   └── TableRow
│       └── TableCell
└── TableFooter
    └── TableRow
        └── TableCell
```

`Table` reads its variant props (`bordered`, `striped`, and the rest) and passes them to the cells via data attributes, so the styling flags live on the root.

## Examples

### With Footer

Use `TableFooter` to hold totals or summary rows below the body.

Set `bordered` on `Table` to draw borders on every cell for a grid look.

### Striped

Set `striped` on `Table` to alternate row backgrounds for easier scanning.

<ComponentPreview component="table" example="table-striped" />

### Row Selection

Set `selected` on a `TableRow` to highlight it as the active selection.

<ComponentPreview component="table" example="table-row-selection" />

## API Reference

### Props

#### Table

Root container that wraps the table and provides variant context to children via data attributes. Features a card-like appearance with a muted background border.

<ApiProp
  name="bordered"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Adds borders to all table cells for a grid appearance.

<ApiProp
  name="striped"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Adds alternating background colors to rows for better readability.

<ApiProp
  name="hoverable"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="true"
>
  Enables hover effect on rows.

<ApiProp
  name="rowDividers"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="true"
>
  Shows horizontal dividers between body rows.

<ApiProp
  name="fadeEdges"
  fullType="boolean | 'x' | 'y' | 'top' | 'bottom' | 'left' | 'right'"
  defaultValue="'bottom'"
>
  Adds gradient fade effect at scroll edges to indicate more content.

<ApiProp
  name="nativeScroll"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Uses native browser scrollbars instead of custom styled scrollbars.

<ApiProp
  name="hideScrollbar"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Hides the scrollbar while maintaining scroll functionality.

<ApiProp
  name="persistScrollbar"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Always shows the scrollbar instead of auto-hiding.

<ApiProp
  name="scrollbarGutter"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Reserves space for scrollbar to prevent layout shift.

<ApiProp name="level" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="3">
  Surface elevation level for the Table's outer frame. See the [Surfaces](/docs/getting-started/surfaces) docs. The outer is a `bg-muted` gray frame; body cells drop to `bg-surface-3 dark:bg-surface-1` to form the inner card.

<ApiProp name="shadowLevel" fullType="1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6 | 7 | 8" defaultValue="1">
  Shadow weight for the outer frame. Defaults to `1`, a flat outlined card (rim only, no drops), matching the rest of the flat-card family.

#### TableRow

Represents a row in the table. Supports polymorphic rendering via the `render` prop.

<ApiProp
  name="selected"
  fullType="boolean"
  defaultValue="false"
>
  Marks the row as selected with a highlighted background.

<ApiProp
  name="render"
  fullType="ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)"
>
  Polymorphic render prop to change the underlying element or customize rendering.

#### TableHeader, TableBody, TableFooter

Semantic table sections. All support polymorphic rendering via the `render` prop.

<ApiProp
  name="render"
  fullType="ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)"
>
  Polymorphic render prop to change the underlying element or customize rendering.

#### TableHead, TableCell

Table header and data cells. Inherit bordered variant from the parent Table. Both support polymorphic rendering via the `render` prop.

<ApiProp
  name="render"
  fullType="ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)"
>
  Polymorphic render prop to change the underlying element or customize rendering.

#### TableCaption

Table caption element. Supports polymorphic rendering via the `render` prop.

<ApiProp
  name="render"
  fullType="ReactElement | ((props, state) => ReactElement)"
>
  Polymorphic render prop to change the underlying element or customize rendering.

# tabs.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/tabs.mdx

title: Tabs
description: Organize content into multiple panels with tab navigation
type: primitive

import { Tabs, TabsContent, TabsList, TabsPanels, TabsTrigger } from "@/registry/default/tabs/tabs";

Tabs split related content into panels and show one at a time behind a row of triggers. Use them to organize a settings screen, a card's detail views, or any section where the panels are peers and only one is relevant at once.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="tabs" example="tabs-basic" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="tabs" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="tabs" />

## Composition

```text
Tabs
├── TabsList
│   └── TabsTrigger
└── TabsPanels
    └── TabsContent
```

Wrap all `TabsContent` panels in `TabsPanels` to get the shared grid layout and directional slide transitions. `TabsList` renders the active indicator internally.

## Examples

### Sizes

Use `size` on `TabsList` to switch between `small` and `medium`; the list and indicator corner radius scale with it.

<ComponentPreview component="tabs" example="tabs-sizes" />

| Size     | Description                            |
| -------- | -------------------------------------- |
| `small`  | Compact triggers with tighter padding. |
| `medium` | The default, roomier triggers.         |

### Controlled

Use `value` and `onValueChange` on `Tabs` to drive the active tab yourself.

<ComponentPreview component="tabs" example="tabs-controlled" />

### Underline Variant

Set `variant="underline"` on `TabsList` for an underline indicator instead of the capsule.

<ComponentPreview component="tabs" example="tabs-underline-variant" />

| Variant     | Description                                          |
| ----------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| `capsule`   | The default, a filled pill behind the active tab.   |
| `underline` | A bar under (or beside) the active tab.             |

### Vertical Layout

Set `orientation="vertical"` on `Tabs` to stack triggers down the side.

<ComponentPreview component="tabs" example="tabs-vertical" />

### Vertical Underline

Combine `orientation="vertical"` with `variant="underline"` for a side rail.

<ComponentPreview component="tabs" example="tabs-vertical-underline" />

### Vertical Underline with Sides

Use `side` on `TabsList` to place the underline on the `left` or `right` edge.

<ComponentPreview component="tabs" example="tabs-vertical-underline-with-sides" />

### Animated

`TabsPanels` slides and fades between panels in the direction of the move.

<ComponentPreview component="tabs" example="tabs-animated" />

## API Reference

The Tabs component is built on top of [Base UI's Tabs](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tabs). All Base UI props are supported. The documentation below only covers custom props and modified defaults specific to our implementation.

For the complete Base UI API, see the [Base UI Tabs documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/tabs).

### Props

#### TabsList

Container for tab triggers with visual styling. Wraps Base UI's `Tabs.List`.

<ApiProp
  name="variant"
  fullType="'capsule' | 'underline'"
  defaultValue="'capsule'"
>
  Visual style variant for the tabs list. Custom prop not available in Base UI.

<ApiProp
  name="size"
  fullType="'small' | 'medium'"
  defaultValue="'medium'"
>
  Size variant for the tabs. Custom prop not available in Base UI.

<ApiProp
  name="side"
  fullType="'left' | 'right'"
  defaultValue="'left'"
>
  Side positioning for vertical tab orientation. Custom prop not available in Base UI.

#### TabsPanels

Grid container for tab panels. Wrap all `TabsContent` items in `TabsPanels` to enable proper layout and smooth directional slide and fade transitions between panels.

#### TabsContent

Panel that displays content for the active tab. Wraps Base UI's `Tabs.Panel`.

# toast.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/toast.mdx

title: Toast
description: Brief notification message that appears temporarily
type: primitive

import { ToastProvider, AnchoredToastProvider, toast } from "@/registry/default/toast/toast";

A toast is a brief, self-dismissing message that confirms an action or reports a result without blocking the page. Call `toast()` from anywhere to show one. Use it for transient feedback like "Saved" or "Upload failed", not for content the user must act on (use [`Dialog`](/docs/components/dialog) or [`Alert Dialog`](/docs/components/alert-dialog) there).

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="toast" example="toast-basic" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="toast" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="toast" />

## Examples

### Types

Use `type` (or the `toast.success`, `toast.error`, and similar shorthands) to set the toast's color and icon.

<ComponentPreview component="toast" example="toast-types" />

| Type      | Description                                  |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `default` | A neutral toast with no status color.        |
| `success` | Confirms an action completed.                |
| `error`   | Reports a failure.                           |
| `warning` | Flags a risk or caution.                     |
| `info`    | Conveys neutral, non-status information.     |

### Anchored Toast

Use `toast.anchored()` to pin a toast to a specific element for contextual feedback like a "Copied" confirmation.

<ComponentPreview component="toast" example="toast-anchored" />

### With Action

Use the `action` option to add a button; clicking it dismisses the current toast and can trigger a follow-up.

<ComponentPreview component="toast" example="toast-action" />

### Deduplicated

Pass a fixed `id` to collapse repeats; a matching toast updates in place with a pulse instead of stacking a duplicate.

<ComponentPreview component="toast" example="toast-deduplicated" />

### Promise

Use `toast.promise()` to drive loading, success, and error states from a promise's resolution.

<ComponentPreview component="toast" example="toast-promise" />

### Varying Heights

Toasts measure their own height and adjust the stack when content sizes differ.

<ComponentPreview component="toast" example="toast-varying-heights" />

### Grouped Toasts

Use `toast.grouped()` to fold related toasts into one summary with an expandable card, for long-running work like deployments or uploads.

<ComponentPreview component="toast" example="toast-grouped" />

## Accessibility

### Announcement urgency

Use `priority` to control how a screen reader announces the toast. `"low"` (the default) announces politely without interrupting the user; reserve `"high"` for messages that must break through, such as a failed save.

```tsx showLineNumbers
toast.error({ title: "Couldn't save", priority: "high" });
```

## API Reference

The Toast component is built on top of [Base UI's Toast](https://base-ui.com/react/components/toast). All Base UI props are supported. The documentation below only covers custom props and modified defaults specific to our implementation.

For the complete Base UI API, see the [Base UI Toast documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/toast).

### Props

#### toast()

Programmatically displays toast notifications. Supports object-based and JSX-based call signatures.

```tsx
// Object-based (recommended)
toast({ title: "Success", description: "Your changes have been saved", type: "success" });

// JSX-based
toast(<div>Custom JSX content</div>, { type: "info" });
```

<ApiProp name="id" fullType="string">
  Fixed identifier for deduplication. If a toast with this ID already exists, it updates in place instead of creating a duplicate.

<ApiProp name="title" fullType="string">
  Displays the title text.

<ApiProp name="description" fullType="string">
  Displays the description text below the title.

<ApiProp name="type" fullType='"default" | "success" | "error" | "warning" | "info"' defaultValue='"default"'>
  Visual type of the toast. Alternatively, use `toast.success()`, `toast.error()`, etc. as shorthand.

<ApiProp name="duration" fullType="number">
  Duration in milliseconds before auto-dismissal. Uses provider's `timeout` if not specified.

<ApiProp name="priority" fullType='"low" | "high"' defaultValue='"low"'>
  Screen reader announcement urgency. `"low"` announces politely without interrupting, `"high"` announces urgently.

<ApiProp name="action" fullType="{ label: string; onClick: () => void }">
  Configures an action button with label and click handler.

<ApiProp name="data" fullType="TData">
  Attaches custom data to the toast for use in callbacks or custom rendering.

<ApiProp name="onClose" fullType="() => void">
  Fires when the toast closes.

<ApiProp name="onRemove" fullType="() => void">
  Fires when the toast is removed from the DOM.

<ApiProp name="showCloseButton" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="true">
  Whether to show the close button.

#### Helper Methods

Type-specific methods for common toast types and programmatic control.

```tsx
// Type variants
toast.success({ title: "Saved!" });
toast.error({ title: "Failed" });
toast.warning({ title: "Warning" });
toast.info({ title: "Info" });

// Async operations - toast.promise() handles loading/success/error automatically
toast.promise(saveData(), {
  loading: "Saving...",
  success: "Saved!",
  error: "Failed to save",
});

// With dynamic messages based on promise result
toast.promise(fetchData(), {
  loading: { title: "Loading...", description: "Fetching data" },
  success: (data) => ({ title: "Success!", description: `Loaded ${data.name}` }), // data = resolved value
  error: (err) => ({ title: "Error", description: err.message }), // err = Error object
});

// Manual control (for advanced use cases)
// All toast methods return an ID that can be used for updates or dismissal
const toastId = toast({ title: "Processing..." });
toast.update(toastId, { title: "Done!", type: "success" });
toast.dismiss(toastId);
```

#### toast.anchored()

Shows toasts anchored to a specific element, useful for contextual feedback like "Copied" confirmations. Inherits all base toast options except `type`.

```tsx
toast.anchored({
  description: "Copied!",
  anchor: buttonRef,
  side: "top",
  sideOffset: 8,
  arrow: true,
  duration: 2000,
});

// Dismiss an anchored toast
toast.dismissAnchored(toastId);
```

<ApiProp name="anchor" fullType="Element | RefObject<Element | null>">
  **Required.** Element or ref to anchor the toast to.

<ApiProp name="side" fullType='"top" | "bottom" | "left" | "right"' defaultValue='"top"'>
  Side of anchor to position toast.

<ApiProp name="sideOffset" fullType="number" defaultValue="8">
  Offset from anchor in pixels.

<ApiProp name="align" fullType='"start" | "center" | "end"'>
  Alignment along the anchor edge.

<ApiProp name="alignOffset" fullType="number">
  Offset for alignment in pixels.

<ApiProp name="arrow" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="false">
  Show arrow pointing to anchor.

#### toast.grouped()

Groups multiple related toasts into a single collapsible summary. When only one item exists, it renders as a normal toast. When multiple items share the same `groupId`, they collapse into a summary with a "Show" button that reveals an expandable card.

```tsx
toast.grouped({
  groupId: "deployments",
  title: "Deployment abc123 is building...",
  type: "loading",
  action: { label: "Cancel", onClick: () => cancelDeployment() },
  groupSummary: ({ loadingCount }) => `${loadingCount} deployments in progress`,
  groupAction: { label: "Show", expandedLabel: "Hide" },
});
```

<ApiProp name="groupId" fullType="string">
  **Required.** Identifier for the group. Items with the same `groupId` are grouped together.

<ApiProp name="title" fullType="string">
  Title of this item.

<ApiProp name="description" fullType="string">
  Description of this item.

<ApiProp name="type" fullType='"default" | "loading" | "success" | "error" | "warning" | "info"' defaultValue='"default"'>
  Visual type. Use `"loading"` for in-progress operations (shows spinner).

<ApiProp name="action" fullType="{ label: string; onClick: () => void }">
  Action button for this item.

<ApiProp name="groupSummary" fullType="string | ((counts: GroupSummaryCounts) => string)">
  **Required.** Summary text when multiple items exist. Can be a string or function receiving counts.

<ApiProp name="groupAction" fullType="{ label: string; expandedLabel?: string }" defaultValue='{ label: "Show", expandedLabel: "Hide" }'>
  Toggle button labels for expand/collapse.

<ApiProp name="duration" fullType="number">
  For non-loading items: group auto-dismiss duration (resets on new item, pauses on hover). For loading items: progress bar duration after transitioning to success/error.

<ApiProp name="showCloseButton" fullType="boolean" defaultValue="true">
  Whether to show the close button.

<ApiProp name="data" fullType="TData">
  Custom data attached to this item.

<ApiProp name="onClose" fullType="() => void">
  Callback when this item closes.

<ApiProp name="onRemove" fullType="() => void">
  Callback when this item is removed from DOM.

**GroupSummaryCounts**

The `groupSummary` function receives a `GroupSummaryCounts` object with these fields:

- `loadingCount` - Items currently in loading state (reflects visible items)
- `completedCount` - Total items that have completed (historical, persists after dismiss)
- `totalCount` - `loadingCount + completedCount`
- `successCount` - Items completed with type `"success"` (historical)
- `errorCount` - Items completed with type `"error"` (historical)
- `warningCount` - Items completed with type `"warning"` (historical)
- `infoCount` - Items completed with type `"info"` (historical)

**Helper methods:**

```tsx
// Dismiss a single item from a group
toast.dismissGroupItem(itemId);

// Dismiss an entire group
toast.dismissGroup(groupId);

// Update a specific item (e.g., loading -> success)
toast.updateGroupItem(itemId, { title: "Deployed!", type: "success" });

// Dismiss a completed item (removes from progress state)
toast.dismissCompletedItem(itemId);
```

**Behavior:**

- **Single item**: Renders as a normal toast with close button
- **Multiple items**: Collapses into summary with Show/Hide button
- **Loading items**: Groups persist until all loading items complete or are dismissed
- **Icon derivation**: Shows loading spinner while any item has `type: "loading"`, then success/warning/error based on results

#### toast.groupedPromise()

Shows a grouped toast that resolves with a promise, handling loading/success/error states automatically. Supports cancellation via `AbortSignal`.

```tsx
const controller = new AbortController();

await toast.groupedPromise(
  uploadFile(file),
  {
    loading: { title: "Uploading...", action: { label: "Cancel", onClick: () => controller.abort() } },
    success: (data) => ({ title: "Uploaded!", description: data.filename }),
    error: (err) => ({ title: "Failed", description: err.message }),
    aborted: { title: "Cancelled" }, // Optional
  },
  {
    groupId: "uploads",
    groupSummary: ({ loadingCount, completedCount }) =>
      loadingCount > 0 ? `${loadingCount} uploading...` : `${completedCount} uploaded`,
    signal: controller.signal,
  }
);
```

<ApiProp name="loading" fullType="{ title?: string; description?: string; action?: { label: string; onClick: () => void } }">
  **Required.** Message configuration for the loading state.

<ApiProp name="success" fullType="PromiseMessage | ((data: T) => { title?: string; description?: string; type?: ToastType })">
  **Required.** Message for success state. Can be a string, object, or function receiving the resolved data.

<ApiProp name="error" fullType="PromiseMessage | ((error: Error) => { title?: string; description?: string; type?: ToastType })">
  **Required.** Message for error state. Can be a string, object, or function receiving the error.

<ApiProp name="aborted" fullType="PromiseMessage | (() => { title?: string; description?: string; type?: ToastType })">
  Message when aborted via `AbortController`. Defaults to error message if not specified.

<ApiProp name="signal" fullType="AbortSignal">
  `AbortSignal` for cancellation support. When aborted, shows the `aborted` message.

All other `GroupedToastOptions` props (`groupId`, `groupSummary`, `groupAction`, etc.) are also supported.

#### ToastProvider

Wraps your app to enable stacked toast notifications. Composes Base UI's `Toast.Provider`, `Toast.Portal`, and `Toast.Viewport`.

<ApiProp name="position" fullType='"top-left" | "top-center" | "top-right" | "bottom-left" | "bottom-center" | "bottom-right"' defaultValue='"bottom-right"'>
  Position of the toast viewport.

<ApiProp name="limit" fullType="number" defaultValue="3">
  Maximum number of toasts visible at once.

<ApiProp name="timeout" fullType="number" defaultValue="5000">
  Default timeout for toasts in milliseconds.

<ApiProp name="container" fullType="HTMLElement | RefObject<HTMLElement | null>">
  Custom portal container element.

#### AnchoredToastProvider

Wraps your app to enable anchored toasts (positioned relative to elements). Composes Base UI's `Toast.Provider`, `Toast.Portal`, and `Toast.Viewport`.

<ApiProp name="limit" fullType="number" defaultValue="5">
  Maximum number of anchored toasts visible at once.

<ApiProp name="timeout" fullType="number" defaultValue="2000">
  Default timeout for anchored toasts in milliseconds.

<ApiProp name="container" fullType="HTMLElement | RefObject<HTMLElement | null>">
  Custom portal container element.

### Setup

Wrap your app with both providers to enable all toast functionality:

```tsx
// app/layout.tsx or similar
import { ToastProvider, AnchoredToastProvider } from "@/registry/default/toast/toast";

export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
  return (
    <html>
      <body>
        <ToastProvider position="bottom-right">
          <AnchoredToastProvider>
            {children}
          </AnchoredToastProvider>
        </ToastProvider>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

---

# toggle-group.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/toggle-group.mdx

title: Toggle Group
description: Group of toggle buttons for selecting one or multiple options
type: primitive

import { ToggleGroup } from "@/registry/default/toggle-group/toggle-group";

A toggle group joins a set of [`Toggle`](/docs/components/toggle) buttons into one segmented control with shared borders. Use it for related on/off choices that share a slot, like a text alignment or a view switcher, where one or several can be active at once.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="toggle-group" example="toggle-group-basic" />

<ComponentInstall component="toggle-group" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="toggle-group" />

## Composition

```text
ToggleGroup
└── Toggle
```

`ToggleGroup` wraps a row of [`Toggle`](/docs/components/toggle) buttons and merges their adjacent borders into one segmented control. Each `Toggle` carries its own `value`.

# toggle.mdx

title: Toggle
description: Two-state button for toggling between on and off

import { Toggle } from "@/registry/default/toggle/toggle";

A toggle is a two-state button that stays pressed when on. Use it for a single on/off control like bold, mute, or pin. For a set of mutually exclusive or multi-select toggles, use [`Toggle Group`](/docs/components/toggle-group); for a labeled settings switch, use [`Switch`](/docs/components/switch).

## Accessibility

```tsx showLineNumbers
<Toggle aria-label="Toggle bold">

```

## API Reference

# toolbar.mdx

Source: https://github.com/joncoronel/cubby-ui/blob/main/content/docs/components/(primitives)/toolbar.mdx

title: Toolbar
description: Container for grouping related actions and controls
type: primitive

import { Toolbar, ToolbarButton, ToolbarSeparator } from "@/registry/default/toolbar/toolbar";

A toolbar groups related buttons, links, and inputs into a single horizontal or vertical strip with arrow-key navigation between its controls. Use it for a formatting bar, a media player's transport controls, or any cluster of actions that act on the same context.

## Preview

<ComponentPreview component="toolbar" example="toolbar-basic" />

## Installation

<ComponentInstall component="toolbar" />

## Usage

<ComponentUsage component="toolbar" />

## Composition

```text
Toolbar
├── ToolbarGroup
│   └── ToolbarButton
├── ToolbarSeparator
├── ToolbarInput
└── ToolbarLink
```

Wrap related buttons in `ToolbarGroup` to keep them visually clustered, and use `ToolbarSeparator` to divide groups. `ToolbarButton` defaults to the `ghost` button variant.

## Examples

### With Input

Use `ToolbarInput` to place a text field inline with the toolbar's buttons.

<ComponentPreview component="toolbar" example="toolbar-with-input" />

## Accessibility

### Keyboard navigation

The toolbar manages a single tab stop with a roving tabindex: `Tab` moves focus into and out of the whole toolbar, and the arrow keys move between controls inside it. Match the arrow direction to the layout by setting `orientation` to `"horizontal"` or `"vertical"`.

### Label icon-only buttons

A `ToolbarButton` with only an icon has no text for a screen reader to announce. Give it an `aria-label` describing the action.

```tsx showLineNumbers
<ToolbarButton aria-label="Bold">
  <BoldIcon />
</ToolbarButton>
```

## API Reference

The Toolbar component is built on top of [Base UI's Toolbar](https://base-ui.com/react/components/toolbar). All Base UI props are supported. The documentation below only covers custom props and modified defaults specific to our implementation.

For the complete Base UI API, see the [Base UI Toolbar documentation](https://base-ui.com/react/components/toolbar).

### Modified Defaults

Our implementation changes the following Base UI prop defaults on ToolbarButton:

- **variant**: defaults to `"ghost"` (Base UI Button defaults to `"solid"`)
- **size**: defaults to `"default"` (standard Base UI default, but made explicit with buttonVariants)
